contents:
Comprehensive list of Free Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer (ACE) exam questions, grouped by official exam domain, curated for cracking the exam with confidence.
Disclaimer: Google Cloud is a protected Brand. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with Google. These are not the official Google Cloud exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from the official Google Cloud documentation and the publicly published Associate Cloud Engineer exam guide. These questions cover all the objectives of the ACE official exam, and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Note: The real ACE exam is 100% multiple choice and multiple select — there are no hands-on, performance-based tasks. The questions below are scenario-based practice questions, in the same format as our other certification posts, meant to solidify your understanding of every ACE exam domain before exam day.
Free Online Practice Exam Take all 50 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:-
Free Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer (ACE) Online Practice Exam
Overview This is an Associate level certification for cloud engineers who deploy applications, monitor operations, and manage Google Cloud solutions. No prerequisites, but Google recommends 6+ months of hands-on experience with Google Cloud. The exam costs 125 USD (plus tax where applicable). You need to answer 50 to 60 multiple choice and multiple select questions in 2 hours, delivered online-proctored (remote) or onsite at a Pearson VUE testing center. Google does not publish a specific passing score for this exam. The certification is valid for 3 years. Associate Cloud Engineer Exam Guide (PDF) and Official Exam Page for more details. 50 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 Setting up a cloud solution environment 20% 10 2 Planning and implementing a cloud solution 30% 15 3 Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution 30% 15 4 Configuring access and security 20% 10 Domain 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment (20%) A city government’s Google Cloud organization has three folders: “Production”, “Development”, and “Shared-Services”. The security team wants a constraint that disables external IP addresses on VM instances to apply automatically to every current and future project in the “Production” folder, without configuring it separately for each project. ⬜ Apply the organization policy constraint constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess directly to each project inside Production individually
⬜ Apply the constraint at the organization node and use IAM conditions to scope it to Production only
⬜ Apply the constraint on the “Production” folder so it is inherited by all projects and sub-folders beneath it
⬜ Create a custom IAM role that denies the compute.instances.setMetadata permission for Production projects
A data analytics team needs a small set of engineers to run BigQuery jobs and read datasets, but the built-in BigQuery Admin role grants far more permissions than required, including deleting datasets and managing IAM policies. What should the cloud administrator do to follow the principle of least privilege? ⬜ Grant the engineers the primitive Editor role, which includes BigQuery permissions along with broad project-wide access
⬜ Grant the predefined roles/bigquery.jobUser and roles/bigquery.dataViewer roles instead of BigQuery Admin
⬜ Grant BigQuery Admin but use IAM Conditions to restrict it to business hours only
⬜ Create a service account with BigQuery Admin and have engineers impersonate it for all queries
A company with 200 engineers onboards and offboards staff frequently and wants new hires on the “data-team” to automatically receive the same set of IAM roles on relevant projects as soon as they join, without an administrator manually granting roles to each new user account. ⬜ Create a Google Group in Cloud Identity, grant IAM roles to the group, and add or remove members as staffing changes
⬜ Grant IAM roles directly to each user’s individual Google Account and update policies whenever staffing changes
⬜ Create a new custom IAM role for every new engineer that copies permissions from an existing engineer
⬜ Use Workforce Identity Federation to map each new hire’s corporate directory attribute directly to a project-level primitive role
A developer just created a brand-new Google Cloud project and immediately tries to run gcloud compute instances create, but the command fails with an error indicating the Compute Engine API is not enabled for the project. What is the correct way to resolve this before creating the instance? ⬜ Request a quota increase for the Compute Engine API from Cloud Quotas
⬜ Grant the developer the Owner role at the organization level
⬜ Recreate the project inside a folder that already has Compute Engine enabled
⬜ Run gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com (or enable it under “APIs & Services” in the console) for the project
The operations team wants to be paged automatically via Slack whenever the average CPU utilization of a production Compute Engine instance group exceeds 90% for 5 minutes. Which Google Cloud Observability capability should they configure? ⬜ A Cloud Logging log-based metric with no alerting configured, reviewed manually each morning
⬜ A Cloud Monitoring alerting policy with a metric-threshold condition and a Slack notification channel
⬜ A budget alert on the billing account tied to compute spend
⬜ An organization policy constraint that blocks instances from exceeding 90% CPU
A team’s batch-processing job is being throttled because it needs to create 50 Compute Engine instances simultaneously in us-central1, but the project’s regional CPU quota only allows 24 vCPUs. What should they do to run the job without redesigning the architecture? ⬜ Move the workload to a different Google Cloud organization that has no quotas
⬜ Contact Google Cloud sales to purchase additional committed use discounts
⬜ Request a quota increase for the relevant CPU quota in that region from the Quotas page (IAM & Admin) or via the Cloud Quotas API
⬜ Delete the default VPC network to free up additional compute quota
A security team needs to answer “which Compute Engine firewall rules and IAM policies existed on this project 20 days ago” for an audit, without having manually taken snapshots at the time. Which Google Cloud service is designed for this? ⬜ Cloud Asset Inventory, which retains a history of resource metadata changes and lets you query state as of a past point in time
⬜ Recommender, which only provides forward-looking cost and security recommendations
⬜ VPC Flow Logs, which capture only network traffic metadata, not IAM policy changes
⬜ Security Command Center Standard tier, which does not retain historical resource metadata the way Cloud Asset Inventory does
An enterprise wants its employees to sign in to the Google Cloud console using their existing Okta credentials, without Google managing separate passwords for each employee and without syncing every employee into Cloud Identity as a Google-managed user. ⬜ Enable Workload Identity Federation and configure Okta as an attribute-based workload pool
⬜ Deploy Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) to continuously sync all Okta users into Cloud Identity
⬜ Create individual Cloud Identity accounts for each employee and enable 2-Step Verification
⬜ Configure Workforce Identity Federation with Okta as the external identity provider so employees federate in via SAML or OIDC without Google-managed accounts
A cloud administrator creates a new Google Cloud project for a proof-of-concept, but when trying to create a Cloud Storage bucket, the console shows “billing is not enabled for this project” and most APIs cannot be used. What must the administrator do first? ⬜ Set an IAM policy granting the Billing Account Administrator role to the project itself
⬜ Link the project to an active Cloud Billing account, either at project creation or afterward through the Billing page
⬜ Enable a budget on the project so charges can start being tracked
⬜ Request a quota increase for the project’s billing budget
A finance manager sets up a Cloud Billing budget of $5,000/month for a project with alert thresholds at 50%, 90%, and 100%, sent to their email. After the project’s spend reaches 100% of the budget in the middle of the month, what happens by default? ⬜ Google Cloud automatically disables billing for the project, stopping all resource usage
⬜ All running Compute Engine instances are automatically stopped to prevent further charges
⬜ The finance manager receives an email alert, but spending continues uninterrupted unless automated actions are separately configured to cap or stop usage
⬜ The project’s quota for every service is automatically reduced to zero
Domain 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution (30%) A team is building a stateless REST API that receives unpredictable, bursty traffic — sometimes zero requests for hours — and wants to avoid managing servers, clusters, or scaling configuration, while paying only for actual request-handling time. Which compute option best fits? ⬜ Cloud Run, which runs stateless containers on a fully managed serverless platform that scales automatically, including to zero
⬜ A GKE Standard cluster with a fixed 3-node pool, so the API always has capacity to absorb bursts
⬜ A single Compute Engine e2-standard-4 VM running the container with a static IP address
⬜ A zonal managed instance group with a fixed instance count of 5 machines
A platform team manages 300 Compute Engine VMs across many projects. Currently, whenever an engineer joins or leaves the team, someone must manually add or remove that engineer’s SSH public key in each VM’s instance metadata — an error-prone, hard-to-audit process. Which feature should they enable to centralize SSH access control through IAM instead? ⬜ VPC firewall rules that allow SSH only from the corporate office IP range
⬜ Shielded VM, to cryptographically verify each engineer’s identity before SSH
⬜ Adding the SSH keys to project-wide metadata instead of per-instance metadata
⬜ OS Login, which links each engineer’s Google identity to their Linux OS user account and grants or revokes SSH access via IAM roles
A team runs a stateful database on a single Compute Engine VM and wants the underlying disk to keep serving with no data loss if the entire zone the VM is running in becomes unavailable, without relying on database-level replication. Which storage option should they choose? ⬜ A zonal Persistent Disk with daily scheduled snapshots
⬜ A Regional Persistent Disk, which synchronously replicates data across two zones in the same region
⬜ Local SSD, which offers the highest IOPS but is physically attached to a single server
⬜ A Cloud Storage bucket configured with the Standard storage class, mounted as a filesystem
A web application’s traffic varies significantly between weekdays and weekends. The team wants Compute Engine to automatically add or remove VM instances based on average CPU utilization, using a consistent, versioned VM configuration for every instance it creates. What should they set up? ⬜ A single Compute Engine VM resized manually with gcloud compute instances set-machine-type during peak hours
⬜ Multiple independent VMs created from separate gcloud compute instances create commands with matching configurations
⬜ A managed instance group (MIG) built from an instance template, with autoscaling configured on a CPU-utilization target
⬜ An unmanaged instance group behind a load balancer, with an administrator manually adding VMs when Cloud Monitoring shows high CPU
A regulated fintech company is deploying a GKE cluster and requires that worker nodes must not be reachable from, or able to directly reach, the public internet, while still allowing engineers to manage the cluster from the corporate network. Which GKE configuration should they use? ⬜ A private cluster, where nodes are provisioned with only internal IP addresses, combined with authorized networks restricting control plane access
⬜ A zonal Standard cluster with default networking, where nodes receive ephemeral external IPs
⬜ A GKE Autopilot cluster with public endpoint access enabled for all IP ranges (0.0.0.0/0)
⬜ A cluster in the default VPC with a firewall rule allowing SSH from anywhere
A retailer wants to run ad-hoc SQL analytics over many years of point-of-sale transaction data, totaling tens of terabytes, with fast query response and no need to manage servers or clusters. Which Google Cloud data product is the best fit? ⬜ Cloud SQL for MySQL, scaled to the largest available machine type
⬜ Firestore, using collection group queries across all transaction documents
⬜ Memorystore for Redis, with transaction data cached in memory
⬜ BigQuery, a serverless, highly scalable enterprise data warehouse designed for fast SQL analytics over large datasets
A hospital must retain patient imaging records for regulatory compliance for at least 7 years and expects to access any given file less than once per year, but occasionally needs to retrieve a specific file immediately when requested by auditors. Which Cloud Storage class minimizes storage cost while meeting the retrieval need? ⬜ Standard storage class, since it has no minimum storage duration and the lowest per-request retrieval fees
⬜ Archive storage class, the lowest-cost class, intended for data accessed less than once a year while still retrievable within milliseconds
⬜ Nearline storage class, since its 30-day minimum storage duration matches monthly compliance reviews
⬜ A Persistent Disk snapshot stored in the same zone as the compute instance that originally wrote the data
A global fintech company needs a relational database for a payments ledger that must scale horizontally across regions to handle massive write throughput, while still guaranteeing strong consistency and ACID transactions across all replicas. Cloud SQL’s single-instance model can’t meet the scale requirement. Which product should they choose? ⬜ Bigtable, since it offers unlimited horizontal scale for structured payment records
⬜ Cloud SQL with read replicas in every region to distribute the write load
⬜ Cloud Spanner, a horizontally scalable, globally distributed relational database that provides strong consistency and ACID transactions
⬜ Firestore in Datastore mode, configured in a multi-region location for strong consistency
A media company currently stores 200 TB of video assets in an Amazon S3 bucket and wants to migrate them to Cloud Storage on a recurring schedule, with built-in retry, filtering, and validation, without writing custom migration scripts. Which Google Cloud tool should they use? ⬜ Storage Transfer Service, which supports scheduled, managed transfers from Amazon S3 and other sources directly into Cloud Storage
⬜ gsutil rsync run manually once per day from an administrator’s laptop
⬜ Cloud Data Fusion, a visual ETL tool intended for building custom data pipelines with transformation logic
⬜ BigQuery Data Transfer Service, since it can load any file type from S3 into a Cloud Storage bucket
An enterprise’s network security team wants sole control over creating subnets, routes, and firewall rules, while individual application teams — each working in their own project — should be able to deploy VMs and GKE clusters into those centrally managed networks without being able to modify network configuration themselves. Which Google Cloud networking approach fits this requirement? ⬜ VPC Network Peering between each application team’s own independent VPC and a central “hub” VPC
⬜ A separate VPC network duplicated in every application team’s project and kept in sync manually
⬜ Granting every application team’s project the Network Admin role on its own project’s default VPC
⬜ Shared VPC, where a host project holds the centrally managed VPC network and application teams’ service projects attach to it to deploy resources using its subnets
A team has web-tier and database-tier VMs in the same VPC network and wants a firewall rule that allows TCP:5432 only from the web-tier VMs to the database-tier VMs, regardless of which subnet or IP range the web-tier VMs happen to get, and without maintaining a manually updated list of IP addresses. What should they use to define the rule’s source and target? ⬜ Source and destination IP address ranges (CIDR blocks) covering the entire VPC’s primary subnet
⬜ Target tags (or service accounts) applied to the database-tier VMs, and a matching source tag (or service account) applied to the web-tier VMs
⬜ A single firewall rule with direction set to both INGRESS and EGRESS and no source or target specified
⬜ Cloud NAT configuration applied to the database-tier VMs to restrict inbound connections
A manufacturing company needs a private, high-bandwidth (10 Gbps), low-latency connection between its on-premises data center and its Google Cloud VPC that does not traverse the public internet, and it already has a presence in a colocation facility where Google has a point of presence. Which connectivity option best fits? ⬜ Cloud VPN using HA VPN, since it can deliver up to 10 Gbps over an IPsec tunnel across the public internet
⬜ VPC Network Peering directly between the on-premises router and the Google Cloud VPC
⬜ Dedicated Interconnect, which provides a direct physical, private connection between the on-premises network and Google’s network at a colocation facility
⬜ A Shared VPC host project configured to allow on-premises traffic through Google’s front-end load balancers
A company runs a web application with backends in multiple Google Cloud regions and wants a single anycast IP address that routes each user’s HTTPS request to the closest healthy regional backend, with support for URL-based routing to different backend services. Which load balancer type should they deploy? ⬜ The Global external Application Load Balancer, which uses a single global anycast IP and can route by URL path or host to backends across multiple regions
⬜ An internal passthrough Network Load Balancer, scoped to a single region’s internal IP range
⬜ A regional external Application Load Balancer deployed separately in each region, each with its own IP address
⬜ Cloud DNS geo-based routing alone, without any load balancer in front of the backends
A platform team wants to define their Google Cloud infrastructure — VPCs, GKE clusters, IAM bindings — as version-controlled configuration files so the same environment can be reproducibly created, reviewed via pull requests, and torn down in a predictable, repeatable way. Which tooling approach fits this requirement? ⬜ Manually clicking through the Google Cloud console and documenting each step in a wiki page for future reference
⬜ A shell script of sequential gcloud commands with no state tracking of what has already been created
⬜ Cloud Shell used interactively each time infrastructure needs to be recreated
⬜ Terraform, using the Google Cloud provider to declare desired infrastructure state in version-controlled configuration files applied through a plan/apply workflow
A cloud architect is designing a new multi-tier application architecture on Google Cloud and wants AI-assisted help generating an initial architecture diagram from a natural-language description, along with suggested Terraform code, directly within the Google Cloud console. Which Google Cloud capability should they use? ⬜ Cloud Asset Inventory, which generates architecture diagrams automatically from natural-language prompts
⬜ Gemini Cloud Assist, including its Application Design Center, which uses natural-language input to help design architectures and generate infrastructure-as-code such as Terraform
⬜ Security Command Center, which recommends architecture changes based only on active threat findings
⬜ Recommender, which only surfaces cost and performance recommendations for existing deployed resources
Domain 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution (30%) Your team runs a public marketing website served from a global external Application Load Balancer. You want to be notified by email and SMS within a few minutes whenever the website becomes unreachable from multiple locations around the world. What should you do? ⬜ Create a Cloud Function that pings the website every minute and sends an email if the request fails.
⬜ Create a Cloud Monitoring uptime check for the website, then create an alerting policy that triggers on the uptime check and attach email and SMS notification channels.
⬜ Enable Cloud Logging on the load balancer and create a log-based metric that counts 5xx responses, with no alerting policy attached.
⬜ Configure a Cloud Armor security policy to block traffic when the backend is unhealthy.
Your application writes structured log entries to Cloud Logging that include a severity=ERROR field. You want to automatically alert your on-call team if error log entries exceed 50 per minute for 5 consecutive minutes, without changing the application code. What should you do? ⬜ Manually search Cloud Logging every hour for error spikes.
⬜ Create a log-based metric that counts matching error log entries, then create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy that triggers when that metric exceeds the threshold over the specified duration.
⬜ Export logs to BigQuery and run a saved SQL query every night.
⬜ Set the log bucket’s retention period to 400 days so errors are never lost.
You manage a fleet of Compute Engine VMs behind an external Application Load Balancer, organized in a managed instance group (MIG). Traffic to the application varies significantly throughout the day. You want the number of VMs to automatically increase during peak hours and decrease during off-peak hours based on average CPU usage, without manual intervention. What should you configure? ⬜ A single Compute Engine VM with a larger machine type.
⬜ An autoscaling policy on the managed instance group based on average CPU utilization.
⬜ A Cloud Scheduler job that resizes the instance group at fixed times every day.
⬜ A health check that restarts VMs whenever CPU usage is high.
Your application runs as a Deployment on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard cluster. During a load test, pod CPU usage spikes and some pods stay in a Pending state because there is not enough allocatable capacity on any existing node. You want the cluster to automatically add pod replicas when CPU usage is high and automatically add nodes when there isn’t enough room to schedule pods. Which two GKE features should you enable? (Choose two.) ⬜ Node auto-repair
⬜ Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)
⬜ Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) in recommendation-only mode
⬜ Cluster autoscaler
You are rolling out a new version of an App Engine standard environment service and want to gradually shift a percentage of traffic to the new version while ensuring that any given end user’s browser session is consistently routed to the same version for the whole test, to avoid a confusing mixed experience. Which traffic-splitting method should you use? ⬜ IP address–based splitting
⬜ Cookie-based splitting
⬜ Deploying the new version with no traffic split, then switching 100% at once
⬜ Deleting the old version so only the new version can serve traffic
You deployed a new revision of a Cloud Run service. Before sending it all production traffic, you want to send only 10% of traffic to the new revision while the remaining 90% continues to go to the last known-good revision, so you can monitor error rates before a full rollout. What should you do? ⬜ Delete the old revision so only the new revision can receive traffic.
⬜ Use gcloud run services update-traffic (or the console Traffic tab) to split traffic between the new and previous revisions by percentage.
⬜ Create a second Cloud Run service and manually load-balance between them using DNS round robin.
⬜ Set the new revision’s minimum instance count to 10% of the old revision’s maximum instance count.
Your company stores application log files in a Cloud Storage bucket. Logs are frequently accessed for the first 30 days, occasionally accessed for the next 60 days, rarely needed after that, and must be deleted entirely once they are 365 days old for compliance reasons. You want this handled automatically with no application changes. What should you do? ⬜ Manually move objects between buckets using a cron job on a Compute Engine VM.
⬜ Configure an Object Lifecycle Management rule that transitions the storage class to Nearline after 30 days, to Coldline after 90 days, and deletes objects after 365 days.
⬜ Enable Object Versioning on the bucket.
⬜ Set the bucket’s default storage class to Archive so all new objects immediately use the cheapest tier.
Your production Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance must remain available with minimal downtime if the primary zone in a region experiences an outage, with failover to a standby happening automatically. What should you do? ⬜ Create a read replica in a different region and manually promote it if the primary fails.
⬜ Enable the high availability (HA) configuration for the instance, which provisions a standby instance in a different zone with synchronous replication and automatic failover.
⬜ Take manual on-demand backups every hour.
⬜ Increase the instance’s machine type to have more vCPUs.
Your read-heavy reporting application is putting sustained load on your Cloud SQL for MySQL primary instance, causing degraded write performance. You want to offload reporting queries without impacting the primary’s write throughput and without requiring automatic failover behavior. What should you do? ⬜ Enable the high availability configuration on the primary instance.
⬜ Create one or more read replicas and point the reporting application at the replica endpoint(s).
⬜ Increase the storage size of the primary instance.
⬜ Add more application server VMs behind a load balancer.
You need a recurring, fully managed way to back up all documents in your Firestore database to Cloud Storage every night without writing custom export code. What should you use? ⬜ Enable Cloud Storage Object Versioning on a bucket linked to Firestore.
⬜ Use Cloud Scheduler together with the managed export feature (gcloud firestore export) to export data to a Cloud Storage bucket on a schedule.
⬜ Manually download each document using the Firestore console every day.
⬜ Enable point-in-time recovery, which fully replaces the need for any export.
You are deploying a custom TCP application (not HTTP) on Compute Engine and need the backend VMs to see the original client’s source IP address directly, without relying on headers like X-Forwarded-For. Which type of Google Cloud load balancer should you use? ⬜ External Application Load Balancer (global HTTP(S))
⬜ External passthrough Network Load Balancer
⬜ Cloud CDN
⬜ Cloud Armor
Your organization runs internal services on VM instances inside a VPC network and wants those VMs to resolve internal hostnames like db.internal.example.com to private IP addresses, without exposing these DNS records to the public internet. What should you configure? ⬜ A Cloud DNS public zone for example.com.
⬜ A Cloud DNS private zone visible only within the specified VPC network(s).
⬜ A public A record pointing to the VM’s external IP address.
⬜ A Cloud NAT gateway.
You create a new custom-mode VPC network named prod-vpc and launch two Compute Engine VMs into it, each in a different subnet. When you try to ping one VM from the other using their internal IP addresses, the ping fails. What is the most likely cause? ⬜ Custom-mode VPC networks do not support internal VM-to-VM communication under any configuration.
⬜ A custom-mode VPC network does not automatically include a rule allowing internal traffic between subnets; you must create an explicit ingress firewall rule to allow it.
⬜ The VMs are using ephemeral external IP addresses, which blocks all internal traffic.
⬜ ICMP (ping) is permanently blocked on all Google Cloud networks by default and cannot be enabled.
An operations engineer wants to use Cloud Deployment Manager to define and deploy new Google Cloud infrastructure for a project starting today. As of 2026, what should you tell them? ⬜ Deployment Manager is the current recommended tool for all new infrastructure-as-code projects on Google Cloud.
⬜ Deployment Manager’s standard support has already ended (April 1, 2026), with a full shutdown planned for June 30, 2027; Google recommends migrating to Infrastructure Manager (which uses Terraform) or another IaC tool such as Terraform directly.
⬜ Deployment Manager was shut off completely and is no longer usable as of January 2026.
⬜ Deployment Manager only supports deploying Compute Engine resources, so it must be paired with gcloud for everything else.
Your team manages Google Cloud infrastructure using Terraform. Before applying any change to a shared production environment, you want to (1) see exactly what resources will be created, changed, or destroyed, and (2) ensure the change is reviewed by a teammate before it is applied. Which two practices should you follow? (Choose two.) ⬜ Run terraform plan and review its output (or a saved plan file) before applying, requiring that output to be reviewed/approved (e.g., in a pull request or CI pipeline) prior to terraform apply.
⬜ Skip terraform plan entirely and run terraform apply -auto-approve to save time.
⬜ Store Terraform state remotely (e.g., in a Cloud Storage backend with locking) so the team works from a single source of truth and avoids concurrent conflicting applies.
⬜ Manually edit resources in the Cloud Console after every terraform apply to fine-tune them.
Domain 4: Configuring access and security (20%) Your operations team needs the ability to start, stop, and reset Compute Engine VM instances as part of routine maintenance, but they should not be able to create new instances, delete instances, or modify firewall rules. Granting the Editor primitive role would give far more access than needed. What is the best approach? ⬜ Grant the Editor primitive role since it is the simplest option.
⬜ Grant the predefined roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 role, since it includes exactly start/stop/reset and nothing else.
⬜ Create a custom IAM role containing only the specific permissions needed (e.g., compute.instances.start, compute.instances.stop, compute.instances.reset, compute.instances.get, compute.instances.list) and grant that role to the team.
⬜ Grant the Viewer primitive role and ask the team to request temporary Owner access whenever maintenance is needed.
A contractor needs temporary access to view logs in a project, but only for the next 30 days, after which the access should automatically expire without anyone needing to remember to revoke it. What should you do? ⬜ Grant the roles/logging.viewer role and set a calendar reminder to manually remove it in 30 days.
⬜ Grant the roles/logging.viewer role with an IAM Condition that expires the binding on a specific date 30 days from now.
⬜ Create a new project just for the contractor and delete the entire project after 30 days.
⬜ Grant the Owner role and tell the contractor to self-revoke access after 30 days.
Your organization has the resource hierarchy Organization > Folder “Finance” > Project “billing-prod”. A user is granted the roles/viewer role at the Organization level. A project administrator on “billing-prod” wants to prevent that same user from viewing resources in just that one project, while still allowing them to view resources in every other project. Can this be done by editing only the IAM allow policy on the “billing-prod” project? ⬜ Yes, adding a “deny Viewer” binding on the project’s allow policy will override the inherited grant for that project only.
⬜ No; IAM allow policies are inherited down the resource hierarchy and are additive, so removing (or never adding) project-level access is not sufficient — the org-level grant still applies to that project.
⬜ Yes, because project-level policies always take precedence over organization-level policies.
⬜ No, because roles granted at the organization level can never be viewed or audited from the project level.
Your security team is reviewing how application code authenticates to Google Cloud APIs and wants to reduce the risk associated with long-lived service account JSON keys. Which two practices should you recommend? (Choose two.) ⬜ Download a new service account key and hardcode it directly into your application’s source code repository for convenience.
⬜ Where possible, avoid creating downloadable service account keys altogether, using service account impersonation (short-lived credentials) or attached service accounts (e.g., Workload Identity Federation for GKE, Compute Engine attached accounts) instead.
⬜ Never rotate service account keys once created, since rotation increases risk.
⬜ If a downloadable key is truly unavoidable, restrict its permissions to least privilege, store it securely (e.g., in Secret Manager), and rotate or delete it regularly.
Pods running in your GKE cluster need to call Google Cloud APIs (e.g., Cloud Storage, BigQuery) using the permissions of a Google service account. Your security policy prohibits exporting and storing service account key files anywhere in the cluster. What should you use? ⬜ Mount a downloaded service account JSON key as a Kubernetes Secret and reference it from each pod.
⬜ Enable Workload Identity Federation for GKE, which lets Kubernetes service accounts impersonate Google service accounts without needing an exported key.
⬜ Disable IAM entirely for the cluster’s project.
⬜ Grant the GKE nodes’ default service account the Owner role at the project level.
Your compliance team wants all access to a sensitive Cloud Storage bucket to be governed solely through IAM policies, with no possibility of a per-object ACL granting access that bypasses IAM review. What should you do? ⬜ Grant roles/storage.objectViewer at the project level and simply stop creating new ACLs going forward, leaving existing per-object ACLs untouched.
⬜ Enable uniform bucket-level access on the bucket, which disables ACLs and makes IAM the sole access control mechanism for that bucket and its objects.
⬜ Delete every object and re-upload it without specifying an ACL.
⬜ Set the bucket’s default object ACL to private for newly created objects only.
A compliance requirement mandates that your organization capture every read of objects in a specific set of sensitive Cloud Storage buckets, including reads by users with legitimate IAM permissions. You check Cloud Logging and find that object read events are not being recorded. What is the correct fix? ⬜ Grant the auditors the roles/owner role so they can see everything.
⬜ Enable Data Access audit logs (the DATA_READ log type) for the Cloud Storage service in the project’s or organization’s audit configuration.
⬜ Nothing can be done; Cloud Storage cannot log read access under any configuration.
⬜ Enable Admin Activity audit logs, since they also capture object reads.
Your security team wants to detect active threats such as malware, outbound DDoS activity, and cryptomining across your Google Cloud organization, in addition to basic misconfiguration findings. Which Security Command Center capability should they use? ⬜ Security Command Center Standard tier alone, which includes full threat detection at no additional cost.
⬜ Security Command Center Premium (or higher) tier, which adds capabilities such as Event Threat Detection and Container Threat Detection on top of the misconfiguration/vulnerability findings available in Standard.
⬜ Cloud Armor, since it fully replaces the need for Security Command Center.
⬜ VPC Flow Logs alone, since they automatically generate threat alerts without any additional service.
An administrator wants to create a custom IAM role that can be assigned across every project inside a specific folder, and tries to create the custom role directly at the folder level. What will happen? ⬜ The custom role is created successfully at the folder level and can immediately be used on any project inside that folder.
⬜ Custom roles cannot be defined at the folder level; the administrator must create the custom role at the organization level (so it can be granted across the folder’s projects) or individually at each project level.
⬜ The folder will automatically be converted into a project so the custom role can be created.
⬜ Custom roles can only be created scoped to an individual resource, such as a single Cloud Storage bucket.
You discover that a Cloud Storage bucket containing internal documents has allUsers granted the Storage Object Viewer role, making every object in the bucket publicly readable on the internet. You need to remove this public access immediately and prevent it from being re-added by mistake in the future. What should you do? ⬜ Remove the allUsers IAM binding from the bucket, and additionally enable the “Public access prevention” setting (or the equivalent organization policy) so public access cannot be re-granted.
⬜ Rename the bucket, since public access does not carry over to buckets with a different name.
⬜ Set the bucket’s storage class to Archive, which automatically blocks public reads.
⬜ Do nothing, since allUsers only grants access to authenticated Google accounts, not the general public.

contents:
Comprehensive list of AI-Empowered SAFe Advanced Scrum Master (SASM) Exam Questions curated for cracking the exam in first attempt.
Certification update (2026): Scaled Agile now offers this certification as the AI-Empowered SAFe Advanced Scrum Master, recommended for experienced Scrum Masters who already hold the SAFe Scrum Master (SSM) certification. The exam is 60 questions, multiple-choice single-select, 120 minutes, 82% passing score, web-based and closed book. A legacy, shorter “SASM” exam version (20 questions / 60 minutes / 80% passing, covering only 3 domains) also still appears in Scaled Agile’s catalog for candidates on the older learning path — check your Learning Plan to confirm which version you’ve been assigned before you start studying.
Disclaimer: Scaled Agile Inc is a protected Brand. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with Scaled Agile. These are not the SAFe official exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from the public web content of the Scaled Agile Framework, the official SASM exam study guide, and other publicly available Scaled Agile articles. These questions cover all the domains and topics of the official exam and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Full Exam Questions Get answers and explanations for all 97 questions from below link:-
Free AI-Empowered SAFe Advanced Scrum Master (SASM) Online Practice Exam
Overview Prepare well for the exam. Understand all SAFe Team and ART flow, coaching, and conflict-resolution concepts covered below. Requires 1 to 2 weeks of preparation if you already hold SSM and have hands-on Scrum Master experience. You need to solve 60 questions (multiple-choice, single-select) in 120 mins from your laptop without any supervision. It is an open-resource but closed-book, unproctored online exam — no outside assistance is allowed per the Candidate Agreement. Passing score is 82%, i.e. you need to get at least 50 out of 60 correct. Recommended prerequisite: SAFe Scrum Master (SSM) certification and real-world experience facilitating a Scrum team. Exam Domains The exam questions below are grouped and weighted to match the official exam blueprint:
# Domain Weight 1 Evolving the Advanced Scrum Master Role 11-13% 2 Improving Flow 22-24% 3 Building High-Performing Teams 26-28% 4 Addressing Conflict 18-20% 5 Improving ART Performance 17-19% Please leave your feedback in the comment section or contact us from main menu.
Wish you all the best for the AI-Empowered SAFe Advanced Scrum Master (SASM) Exam!
97 Practice Questions Domain 1: Evolving the Advanced Scrum Master Role What is the primary difference in scope between a SAFe Scrum Master (SSM) and an Advanced Scrum Master (SASM)? ⬜ The SASM writes code alongside the development team
⬜ The SASM extends servant leadership and coaching beyond a single team to the ART and cross-team level
⬜ The SASM replaces the Product Owner during PI Planning
⬜ The SASM only facilitates the Daily Stand-up
An Advanced Scrum Master notices a team consistently looks to them to make every decision. What leadership behavior should the SASM adopt to correct this? ⬜ Make the decisions faster so the team isn’t blocked
⬜ Shift from a directive style to coaching and asking powerful questions so the team builds its own decision-making capability
⬜ Escalate every team decision to the Release Train Engineer
⬜ Assign a technical lead to make decisions instead
Which best describes how an Advanced Scrum Master should use AI tools when coaching teams? ⬜ Let AI fully automate retrospectives and conflict resolution without team involvement
⬜ Use AI to augment tasks like summarizing flow data, surfacing patterns, or drafting retrospective prompts, while keeping human judgment and empathy central to coaching decisions
⬜ Avoid AI entirely, since SAFe coaching must remain fully manual
⬜ Use AI only to generate PI Planning slide decks
What is a key responsibility of an Advanced Scrum Master that goes beyond the SSM role? ⬜ Owning the Team Backlog
⬜ Coaching other Scrum Masters and helping coordinate Scrum of Scrums across the ART
⬜ Approving the Program Increment objectives on behalf of Business Owners
⬜ Writing the ART’s Vision document
Which statement best reflects the difference between “managing” and “leading” a team, as emphasized in the SASM role? ⬜ Leading focuses on inspiring shared purpose and growing capability, while managing focuses on directing tasks and controlling output
⬜ Leading and managing are identical in SAFe
⬜ Managing means only assigning story points
⬜ Leading applies only to Release Train Engineers, not Scrum Masters
A new Scrum Master on the ART frequently asks the SASM to resolve their team’s technical disagreements. What should the SASM do? ⬜ Resolve the disagreement directly since the SASM has more experience
⬜ Coach the new Scrum Master on facilitation and conflict-resolution techniques so they can handle it themselves
⬜ Ask the Release Train Engineer to step in
⬜ Ignore the request since it isn’t the SASM’s job
Why is continuously growing agile maturity across the organization considered part of the Advanced Scrum Master’s role? ⬜ It is not part of the SASM role; that belongs to the Lean-Agile Center of Excellence only
⬜ Because sustainable flow and high performance require the whole organization, not just one team, to keep improving its Lean-Agile practices
⬜ Because the SASM is evaluated only on the number of certifications their teammates hold
⬜ Because it replaces the need for retrospectives
What is the primary goal of decentralized decision-making in SAFe? ⬜ To minimize WIP
⬜ To reduce the delay caused by routing decisions through layers of management
⬜ To eliminate the need for Release Train Engineers
⬜ To shift all technical decisions to System Architects
What is one way a Scrum Master can lead the team’s efforts toward relentless improvement? ⬜ By scheduling additional team meetings
⬜ By helping the team become better problem solvers
⬜ By making every improvement decision for the team
⬜ By focusing only on technical discipline practices
A developer reports the same status at every Daily Stand-up — “Yesterday I worked on indexing. Today I will work on indexing. I have no impediments.” — without further detail. What coaching should the Scrum Master provide to improve the team’s visibility into this person’s work? ⬜ Ask the team to break the developer’s Stories into smaller tasks for clarity
⬜ Assign another team member to take over the work so the developer can start something new
⬜ Tell the developer to pair with another team member
⬜ Have the developer discuss their progress in the context of the Iteration Goals
When should centralized decision-making be used in SAFe, rather than decentralized decision-making? ⬜ When decisions involve significant economies of scale
⬜ When decisions need specific local context
⬜ When decisions must be made frequently
⬜ When decisions are short-term in duration
Which two Framework elements would a Scrum Master have the strongest connection and most frequent interaction with? (Choose two.) ⬜ Business Owners
⬜ Release Train Engineer
⬜ Systems Team
⬜ Product Owner
⬜ Epic Owner
What is one way a Scrum Master can gain the confidence of a stakeholder? ⬜ Establish a daily sync meeting with the stakeholder
⬜ Invite the stakeholder to the Iteration Retrospective
⬜ Make sure the results of the Retrospectives are made public
⬜ Make the process visible
Domain 2: Improving Flow Which flow metric answers the question “How fast is value being delivered?” ⬜ Flow Velocity
⬜ Flow Load
⬜ Flow Distribution
⬜ Flow Predictability
Which flow metric measures the elapsed time from when work enters the value stream until it is delivered to the customer? ⬜ Flow Efficiency
⬜ Flow Time
⬜ Flow Load
⬜ Flow Distribution
A team notices their Flow Efficiency is low even though team members appear busy. What does this most likely indicate? ⬜ The team has too few work items in progress
⬜ Work items spend a large proportion of time waiting (e.g., for reviews or approvals) rather than being actively worked on
⬜ The team’s Flow Velocity is too high
⬜ The Program Increment is too short
Which flow metric helps a team understand whether the amount of work-in-progress matches its capacity? ⬜ Flow Time
⬜ Flow Load
⬜ Flow Distribution
⬜ Flow Velocity
Which flow metric would a Product Owner use to check whether the team is investing appropriately in new features versus defects, technical debt, and risk reduction? ⬜ Flow Time
⬜ Flow Velocity
⬜ Flow Distribution
⬜ Flow Predictability
Which flow metric is most useful for assessing how reliably a Team, ART, or Solution Train delivers against its planned business value at PI boundaries? ⬜ Flow Load
⬜ Flow Efficiency
⬜ Flow Predictability
⬜ Flow Time
Which of the eight flow accelerators is being applied when a team puts an explicit limit on the number of stories that can be “In Progress” on its Kanban board? ⬜ Visualize and Limit WIP
⬜ Reduce Queue Length
⬜ Work in Smaller Batches
⬜ Address Bottlenecks
A team uses value stream mapping and a cumulative flow diagram to find where work is piling up in their process. Which flow accelerator does this represent? ⬜ Get Faster Feedback
⬜ Address Bottlenecks
⬜ Optimize Time in the Zone
⬜ Remediate Legacy Policies and Practices
Which flow accelerator specifically targets delays caused by passing work between different teams or specialized roles? ⬜ Work in Smaller Batches
⬜ Minimize Handoffs and Dependencies
⬜ Reduce Queue Length
⬜ Get Faster Feedback
A team implements continuous integration and automated testing so defects surface within minutes instead of weeks. Which flow accelerator is this an example of? ⬜ Visualize and Limit WIP
⬜ Work in Smaller Batches
⬜ Get Faster Feedback
⬜ Address Bottlenecks
Why does breaking work into smaller batches generally accelerate flow? ⬜ Smaller batches reduce variability and lead time, and let value be delivered and validated more frequently
⬜ Smaller batches always require more people
⬜ Smaller batches eliminate the need for a Definition of Done
⬜ Smaller batches remove the need for a Sprint/Iteration Review
An ART notices long queues of work waiting between the “Ready” and “In Progress” columns of its ART Kanban. Which flow accelerator most directly addresses this? ⬜ Get Faster Feedback
⬜ Optimize Time in the Zone
⬜ Reduce Queue Length
⬜ Minimize Handoffs and Dependencies
A developer is frequently interrupted by chat messages and unplanned meetings during focused coding work. Which flow accelerator addresses this problem? ⬜ Address Bottlenecks
⬜ Optimize Time in the Zone
⬜ Work in Smaller Batches
⬜ Remediate Legacy Policies and Practices
An organization requires a lengthy, multi-department change-approval process for even small production fixes, which slows every team on the ART. Which flow accelerator applies here? ⬜ Minimize Handoffs and Dependencies
⬜ Reduce Queue Length
⬜ Remediate Legacy Policies and Practices
⬜ Visualize and Limit WIP
How is average lead time typically measured using a cumulative flow diagram (CFD)? ⬜ By taking the average velocity over the last three Iterations
⬜ By measuring the vertical distance between the arrival and departure lines
⬜ By measuring the horizontal distance between the arrival and departure lines
⬜ By averaging the lead time of at least three items
On a team’s cumulative flow diagram, the distance between the arrival and departure curves is steadily growing wider. What does this most likely indicate? ⬜ Lead time is increasing
⬜ Unplanned work is being pushed into the backlog
⬜ WIP is decreasing
⬜ The backlog is being reprioritized
A team has fallen into a pattern of integrating and testing their Stories only on the last day of every Iteration. Why is this considered an anti-pattern? ⬜ Because the team is effectively “waterfalling” the Iteration
⬜ Because the team demonstrates the full Stories to the Product Owner during the Iteration Review
⬜ Because the team consistently meets its commitments and the Product Owner accepts the Stories
⬜ Because it becomes difficult to manage dependencies with other teams
Which statement is true about work in process (WIP) on a team’s Kanban board? ⬜ It should be managed strictly by looking at team capacity alone
⬜ Increasing WIP increases cross-training opportunities
⬜ Too much WIP leads to slower throughput
⬜ WIP limits reduce visibility into the team’s work
What are two timestamps required to measure lead time when using a Team Kanban board? (Choose two.) ⬜ When the Story is released to users and validated
⬜ When the Story is deployed
⬜ When the Agile Team pulls a Story onto the board
⬜ When the Story is accepted by the Product Owner
⬜ When the team completes validation of the Story
Which statement is true about batch size, lead time, and utilization? ⬜ Higher team member utilization leads to longer lead times
⬜ There is no direct relationship between lead time and utilization
⬜ As batch size increases, lead time decreases
⬜ There is no direct relationship between lead time and batch size
Domain 3: Building High-Performing Teams Which of the following best characterizes a high-performing Agile team? ⬜ A team that never has disagreements
⬜ A team with high trust, shared ownership, and a relentless focus on delivering value together
⬜ A team led entirely by a single technical expert
⬜ A team that strictly follows a fixed process without adapting it
What does it mean for a SAFe team to be “self-organizing”? ⬜ The team has no Scrum Master or Product Owner
⬜ The team decides how best to accomplish the work assigned to it
⬜ The team sets its own compensation
⬜ The team reports only to executive leadership
SAFe increasingly emphasizes teams being “self-managing” in addition to self-organizing. What does self-managing add? ⬜ The team no longer needs a Product Owner
⬜ The team also has authority over some aspects of what work to do and when, not just how, within given guardrails
⬜ The team sets Portfolio-level strategic themes
⬜ The team manages its own budget without any Lean Portfolio Management oversight
An Advanced Scrum Master observes a newly-formed team being polite but avoiding any disagreement in meetings. Using Tuckman’s model, which stage is this team most likely in? ⬜ Forming
⬜ Storming
⬜ Norming
⬜ Performing
A team starts openly disagreeing about ways of working and roles shortly after formation, with visible friction between members. Which Tuckman stage is this? ⬜ Forming
⬜ Storming
⬜ Norming
⬜ Performing
According to Lencioni’s Five Dysfunctions of a Team model, which dysfunction forms the foundation that all other dysfunctions build on? ⬜ Absence of Trust
⬜ Fear of Conflict
⬜ Lack of Commitment
⬜ Avoidance of Accountability
A team avoids any candid debate during planning because members are afraid of damaging relationships. Which of the Five Dysfunctions does this describe? ⬜ Absence of Trust
⬜ Fear of Conflict
⬜ Inattention to Results
⬜ Avoidance of Accountability
Team members verbally agree to a PI Objective in a meeting but show little follow-through afterward. Which dysfunction is most likely at play? ⬜ Fear of Conflict
⬜ Lack of Commitment
⬜ Absence of Trust
⬜ Inattention to Results
Team members consistently let a peer miss deadlines without saying anything, even though it affects the whole team’s delivery. Which dysfunction does this reflect? ⬜ Lack of Commitment
⬜ Avoidance of Accountability
⬜ Inattention to Results
⬜ Fear of Conflict
A team celebrates individual output even when the overall Program Increment objectives were missed. Which dysfunction is this an example of? ⬜ Avoidance of Accountability
⬜ Lack of Commitment
⬜ Inattention to Results
⬜ Absence of Trust
Why is psychological safety important to building a high-performing team? ⬜ It allows team members to take risks, admit mistakes, and raise concerns without fear of punishment or embarrassment
⬜ It guarantees the team will never miss a PI Objective
⬜ It removes the need for retrospectives
⬜ It means the SASM should never give critical feedback
What is a “powerful question” in the context of Advanced Scrum Master coaching? ⬜ A question with only one correct answer
⬜ An open-ended question that prompts the team to reflect and discover their own solution rather than being told the answer
⬜ A question the SASM asks only during hiring interviews
⬜ A closed yes/no question used to speed up meetings
Which behavior best demonstrates servant leadership by an Advanced Scrum Master? ⬜ Removing organizational impediments so the team can focus on delivering value
⬜ Assigning story points on behalf of the team
⬜ Deciding the Sprint/Iteration Backlog unilaterally
⬜ Approving all code before it merges
Two teams on the same ART regularly duplicate effort because they don’t know what the other is building. What is the best mechanism to improve this cross-team collaboration? ⬜ Assign both teams the same Product Owner
⬜ Regular cross-team syncs such as Scrum of Scrums and PO Sync
⬜ Merge the two teams’ backlogs into one without discussion
⬜ Escalate every overlap to the Business Owners
Why does SAFe encourage developing “T-shaped” skills within a team? ⬜ To ensure every member becomes a generalist with no deep expertise
⬜ To reduce single points of failure and bottlenecks by having members with deep expertise in one area and working knowledge across others
⬜ To reduce the number of roles needed on an ART
⬜ To replace the need for a Scrum Master
What is a practical way for an Advanced Scrum Master to assess a team’s health and performance over time? ⬜ Rely solely on velocity numbers
⬜ Use a combination of qualitative team self-assessments and quantitative flow/quality metrics
⬜ Ask the Release Train Engineer to rate the team
⬜ Compare the team’s story points directly against other teams
An Advanced Scrum Master wants to build trust with a skeptical stakeholder who was burned by missed commitments in the past. What is the most effective first step? ⬜ Deliver consistently on smaller, transparent commitments and communicate progress openly
⬜ Promise an ambitious delivery date to win the stakeholder over immediately
⬜ Avoid the stakeholder until the team’s metrics improve
⬜ Ask a more senior leader to reassure the stakeholder instead
The Agile Team includes the Scrum Master/Team Coach and the Developers, and which other key role? ⬜ Release Train Engineer
⬜ Product Owner
⬜ Project Manager
⬜ Product Manager
Which statement is true about refactoring code? ⬜ It is a prioritized backlog item used to build the Architecture Runway
⬜ It involves small changes that keep the code’s external behavior intact
⬜ It increases technical debt
⬜ It changes the system’s functionality
What are two purposes of the Scrum of Scrums meeting? (Choose two.) ⬜ Identify impediments
⬜ Facilitate cross-team collaboration
⬜ Review Solution Architecture
⬜ Collaborate on release details with the Systems Team
What are relationships within a highly collaborative team based on? ⬜ Trust
⬜ Communication
⬜ Collaboration
⬜ Alignment
A team insists that big Stories cannot be split into smaller ones. How should the Scrum Master coach them to do otherwise? ⬜ Emphasize the SAFe Principles to highlight the importance of flow
⬜ Suggest a story-splitting bootcamp during the next IP Iteration
⬜ Demonstrate story-splitting techniques using a specific example from the team’s own backlog
⬜ Invite a development manager to emphasize the importance of splitting Stories
What is one characteristic of an effective Agile Team? ⬜ It reliably delivers value by deploying working features
⬜ It relies on its manager to define work prioritization
⬜ Team members focus only on improving their own specialized skill sets
⬜ Team members always agree with each other’s ideas
Which statement is true about large Stories? ⬜ They require additional refinement sessions to fully understand the scope
⬜ They make it difficult to apply iterative development
⬜ They fit into one Iteration
⬜ They should be split into multiple tasks
An Agile Team decides they want to start using pair programming in future Iterations. Where should this decision typically be captured? ⬜ In the Inspect and Adapt meeting notes
⬜ In the team’s Iteration Retrospective notes
⬜ In the ART Backlog
⬜ Nowhere — it does not need to be documented
Which SAFe Core Value most directly enables trust across the Agile Release Train? ⬜ Transparency
⬜ Built-In Quality
⬜ Relentless Improvement
⬜ Alignment
Which two events provide opportunities for the team to collaborate? (Choose two.) ⬜ Iteration Planning
⬜ Portfolio Sync
⬜ Solution Demo
⬜ Pre-PI Planning
⬜ Backlog refinement
Domain 4: Addressing Conflict Which statement best reflects how SAFe views conflict within a team? ⬜ All conflict is destructive and should be eliminated
⬜ Task-focused conflict is natural and can be productive, while unmanaged relationship conflict is destructive
⬜ Conflict should always be escalated to the Release Train Engineer
⬜ Conflict only occurs when a team lacks a Scrum Master
A disagreement over which architectural approach to use is an example of what type of conflict? ⬜ Task or process conflict
⬜ Relationship conflict
⬜ Value conflict only
⬜ There is no such thing as task conflict in Agile teams
Using the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode framework, which style involves pursuing one’s own position at the expense of the other party, often used in a crisis needing quick, decisive action? ⬜ Competing
⬜ Collaborating
⬜ Accommodating
⬜ Avoiding
Which Thomas-Kilmann conflict style seeks a solution that fully satisfies the concerns of all parties involved, and is generally best suited to complex issues where the relationship matters? ⬜ Compromising
⬜ Collaborating
⬜ Accommodating
⬜ Avoiding
A Scrum Master and Product Owner each give up part of their preferred approach to quickly reach a workable middle-ground decision before a deadline. Which conflict style does this represent? ⬜ Competing
⬜ Collaborating
⬜ Compromising
⬜ Avoiding
A team member consistently withdraws from a disagreement and changes the subject rather than addressing it. Which Thomas-Kilmann style is this person exhibiting? ⬜ Accommodating
⬜ Avoiding
⬜ Compromising
⬜ Competing
A developer repeatedly gives in to a more vocal teammate’s preferences on design decisions to keep the peace, even when they disagree. Which Thomas-Kilmann style does this represent? ⬜ Accommodating
⬜ Competing
⬜ Collaborating
⬜ Avoiding
What does “interest-based” (as opposed to “positional”) conflict resolution focus on? ⬜ Determining who has the higher position in the org chart
⬜ Understanding the underlying needs and motivations behind each party’s stated position, to find a solution that addresses both
⬜ Always finding a 50/50 compromise regardless of underlying needs
⬜ Letting the most senior person decide
What is generally the most appropriate role for an Advanced Scrum Master when conflict arises between two team members? ⬜ Decide who is right and instruct the other to comply
⬜ Facilitate a constructive conversation so the team members work through the conflict themselves
⬜ Report the conflict to HR immediately in all cases
⬜ Ignore it since it will resolve itself
A disagreement between two teams on an ART about a shared dependency cannot be resolved despite repeated attempts at the team level. What should the Advanced Scrum Master do? ⬜ Let the disagreement continue since ASMs shouldn’t get involved in cross-team issues
⬜ Escalate and facilitate resolution at the ART level, involving the Release Train Engineer if needed
⬜ Instruct one team to unilaterally give in
⬜ Wait until the next Program Increment to address it
A team has the same disagreement resurface in every retrospective without real resolution. What technique should the Advanced Scrum Master introduce to address the recurring pattern? ⬜ Skip retrospectives until the conflict fades
⬜ Use root-cause analysis techniques, such as the 5 Whys, to identify and address the underlying cause rather than the symptoms
⬜ Rotate team members every Sprint to avoid the friction
⬜ Simply document the conflict without further action
Domain 5: Improving ART Performance What are the three main parts of the SAFe Inspect and Adapt (I&A) event? ⬜ PI System Demo, Quantitative and Qualitative Measurement, and the Problem-Solving Workshop
⬜ Sprint Planning, Daily Stand-up, and Sprint Review
⬜ PI Planning, Backlog Refinement, and Retrospective
⬜ Vision, Roadmap, and Backlog
What is the primary purpose of the PI System Demo within the Inspect and Adapt event? ⬜ To plan the next Program Increment’s objectives
⬜ To demonstrate the integrated, working system increment to stakeholders and gather their feedback
⬜ To calculate individual team member performance ratings
⬜ To resolve conflicts between teams
How is the ART Predictability Measure typically calculated? ⬜ By counting the number of stories completed regardless of value
⬜ By aggregating each team’s actual versus planned business value achieved for their PI Objectives
⬜ By averaging individual developer story points
⬜ By counting the number of retrospectives held
Besides the ART Predictability Measure, what other type of data is examined during the Quantitative and Qualitative Measurement part of I&A? ⬜ Only the ART’s total budget spent
⬜ Qualitative data such as customer satisfaction (e.g., NPS), defect/quality trends, and team/employee engagement feedback
⬜ Individual salary and compensation data
⬜ Only competitor product pricing
Which root-cause analysis technique, commonly used in the I&A Problem-Solving Workshop, involves repeatedly asking “why” to trace a problem back to its underlying cause? ⬜ Value stream mapping
⬜ The 5 Whys
⬜ Planning poker
⬜ A cumulative flow diagram
What visual technique is commonly used alongside the 5 Whys in the Problem-Solving Workshop to organize potential causes of a problem into categories? ⬜ A Kanban board
⬜ A fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram
⬜ A burn-down chart
⬜ A program board
After the Problem-Solving Workshop identifies root causes and improvement actions, where do those improvement items typically go? ⬜ They are discarded once the workshop ends
⬜ They become backlog items considered for the next Program Increment
⬜ They are only tracked informally by the Scrum Master
⬜ They must be implemented within the same day
What is the main purpose of the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration within a Program Increment? ⬜ To add an extra Iteration of committed feature work
⬜ To provide dedicated time for innovation, exploration, PI Planning preparation, and events like Inspect and Adapt, without the pressure of iteration velocity
⬜ To replace the need for a System Demo
⬜ To extend the deadline for unfinished committed stories
What does it mean for ART events to be “outcome-based” rather than purely ceremonial? ⬜ Events are run to produce meaningful decisions and improvements, not just to check a box that the ceremony happened
⬜ Events no longer need a fixed agenda
⬜ Events are optional for the Release Train Engineer
⬜ Events should be canceled if attendance is low
How can an Advanced Scrum Master best support the Release Train Engineer in improving ART performance? ⬜ By taking over the RTE’s responsibilities during I&A
⬜ By helping facilitate Scrum of Scrums, coaching individual Scrum Masters, and surfacing team-level flow data that feeds into ART-level decisions
⬜ By avoiding involvement in ART-level events entirely
⬜ By only focusing on their own team and ignoring ART-wide concerns
An ART’s flow metrics show consistently high Flow Load and low Flow Predictability across multiple teams. What should this signal to the Advanced Scrum Master and RTE? ⬜ Nothing; these metrics are unrelated to ART performance
⬜ A likely systemic capacity/demand imbalance across the ART that should be investigated and addressed, potentially in the Problem-Solving Workshop
⬜ That the ART should immediately add more Program Increments per year
⬜ That the next System Demo should be canceled
Three teams on an Agile Release Train are all working on the same Feature. Two stream-aligned teams commit, during PI Planning, to finish their part by the end of Iteration 5 and then integrate with the third (complicated-subsystem) team’s piece during the first week of the IP Iteration. Why is this an anti-pattern? ⬜ Because Product Management accepted each team’s plan at the end of PI Planning Day 2
⬜ Because each team needs to integrate with the complicated-subsystem team

Overview This is a Foundational level certification, ideal for business and technical roles who want to understand AI/ML and generative AI concepts on AWS, regardless of technical background. Requires 4 to 6 weeks of preparation depending upon your familiarity with AI/ML concepts. Exam code is AIF-C01 and costs 100 USD per attempt.
