Exam Guide for more details. 53 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 Fundamentals of AI and ML 20% 9 2 Fundamentals of Generative AI 24% 14 3 Applications of Foundation Models 28% 15 4 Guidelines for Responsible AI 14% 8 5 Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions 14% 7 Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML (20%) A retail company wants a system that can learn from historical sales data and improve its demand forecasts automatically over time, without being explicitly reprogrammed for every new pattern in the data.Which term BEST describes this capability? ⬜ Artificial intelligence (AI)
⬜ Machine learning (ML)
⬜ Business intelligence (BI)
⬜ Robotic process automation (RPA)
Which statement correctly describes the difference between supervised learning and unsupervised learning? ⬜ Supervised learning uses labeled data to learn a mapping from inputs to known outputs, while unsupervised learning finds patterns or structure in unlabeled data.
⬜ Supervised learning only works with image data, while unsupervised learning only works with text data.
⬜ Supervised learning requires no training data, while unsupervised learning requires large labeled datasets.
⬜ Supervised learning and unsupervised learning are two names for the same technique.
A company wants to process a large batch of scanned invoices overnight and does not need results immediately. Which type of inferencing is the MOST cost-effective fit for this use case? ⬜ Real-time inferencing
⬜ Asynchronous inferencing
⬜ Batch inferencing
⬜ Serverless inferencing with sub-second latency requirements
A data science team is building a model to predict which of three shipping carriers will deliver a package fastest, based on structured features like distance, weight, and historical delivery times. Which type of ML technique is this? ⬜ Regression
⬜ Classification
⬜ Clustering
⬜ Reinforcement learning
A company needs to add multi-language customer support to its application by translating incoming support tickets. Which AWS AI service is purpose-built for this use case with the LEAST implementation effort? ⬜ Amazon Comprehend
⬜ Amazon Translate
⬜ Amazon Transcribe
⬜ Amazon Polly
Which scenario is the LEAST appropriate use case for an AI/ML solution? ⬜ Forecasting next month’s product demand based on historical sales trends.
⬜ Detecting potentially fraudulent credit card transactions in near real time.
⬜ Calculating the exact income tax owed by a taxpayer under a fixed, published tax formula.
⬜ Recommending products to a customer based on browsing history.
A company is building a fraud-detection pipeline and wants to identify the AWS services and stages typically involved in an end-to-end AI/ML pipeline. Which sequence BEST reflects the stages of a typical ML pipeline? ⬜ Model deployment, then data collection, then model monitoring, then data labeling.
⬜ Data collection and preparation, model building and training, model evaluation, deployment, and ongoing monitoring/retraining.
⬜ Model training only, since AWS managed services eliminate the need for data preparation or monitoring.
⬜ Data labeling, followed immediately by production deployment, with no evaluation step.
A company has deployed a fraud-detection model and wants to track ongoing model quality metrics like accuracy and precision in production, in addition to business metrics like cost per transaction reviewed. Which concept does this practice belong to? ⬜ Model Context Protocol (MCP)
⬜ MLOps (ML Operations)
⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Prompt engineering
A team evaluating a binary fraud classifier wants a single metric that balances both precision (avoiding false fraud flags) and recall (catching actual fraud). Which metric should they use? ⬜ F1 score
⬜ Mean squared error (MSE)
⬜ R-squared
⬜ BLEU score
Domain 2: Fundamentals of Generative AI (24%) A company is deciding between building a custom ML model from scratch versus using a pre-trained foundation model (FM) for a new text-summarization feature. Which factor would MOST justify choosing a pre-trained FM over training a custom model from scratch? ⬜ The company has years of proprietary labeled data and unlimited budget for training infrastructure.
⬜ The company needs a general-purpose capability quickly, without the time and cost of collecting massive training datasets and training a model from zero.
⬜ The company requires a model trained exclusively on its own private data, with no exposure to any external data.
⬜ The company wants the lowest possible per-inference cost regardless of development timeline.
Which term refers to the smallest units of text (such as words or sub-word pieces) that a large language model (LLM) processes and generates? ⬜ Embeddings
⬜ Tokens
⬜ Vectors
⬜ Chunks
A company wants to build a semantic search feature that finds documents with similar meaning to a user’s query, even when they don’t share the same exact keywords. Which underlying GenAI concept makes this possible? ⬜ Prompt templates
⬜ Embeddings
⬜ Diffusion models
⬜ Token-based pricing
Which AWS service allows a company to access a variety of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers through a single, unified API to build generative AI applications? ⬜ Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
⬜ Amazon Bedrock
⬜ AWS Glue
⬜ Amazon Kinesis
A generative AI application’s monthly cost varies significantly depending on the number of input and output tokens processed by the foundation model. Which pricing model does this describe? ⬜ Flat monthly subscription
⬜ Token-based pricing
⬜ Per-user licensing
⬜ Free tier only, with no usage-based charges
Which of the following is a well-known DISADVANTAGE of generative AI solutions that a company should account for before deploying a customer-facing chatbot? ⬜ Generative AI models are always fully deterministic and produce identical output every time for the same input.
⬜ Generative AI models can hallucinate, producing plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or fabricated responses.
⬜ Generative AI models cannot generate any conversational responses.
⬜ Generative AI models require no evaluation before production deployment.
A company is comparing several foundation models for a customer-service application and wants to evaluate cross-model performance, return on investment (ROI), and customer satisfaction. Which category of consideration BEST describes this evaluation? ⬜ Determining the business value and metrics of a GenAI application
⬜ Choosing an inference parameter such as temperature
⬜ Selecting a vector database for embeddings
⬜ Defining a prompt template
A company building an autonomous AI agent needs its agent to call external tools, maintain memory across steps, and communicate with other agents in a standardized way. Which foundational agentic AI concept addresses standardizing how an agent connects to external tools and data sources? ⬜ Model Context Protocol (MCP)
⬜ Token-based pricing
⬜ Diffusion models
⬜ BLEU score
Which AWS capability provides curated, pre-built foundation models and solution templates that developers can quickly deploy within Amazon SageMaker AI to accelerate GenAI application development? ⬜ SageMaker JumpStart
⬜ AWS CloudTrail
⬜ Amazon Macie
⬜ AWS Config
A startup wants to launch a generative AI proof-of-concept quickly, with a low upfront cost and without managing GPU infrastructure. Which is an advantage of using AWS managed GenAI services like Amazon Bedrock for this use case? ⬜ It requires the company to build and train a foundation model from scratch.
⬜ It lowers the barrier to entry by providing managed access to foundation models with pay-as-you-go pricing, without needing to manage the underlying infrastructure.
⬜ It eliminates the need for any prompt engineering or evaluation of model output.
⬜ It requires committing to a single foundation model provider with no flexibility to switch models.
A company generating GenAI-produced marketing images at high volume wants to understand the cost tradeoffs of committing to provisioned throughput versus on-demand token-based pricing on Amazon Bedrock. Which factor is the PRIMARY consideration for choosing provisioned throughput? ⬜ Provisioned throughput is always cheaper than on-demand pricing regardless of usage volume.
⬜ Provisioned throughput reserves dedicated model capacity for predictable, high-volume workloads, typically at a different cost structure than on-demand token pricing.
⬜ Provisioned throughput is required before any model can be invoked on Amazon Bedrock.
⬜ Provisioned throughput only applies to model fine-tuning jobs, not inference.
Which statement BEST describes a foundation model (FM)? ⬜ A small, task-specific model trained only on one company’s internal dataset for a single narrow use case.
⬜ A large model pre-trained on a broad range of data that can be adapted to many different downstream tasks through prompting or fine-tuning.
⬜ A rule-based expert system with no learned parameters.
⬜ A model that can only process image data, never text.
A company is evaluating whether generative AI is the right approach for a use case where they need a highly precise, exact numeric output every time (such as a legal filing deadline calculation), rather than a fluent but potentially varying response. Which GenAI limitation is MOST relevant here? ⬜ Adaptability
⬜ Nondeterminism
⬜ Conversational capability
⬜ Content generation ability
A company wants to increase the consistency and quality of large language model (LLM) responses by providing the model with access to external sources of knowledge. Which technique will meet the requirement with the least development effort? ⬜ Pre-train a new foundation model from scratch on the company’s proprietary data.
⬜ Use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve relevant external data at query time and include it in the model’s prompt.
⬜ Fine-tune the foundation model on the company’s proprietary data.
⬜ Increase the model’s temperature parameter to make responses more consistent.
Domain 3: Applications of Foundation Models (28%) A company wants its customer-support chatbot to answer questions using the most current internal knowledge-base articles, without retraining or fine-tuning the underlying foundation model every time an article changes. Which technique BEST meets this requirement? ⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Full model pre-training from scratch
⬜ Increasing the temperature parameter
⬜ Reducing the maximum output token length
Which AWS service allows a company to connect Amazon Bedrock foundation models to external data sources such as Amazon S3 for a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, including automatically converting documents into embeddings? ⬜ Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon CloudFront
⬜ AWS Snowball
A company implementing a RAG solution on AWS needs to store vector embeddings so they can be efficiently searched for semantic similarity. Which of the following is a valid AWS option for storing and querying vector embeddings? ⬜ Amazon OpenSearch Service
⬜ Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS)
⬜ AWS Step Functions
⬜ Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS)
A developer wants a foundation model’s responses to be MORE deterministic and focused, consistently choosing the most likely next token rather than exploring less probable alternatives. Which inference parameter adjustment achieves this? ⬜ Increase the temperature value.
⬜ Decrease the temperature value.
⬜ Increase the maximum output token length.
⬜ Enable a higher top-p value only.
A prompt engineer provides a large language model with several example input-output pairs directly within the prompt before asking it to complete a new, similar task. Which prompt engineering technique is being used? ⬜ Zero-shot prompting
⬜ Few-shot prompting
⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Fine-tuning
Which of the following is a well-documented RISK of prompt engineering that a company should guard against when exposing a chatbot to public users? ⬜ Prompt hijacking, where a malicious user manipulates the model into ignoring its original instructions.
⬜ Improved response quality from well-structured prompts.
⬜ Faster experimentation and iteration on prompt design.
⬜ Clearer, more specific outputs due to well-crafted instructions.
A company wants to save, version, and reuse a library of tested prompts across multiple generative AI applications and team members on Amazon Bedrock. Which capability should they use? ⬜ Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management
⬜ Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
⬜ AWS Config
⬜ Amazon Inspector
A company wants to adapt a general-purpose foundation model to understand company-specific terminology and respond in a particular tone, by further training the model on a smaller, labeled, domain-specific dataset. Which FM customization approach is this? ⬜ Fine-tuning
⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Prompt engineering with zero-shot prompts
⬜ Increasing the temperature parameter only
Which customization approach generally has the LOWEST upfront cost and fastest time-to-value, since it requires no additional model training? ⬜ Pre-training a foundation model from scratch
⬜ Fine-tuning with a large labeled dataset
⬜ In-context learning through prompt engineering (zero-shot/few-shot)
⬜ Continuous pre-training on a domain corpus
A company wants to improve a foundation model’s responses using human feedback about which of several generated responses is preferred, and use that feedback signal to further align the model’s behavior. Which technique does this describe? ⬜ Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
⬜ Zero-shot prompting
⬜ Vector embedding generation
⬜ Model distillation
A company wants a smaller, faster, and cheaper model that mimics the behavior of a larger, more capable foundation model for a narrower production use case. Which technique BEST achieves this? ⬜ Model distillation
⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Prompt hijacking
⬜ Increasing the context window size
A team wants to evaluate the quality of a foundation model’s generated text summaries against human-written reference summaries using an automated, well-established metric. Which metric is commonly used for this purpose? ⬜ ROUGE
⬜ F1 score
⬜ Precision and recall only
⬜ Mean squared error (MSE)
A company wants to run a structured evaluation job on Amazon Bedrock that compares multiple foundation models against built-in metrics and, optionally, human review. Which Amazon Bedrock capability supports this? ⬜ Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
⬜ Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
⬜ AWS Trusted Advisor
⬜ Amazon Macie
A company deployed a RAG-based question-answering agent and wants to measure whether end users actually complete their intended task and are satisfied with the answers, beyond just automated text-quality metrics. Which type of metric BEST addresses this? ⬜ Business objective alignment metrics, such as task completion rate and user satisfaction.
⬜ BLEU score only
⬜ ROUGE score only
⬜ Token count per request
A software development company is working on a new product with a very tight deadline. The company needs a way to develop code faster without sacrificing reliability or security. Which service could best help this company meet its deadline? ⬜ Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
⬜ Amazon Bedrock
⬜ Amazon Q Business
⬜ Amazon Q Developer
Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI (14%) A company wants to detect and filter harmful, biased, or off-topic content generated by its foundation model before it reaches end users. Which Amazon Bedrock capability is purpose-built for this? ⬜ Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
⬜ Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management
⬜ Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
⬜ AWS Config
A company training a hiring-recommendation model discovers that its training dataset contains far more examples from one demographic group than others. What is the PRIMARY risk this creates? ⬜ The model will train faster because the dataset is smaller.

⬜ The model will be immune to overfitting.
Which AWS capability helps document a machine learning model’s intended use, training details, risk ratings, and evaluation results in a single, structured, shareable record to support transparency and governance? ⬜ Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
⬜ AWS Snowmobile
A company is evaluating the legal risks of deploying a generative AI application that produces marketing copy and images. Which of the following is a recognized legal risk category associated with generative AI? ⬜ Guaranteed accuracy of all generated content

⬜ Elimination of all end-user risk
⬜ Complete removal of the need for human review
Which AWS capability can help a data science team analyze training data and model predictions for potential bias across different demographic groups, both before and after training? ⬜ Amazon SageMaker Clarify
⬜ AWS Snowball Edge
⬜ Amazon CloudFront
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
A company wants end users to understand, in general terms, why an AI system produced a particular recommendation, and wants to incorporate a feedback mechanism so users can flag incorrect or concerning outputs. Which responsible-AI principle does this BEST reflect? ⬜ Human-centered design for explainable AI
⬜ Maximizing model throughput
⬜ Minimizing infrastructure cost
⬜ Reducing the number of foundation model parameters
A company must choose between a highly transparent, simpler model and a more complex, higher-performing model that is harder to interpret. Which concept describes this decision? ⬜ The tradeoff between model interpretability and performance.

A deep learning system developer doesn’t document the origin of the training data or whether it has been manipulated. Reviewers raise concerns about fairness and bias in the system’s results. Which step of promoting AI training transparency does this scenario represent? ⬜ Model evaluation
⬜ Human-in-the-loop review
⬜ Data lineage and provenance documentation
⬜ Model monitoring
Domain 5: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions (14%) Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for securing an AI/ML workload’s data and configuring appropriate access controls (such as IAM policies) for resources like Amazon Bedrock or Amazon SageMaker AI? ⬜ AWS is solely responsible for all security, with no customer responsibility.

A company wants to grant fine-grained permissions so that only specific users can invoke certain Amazon Bedrock foundation models, while denying access to others. Which AWS service should be used to define and enforce these permissions? ⬜ AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)

A company storing training data in Amazon S3 wants to automatically discover and alert on personally identifiable information (PII) present in its data before it is used to train or fine-tune a model. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this? ⬜ Amazon Macie

⬜ Managing IAM users and permissions.
For a managed database service like Amazon RDS, which of the following is the CUSTOMER’s responsibility under the Shared Responsibility Model? ⬜ Patching the underlying database engine software.
⬜ Maintaining the physical data center facilities.
⬜ Managing database access permissions, data content, and network configuration (such as security groups) for their database instance.
⬜ Replacing failed physical hard drives in the data center.
A company needs to download AWS’s compliance reports, such as SOC reports and ISO certifications, to satisfy an internal audit requirement. Which AWS service provides on-demand access to this compliance documentation? ⬜ AWS Artifact
⬜ AWS Trusted Advisor
⬜ AWS Config
⬜ AWS Shield
Which AWS service continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior, such as unusual API calls or potentially compromised EC2 instances, using machine learning and threat intelligence? ⬜ Amazon GuardDuty
⬜ AWS Config
⬜ AWS Artifact
⬜ AWS Budgets
A company’s public-facing web application needs protection against common web exploits, such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS), at the application layer. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this? ⬜ AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall)
⬜ AWS Shield only
⬜ Amazon Route 53
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
Which AWS service is specifically designed to provide protection against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks? ⬜ AWS Shield
⬜ AWS Config
⬜ Amazon Inspector
⬜ AWS Trusted Advisor
A company wants to continuously track configuration changes to its AWS resources and evaluate whether those configurations comply with internal policies over time. Which AWS service should they use? ⬜ AWS Config
⬜ AWS Budgets
⬜ Amazon SNS
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
Which AWS service records a detailed history of API calls made within an AWS account, including who made the call and when, supporting security analysis and auditing? ⬜ AWS CloudTrail
⬜ Amazon CloudWatch only
⬜ AWS Organizations
⬜ Amazon QuickSight
Which of these is considered a best practice for protecting the AWS account root user? ⬜ Use the root user account for all daily administrative tasks.
⬜ Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user and avoid using it for everyday tasks, creating IAM users/roles instead.
⬜ Share the root user credentials with the entire engineering team for convenience.
⬜ Disable password requirements on the root user account.
A company wants to require users to provide a second form of verification, such as a code from an authenticator app, in addition to their password when signing in to AWS. Which security feature should they enable? ⬜ Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
⬜ AWS Organizations
⬜ AWS Config rules
⬜ Amazon Route 53 failover routing
A company wants its employees to sign in once through a centralized portal and then access multiple AWS accounts and business applications without separate credentials for each. Which AWS service is designed for this kind of centralized workforce identity and single sign-on? ⬜ AWS IAM Identity Center
⬜ Amazon GuardDuty
⬜ AWS Shield
⬜ AWS Artifact
A development team needs to securely store and automatically rotate a database credential used by an application, rather than hardcoding it. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this? ⬜ AWS Secrets Manager
⬜ Amazon S3 Standard storage class
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
Which principle states that users and systems should be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform their required tasks, and no more? ⬜ Principle of least privilege
⬜ Principle of shared responsibility
⬜ Principle of economies of scale
⬜ Principle of elasticity
A company wants to identify security misconfigurations, get consolidated security findings, and check compliance status across multiple AWS security services in one centralized dashboard. Which AWS service aggregates this? ⬜ AWS Security Hub
⬜ Amazon Route 53
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon QuickSight
Which AWS service encrypts data and manages the cryptographic keys used to protect that data across many AWS services, such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS? ⬜ AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
⬜ Amazon CloudWatch
⬜ AWS Trusted Advisor
⬜ Amazon SNS
Domain 3: Cloud Technology and Services (34%) A company wants to define and provision its AWS infrastructure using version-controlled, repeatable configuration files rather than manually clicking through the AWS Management Console each time. Which approach does this describe? ⬜ Infrastructure as Code (IaC), such as using AWS CloudFormation.
⬜ Manual console-only provisioning.
⬜ Only using the AWS Command Line Interface interactively, one command at a time, with no saved files.
⬜ Physically racking new on-premises servers.
Which statement correctly describes the relationship between AWS Regions and Availability Zones? ⬜ A Region contains exactly one Availability Zone.
⬜ A Region is a physical geographic location that contains multiple, isolated Availability Zones, each consisting of one or more discrete data centers.
⬜ Availability Zones span multiple Regions.
⬜ Regions and Availability Zones are the same thing, just different names.
A company wants to serve cached content to end users with the lowest possible latency by placing content physically closer to users around the world. Which AWS global infrastructure component is designed for this? ⬜ Availability Zones
⬜ Edge locations (used by services like Amazon CloudFront)
⬜ AWS Direct Connect locations only
⬜ AWS Local Zones exclusively
A company running a business-critical application wants to ensure the application remains available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which strategy addresses this? ⬜ Deploy the application in a single Availability Zone only.
⬜ Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones within a single Region only.
⬜ Deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions, so it can fail over if one Region becomes unavailable.
⬜ Rely solely on a single on-premises data center as a backup.
A company has a short-lived, fault-tolerant batch processing workload that can be interrupted, and wants to minimize compute costs. Which EC2 purchasing/compute option is typically the most cost-effective fit? ⬜ On-Demand Instances
⬜ Spot Instances
⬜ Dedicated Hosts
⬜ Savings Plans requiring a 3-year commitment
A company wants to run containerized applications without having to manage the underlying EC2 servers or clusters themselves. Which combination of AWS services fits this serverless container requirement? ⬜ Amazon EC2 with manually managed instances
⬜ Amazon ECS or Amazon EKS running on AWS Fargate
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
A company wants to run short-lived, event-driven code (such as processing an uploaded file) without provisioning or managing any servers at all, paying only for the compute time consumed. Which AWS service fits this best? ⬜ AWS Lambda
⬜ Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon WorkSpaces
A company’s web application experiences unpredictable spikes in traffic. Which AWS capability automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances up or down based on demand? ⬜ Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
⬜ Amazon Route 53 only
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ AWS Artifact
A company wants to distribute incoming application traffic automatically across multiple EC2 instances in different Availability Zones to improve fault tolerance and availability. Which AWS service is designed for this? ⬜ Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
⬜ Amazon S3
⬜ AWS Storage Gateway
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
A company needs a fully managed relational database compatible with MySQL that automatically handles patching, backups, and replication. Which type of AWS database service fits this need? ⬜ Amazon DynamoDB
⬜ Amazon RDS (or Amazon Aurora)
⬜ Amazon ElastiCache
⬜ Amazon S3 Glacier
A company needs a fully managed, key-value and document NoSQL database that delivers consistent, single-digit millisecond performance at virtually any scale. Which AWS service fits this requirement? ⬜ Amazon DynamoDB
⬜ Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
⬜ AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS)
⬜ Amazon Redshift
A company wants to reduce database read latency for a frequently accessed dataset by caching query results in memory. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this? ⬜ Amazon ElastiCache
⬜ AWS Storage Gateway
⬜ Amazon FSx
⬜ AWS Backup
Which core components make up an Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) network, allowing a company to define an isolated section of the AWS Cloud with its own IP address range? ⬜ Subnets, route tables, and gateways
⬜ S3 buckets only
⬜ DynamoDB tables only
⬜ AWS Lambda functions only
A company wants a scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service to route end users to their application, and also wants to register a new domain name. Which AWS service provides both capabilities? ⬜ Amazon Route 53
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon CloudFront only
⬜ Amazon VPC
A company wants a dedicated, private network connection between its on-premises data center and AWS, bypassing the public internet for more consistent network performance. Which AWS service should they use? ⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
⬜ Amazon CloudFront
⬜ AWS Config
A company stores infrequently accessed data that must still be retrievable within milliseconds when needed, but wants to minimize storage costs compared to its frequently accessed data. Which Amazon S3 storage class fits this use case? ⬜ S3 Standard
⬜ S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
⬜ S3 Glacier Deep Archive
⬜ Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS
A company wants a fully managed AI service that can add pre-built machine learning capabilities like building conversational chatbots to its application without needing deep ML expertise. Which AWS service fits this? ⬜ Amazon Lex
⬜ Amazon EBS
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
An organization is currently operating MySQL databases on its own on-premises servers. To reduce the operational burden of database maintenance and management, the organization wants to move to a fully managed AWS database offering. Which migration strategy best aligns with this goal? ⬜ Rehost the MySQL databases as-is on Amazon EC2 instances, keeping full control over the operating system and database software.
⬜ Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the on-premises MySQL databases to Amazon RDS for MySQL.
⬜ Back up the on-premises databases to Amazon S3 and manually restore them onto new self-managed database servers within a VPC.
⬜ Replace the MySQL databases with Amazon DynamoDB tables to remove the need for database administration entirely.
Domain 4: Billing, Pricing, and Support (12%) A company has a steady, predictable EC2 workload it expects to run continuously for the next year and wants to reduce its compute costs compared to On-Demand pricing in exchange for a commitment. Which purchasing option is generally the best fit? ⬜ Spot Instances
⬜ Reserved Instances or Savings Plans
⬜ Pay only On-Demand pricing with no commitment
⬜ Dedicated Hosts, chosen purely for cost savings
A company wants to set spending thresholds for its AWS usage and receive automated alerts when actual or forecasted costs exceed those thresholds. Which AWS service is designed for this? ⬜ AWS Budgets
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
⬜ AWS Artifact
A company wants to visualize and analyze its historical AWS spending patterns over time, broken down by service, to identify cost trends. Which AWS tool is designed for this? ⬜ AWS Cost Explorer
⬜ Amazon CloudWatch Logs
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
Before deploying a new workload, a company wants to estimate the monthly cost of a proposed AWS architecture based on selected services and configurations. Which AWS tool is designed for this pre-deployment cost estimation? ⬜ AWS Pricing Calculator
⬜ AWS Config
⬜ Amazon GuardDuty
⬜ AWS CloudTrail
A company manages multiple AWS accounts for different departments and wants to combine usage across all accounts onto a single bill, potentially unlocking volume pricing discounts. Which AWS capability supports this? ⬜ AWS Organizations consolidated billing
⬜ AWS Direct Connect
⬜ Amazon Route 53
⬜ AWS Artifact
A startup with no dedicated operations team wants access to basic AWS Support for billing and account questions at no additional cost beyond their AWS usage. Which AWS Support plan provides this baseline? ⬜ AWS Basic Support, included automatically with every AWS account
⬜ AWS Enterprise Support only
⬜ AWS Business Support only
⬜ No support is available unless a paid plan is purchased

contents:
Comprehensive list of Free Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer (AI-103) exam questions, grouped by official exam domain, curated for cracking the exam with confidence.
Disclaimer: Microsoft Azure is a protected Brand. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with Microsoft. These are not the official Microsoft exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from the web resources of Microsoft Learn. These questions cover all the objectives and services of the AI-103 official exam and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Note: AI-102 (Azure AI Engineer Associate) retired on June 30, 2026 and has been replaced by AI-103 (Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate), the current active exam. These questions target AI-103 and use Microsoft’s current “Microsoft Foundry” / “Foundry Tools” branding for what were previously called Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI services.
Online Practice Exams Take all 67 questions as timed online practice exams in the real exam format:-
Free Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer (AI-103) Online Practice Exam
Overview This is an Associate level certification for Azure AI engineers who build, manage, and deploy AI apps and agents using Microsoft Foundry. Requires experience developing apps with Python, along with familiarity with general AI, generative AI, and Azure services. Exam code is AI-103; cost varies by country/region. Exam duration is 120 minutes, proctored, with interactive question components. Passing score is 700 (out of 1000). Question format includes multiple choice, multiple response, and interactive/case-study style questions. Like other Microsoft Associate certifications, it is valid for 1 year and can be renewed with a free online assessment. Study Guide for more details. 67 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 Plan and Manage an Azure AI Solution 28% 20 2 Implement Generative AI and Agentic Solutions 32% 21 3 Implement Computer Vision Solutions 14% 8 4 Implement Text Analysis Solutions 14% 9 5 Implement Information Extraction Solutions 12% 9 Domain 1: Plan and Manage an Azure AI Solution (28%) A company wants a single, unified platform to discover and deploy models from a large model catalog, build both simple declarative agents and full-code hosted agents, and get built-in tracing, evaluation, and governance for all of it. Which Microsoft platform is purpose-built for this? ⬜ Microsoft Foundry
⬜ Azure Kubernetes Service
⬜ Azure DevOps
⬜ Azure Data Factory
A developer wants to provision a single Azure resource that provides access to multiple AI capabilities at once (such as vision, language, and speech), using one endpoint and one set of keys, rather than provisioning and managing a separate resource for each capability. Which Azure resource type should be created? ⬜ A single-service resource
⬜ A multi-service resource
⬜ A resource group
⬜ A management group
An enterprise application calls an Azure AI Language endpoint from a backend service running on an Azure VM, and the security team wants to avoid storing and rotating a static API key in application configuration. Which authentication approach should be used instead? ⬜ Microsoft Entra ID authentication using a managed identity
⬜ Hardcoding the API key directly in source code
⬜ Sharing the API key over email with the development team
⬜ Disabling authentication on the resource
A company deploys a resume-screening AI model and later discovers it consistently ranks candidates from certain demographic groups lower, even when their qualifications are equivalent. Which Microsoft responsible AI principle is most directly violated? ⬜ Fairness
⬜ Transparency
⬜ Accountability
⬜ Privacy and security
A hospital deploying a diagnostic-support AI model wants to ensure the system performs consistently and safely under a wide range of real-world conditions, including unusual or edge-case patient data, and minimizes the risk of harmful errors. Which responsible AI principle does this concern primarily reflect? ⬜ Reliability and safety
⬜ Inclusiveness
⬜ Fairness
⬜ Transparency
A company building a customer-facing chatbot wants users to always be clearly informed that they are interacting with an AI system rather than a human agent, and wants the chatbot’s capabilities and limitations to be clearly documented for stakeholders. Which responsible AI principle does this practice support? ⬜ Transparency
⬜ Fairness
⬜ Privacy and security
⬜ Reliability and safety
A team building a generative AI chat application wants to automatically detect and block model outputs that fall into categories like hate speech, violence, self-harm, or sexual content, with configurable severity thresholds for each category. Which Microsoft Foundry capability provides this? ⬜ Content Safety / content filtering
⬜ Azure Resource Manager
⬜ Azure Cost Management
⬜ Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access
A regulated financial services company wants to ensure that traffic to its Microsoft Foundry resource never traverses the public internet, restricting access to only its own private Azure virtual network. Which capability should it configure on the Foundry resource? ⬜ Private endpoint / virtual network isolation
⬜ A resource lock
⬜ A higher pricing tier
⬜ Multi-factor authentication for end users
A startup wants to try several AI capabilities during development at no cost before committing to a paid tier, understanding that this tier has significantly lower request limits than production tiers. Which type of pricing tier should they select when creating their Azure AI resource? ⬜ The Free (F0) tier
⬜ The Standard (S) tier
⬜ A Reserved Instance
⬜ A customer-managed key tier
An organization wants to browse a catalog of thousands of models from Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and other providers, compare their capabilities, and deploy the chosen model for their generative AI application, all from within one platform. Which Microsoft Foundry feature enables this? ⬜ The model catalog
⬜ Azure Policy
⬜ Azure Advisor
⬜ Resource tags
A team wants to grant a developer the ability to call models and use tools within a Foundry project, without giving them permission to delete the underlying Foundry resource or change its network configuration. Which Azure access control approach should be used? ⬜ Assign a scoped role-based access control (RBAC) role such as a Cognitive Services User role at the project level
⬜ Give the developer the Owner role on the entire Azure subscription
⬜ Share the resource’s primary API key with the entire team
⬜ Disable authentication so the developer can access it freely
A compliance team requires that data stored at rest in a company’s Foundry resource be encrypted using encryption keys that the company generates, controls, and can revoke itself, rather than relying solely on Microsoft-managed keys. Which capability should be configured? ⬜ Customer-managed keys (CMK)
⬜ A resource lock
⬜ A free-tier pricing plan
⬜ Multi-service resource consolidation
After deploying a generative AI application on Microsoft Foundry, an operations team wants to continuously collect logs and metrics about model calls, latency, and errors, and route them into Application Insights for long-term analysis and alerting. Which built-in Foundry capability supports this? ⬜ Observability and tracing (integrated with Application Insights)
⬜ Azure Blueprints
⬜ Custom Vision training
⬜ The Translator service
A data science team wants to organize the agents, model deployments, and connected data sources for one customer engagement separately from another engagement, while both engagements share the same underlying Foundry resource, quota, and networking configuration. Which Microsoft Foundry construct should be used to separate the two engagements’ work? ⬜ Foundry projects
⬜ Resource locks
⬜ Availability zones
⬜ Region pairs
A generative AI application’s default content filtering configuration is blocking some legitimate medical-education content because it is being flagged under the “self-harm” category at a low severity threshold. The team has a valid, approved use case and wants to adjust how aggressively that specific category is filtered for their deployment. What should they configure? ⬜ A custom content filter configuration with an adjusted severity threshold for that category, subject to Microsoft’s eligibility and review process
⬜ Permanently disable all content filtering for the resource with no review
⬜ Switch to a completely different, less capable model
⬜ Ignore the issue since content filters cannot be adjusted
A company deploying an internal generative AI assistant wants to make sure its data used for grounding (via RAG) stays isolated to their own tenant and is not used to train or improve Microsoft’s underlying foundation models. Which general principle from Microsoft’s approach to Foundry and Azure OpenAI addresses this concern? ⬜ Customer data used in Foundry (including RAG grounding data and prompts) is not used to train the underlying foundation models without explicit customer opt-in
⬜ All customer data is automatically pooled to improve the shared model for every tenant
⬜ Data isolation cannot be guaranteed on any Azure AI service
⬜ Customers must disable logging entirely to prevent any data use
A team designing a generative AI application follows Microsoft’s layered approach to responsible AI and wants to apply a mitigation at the “Safety System” level to help block harmful model output, independent of any application-level prompt engineering or user education. Which Microsoft Foundry capability operates at this safety system level? ⬜ Guardrails (formerly called content filters)
⬜ DALL-E model support
⬜ Fine-tuning
⬜ A resource lock
You are planning a Microsoft Foundry project that will contain multiple agents. Each agent will access the same Azure AI Search resource. You need to recommend a solution to centrally manage the Azure AI Search credentials within the project, so the same configuration is used across all the agents. What should you recommend? ⬜ Enable role-based access control (RBAC) for the Azure AI Search resource.
⬜ Add a connection to the Azure AI Search resource.
⬜ Disable key-based access control on the Azure AI Search resource.
⬜ Create a managed private endpoint that connects to the Azure AI Search resource.
Which statement best describes how keys, secrets, and endpoints work together in an Azure-based AI application? ⬜ The key is the location where model responses are stored, and the endpoint retrieves those responses from Azure Key Vault.
⬜ The endpoint stores sensitive values for an AI application, and the key determines how much data the endpoint can return.
⬜ The endpoint is a URL for calling a deployed model, and the key (stored as a secret in Azure Key Vault) authenticates the request made to that endpoint.
⬜ The secret is the model’s raw training data, and the endpoint encrypts it before storage in Azure Key Vault.
A startup with no prior AI experience wants to start building AI-powered applications and agents on Azure — including things like a document-understanding bot and a conversational support agent — without building model training infrastructure from scratch. Which Azure capability should they use as the foundation for this work? ⬜ Microsoft Paint
⬜ Azure AI services and related Azure AI tooling (Microsoft Foundry)
⬜ Windows Calculator
⬜ File Explorer
Domain 2: Implement Generative AI and Agentic Solutions (32%) A developer deploys a GPT model in Microsoft Foundry and wants to establish the assistant’s persona, tone, and behavioral constraints (such as “always respond in formal English and never provide medical advice”) before any user messages are sent. Where should this instruction be placed in the chat completion request? ⬜ In the system message
⬜ In the user message
⬜ In the model’s fine-tuning dataset only
⬜ In the HTTP response headers
A developer wants a generative AI model to follow a specific output format (for example, always returning a JSON object with “name” and “summary” fields) and provides the model with two or three example input/output pairs directly in the prompt to demonstrate the desired pattern, without any model retraining. Which prompt engineering technique is this? ⬜ Few-shot prompting
⬜ Fine-tuning
⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Content filtering
A company wants its generative AI chatbot to answer questions using the company’s own internal, frequently updated product documentation, without retraining the underlying language model every time the documentation changes. Which architecture pattern is best suited to this requirement? ⬜ Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), grounding responses with a search index over the documentation
⬜ Increasing the model’s temperature parameter
⬜ Disabling the content filter
⬜ Switching to a smaller, cheaper model
A developer wants to build an AI agent by simply specifying its instructions, choosing a model from the catalog, and attaching a couple of built-in tools, all through the Foundry portal or SDK, without writing custom orchestration code or managing any infrastructure. Which Foundry agent-building approach fits this scenario? ⬜ A prompt agent
⬜ A hosted agent using a custom container
⬜ Fine-tuning a base model from scratch
⬜ Deploying a Kubernetes cluster
An agent built in Foundry Agent Service needs to look up a customer’s live order status from the company’s internal REST API during a conversation, something the underlying language model cannot know on its own. Which agent capability should be used to let the model invoke that external API during a conversation? ⬜ Tools / function calling
⬜ Increasing the max token limit
⬜ Enabling the free pricing tier
⬜ A resource lock
A team wants their Foundry agent to be able to write and execute a short Python snippet to perform a calculation or generate a chart as part of answering a user’s question, without the team writing custom code to sandbox and run that snippet themselves. Which built-in Foundry Agent Service tool provides this? ⬜ The code interpreter tool
⬜ The content filter
⬜ The pricing calculator
⬜ A management group
A company wants to build a complex workflow where a “router” agent analyzes an incoming customer request and delegates it to one of several specialized agents (billing, technical support, or returns), each with its own instructions and tools, and combines their outputs into a final response. What is this overall pattern called? ⬜ Multi-agent orchestration
⬜ Prompt engineering
⬜ Vector indexing
⬜ Resource tagging
A company has a very specific, narrow task (classifying support tickets into one of 12 internal categories using their own historical labeled examples) and wants the model itself to internalize this pattern so it performs the task accurately with short prompts and lower per-call token usage, rather than repeatedly including many examples in every prompt. Which approach best fits this requirement? ⬜ Fine-tuning a model on the company’s labeled dataset
⬜ Increasing the context window size only
⬜ Enabling multi-agent orchestration
⬜ Applying a resource lock
Before releasing a RAG-based chatbot to production, a team wants to systematically measure whether the chatbot’s answers are actually supported by the retrieved source documents (as opposed to being fabricated), using a repeatable, quantifiable process. Which Foundry capability addresses this? ⬜ Built-in evaluation metrics such as groundedness
⬜ Azure Cost Management budgets
⬜ Resource tags
⬜ Azure DNS
A developer sends a long conversation history along with a new user question to a deployed chat model, and receives an error indicating the request exceeds the model’s maximum input size. Which concept describes the limit that was exceeded? ⬜ The model’s context window (token limit)
⬜ The resource’s pricing tier
⬜ The content filter severity threshold
⬜ The region pair
A development team wants their Foundry agent to connect to an external, standardized tool server that exposes capabilities like file access and web search through a common, model-agnostic protocol, so the agent can use tools built by third parties without custom per-tool integration code. Which capability supports this? ⬜ Connecting to tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
⬜ Applying a resource lock
⬜ Increasing the pricing tier
⬜ Enabling Availability Zones
A team wants full code-level control over their agent’s orchestration logic, including custom control flow between multiple tool calls and model invocations, and plans to use an open-source agent orchestration framework rather than the portal’s no-code agent builder. Which Foundry agent-building approach matches this need? ⬜ A hosted agent using a code-first framework such as Agent Framework, LangGraph, or Semantic Kernel
⬜ A prompt agent configured entirely in the portal
⬜ Increasing the content filter severity threshold
⬜ Applying a customer-managed key
A developer building a RAG-based generative AI application assembles the final prompt that gets sent to the generative model from several distinct parts. Which of the following are typically components of that assembled prompt? (Select all that apply.) ⬜ The retrieved data as context (grounding data)
⬜ The query
⬜ Instructions for the response, such as tone, length, and specificity
⬜ The vector embeddings
An AI agent is connected to the Azure Language MCP server as a tool provider. When processing a user’s prompt, how does the agent determine which specific Azure Language MCP tool to call? ⬜ The agent matches the prompt to the tool descriptions it receives from the MCP server
⬜ The developer writes custom routing logic to direct each prompt to a specific tool
⬜ The MCP server itself analyzes the prompt and automatically routes it to a tool
⬜ The user manually selects which tool should handle their prompt before sending it
What is the primary role of the Azure Language MCP server in an agentic AI solution? ⬜ To expose Azure Language’s text analysis capabilities — such as PII redaction, sentiment analysis, entity extraction, and summarization — as MCP tools that agents can call
⬜ To train and fine-tune custom language models for use by AI agents
⬜ To deploy and manage large language models within an Azure subscription
⬜ To provide a no-code portal for building declarative prompt agents
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains a high-traffic agent. After a recent update, operational costs increase significantly, even though monitoring confirms the volume of user traffic to the agent is unchanged. You suspect that changes to the request or response characteristics are causing the increase. You need to identify whether the additional costs are driven by the model input size, the model output size, or expanded tool usage. Which observability capability should you use? ⬜ Evaluation metrics
⬜ Token usage
⬜ Latency
⬜ Run success rate
What are the components of the prompt in a generative model using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)? (Select all that apply.) ⬜ The retrieved data as context
⬜ The query
⬜ Instructions for the response, such as tone, length, and specificity
⬜ The vector embeddings
How does an agent determine which Azure AI Language MCP tool to call when processing a user’s prompt? ⬜ The developer writes routing logic to direct each prompt to a specific tool.
⬜ The agent matches the prompt to tool descriptions received from the MCP server.
⬜ The MCP server analyzes the prompt and automatically routes it to a tool.
⬜ The client randomly selects among all available tools.
What capability of Microsoft Foundry helps mitigate harmful content generation at the safety system level? ⬜ Fine-tuning
⬜ DALL-E model support
⬜ Guardrails and controls (content safety filtering)
⬜ Prompt flow orchestration
When constructing a prompt for a generative AI model in a retrieval-augmented application, which of the following is typically authored as part of the prompt itself, rather than produced internally by the retrieval system? ⬜ Instructions for the response, such as desired tone, length, and specificity
⬜ The vector embeddings computed for the retrieved documents
⬜ The similarity scores calculated between the query and indexed vectors
⬜ The index metadata describing how documents were chunked and embedded
A developer wants a generative AI model to return code in a specific programming language, following a particular structure, and respecting certain constraints (for example, no external libraries, under 50 lines). Which approach to writing the prompt is most effective? ⬜ Ask only for “code” with no further detail
⬜ Avoid describing the expected result and let the model infer everything
⬜ Include unrelated background text before the request
⬜ Specify the language, the task, any constraints, and the required output format
Domain 3: Implement Computer Vision Solutions (14%) A marketing team wants to generate original promotional images from text descriptions (for example, “a minimalist product photo of a coffee mug on a wooden table”) as part of their generative AI application. Which type of model should be deployed for this capability? ⬜ An image generation model (such as a DALL-E-family model)
⬜ A speech-to-text model
⬜ A text embedding model
⬜ A key phrase extraction model
A media company wants to automatically generate a short natural-language caption describing the content of each uploaded photo (for example, “a dog running on a beach”), along with a list of relevant tags. Which Azure Vision capability should they use? ⬜ Image Analysis (captioning and tagging)
⬜ Custom Vision object detection
⬜ Document Intelligence
⬜ Translator
A manufacturer wants to train a model that can tell the difference between three specific types of proprietary machine parts in photos taken on their factory floor, a distinction that no general-purpose, prebuilt vision model would know out of the box. Which Azure service is designed for training this kind of custom image classification model using the company’s own labeled images? ⬜ Custom Vision
⬜ Azure Vision Image Analysis
⬜ Face service
⬜ Video Indexer
In addition to classifying what is in an image overall, a retailer wants a model that can also draw bounding boxes around each individual product on a store shelf and identify the location of each one in the photo. Which Custom Vision project type should be created? ⬜ Object detection
⬜ Image classification
⬜ Sentiment analysis
⬜ Key phrase extraction
An access-control vendor wants to build a solution that can detect the presence and location of human faces in a video feed and analyze attributes for legitimate, approved access-control scenarios, in compliance with Microsoft’s Limited Access policies governing facial recognition. Which Azure Vision capability is relevant here? ⬜ The Face service
⬜ Custom Vision image classification
⬜ Translator
⬜ Question answering
A media company has a large archive of video files and wants to automatically extract insights such as spoken transcripts, detected faces, keywords, and scene changes from each video, without manually reviewing the footage. Which Azure AI capability is purpose-built for extracting these combined insights from video content? ⬜ Azure AI Video Indexer
⬜ Custom Vision object detection
⬜ Document Intelligence
⬜ Key phrase extraction on transcripts only
A quality-control application on a manufacturing line needs to identify whether a product on the assembly line is a specific one of five known defect types, using photos captured by a fixed camera, and the categories are mutually exclusive (a product has exactly one defect type or none). Which Custom Vision project type is the best fit? ⬜ Image classification (multiclass)
⬜ Object detection
⬜ OCR
⬜ Video Indexer
You are deploying a support agent that enables users to upload photos. You need to automatically classify uploaded images for harmful content, and the solution must block content based on severity levels. What should you do? ⬜ Implement image moderation.
⬜ Enable prompt shields.
⬜ Apply keyword scanning to optical character recognition (OCR) output by using Azure Vision in Foundry Tools.
⬜ Use blocklists.
Domain 4: Implement Text Analysis Solutions (14%) A retail company wants to automatically determine whether each customer product review expresses a positive, negative, mixed, or neutral opinion, and also identify which specific aspects of the product (like “battery life” or “screen quality”) drove that opinion. Which Azure Language capability should be used? ⬜ Sentiment analysis and opinion mining
⬜ Key phrase extraction
⬜ Language detection
⬜ Named entity recognition
A news aggregation service wants to automatically pull out the most important topics and concepts from each article (such as “climate policy,” “renewable energy,” and “carbon tax”) to use as article tags, without extracting full sentences. Which Azure Language capability fits this need? ⬜ Key phrase extraction
⬜ Sentiment analysis
⬜ PII detection
⬜ Custom question answering
A healthcare provider needs to automatically identify and redact sensitive personal details — such as patient names, phone numbers, and social security numbers — from free-text clinical notes before sharing them with a research partner. Which Azure Language capability is designed for this? ⬜ PII (Personally Identifiable Information) detection
⬜ Custom Vision object detection
⬜ Translator
⬜ Video Indexer
A customer support bot needs to determine what a user is trying to accomplish from a free-text message (for example, recognizing the intent “CheckOrderStatus” and extracting the entity “order number: 12345”) so it can route the request to the right backend workflow. Which Azure Language capability is purpose-built for this intent-and-entity extraction task? ⬜ Conversational Language Understanding (CLU)
⬜ Sentiment analysis
⬜ OCR
⬜ Video Indexer
An enterprise wants to build a FAQ bot that answers employee questions by matching them against a curated set of question-and-answer pairs drawn from HR policy documents, returning the best matching pre-written answer rather than generating a new response. Which Azure Language capability is designed for this? ⬜ Custom question answering (CQA)
⬜ Named entity recognition
⬜ Key phrase extraction
⬜ Custom Vision
A global e-commerce platform wants to automatically translate product descriptions from English into a dozen other languages for its international storefronts, preserving formatting where possible. Which Azure AI service should be used? ⬜ Azure Translator
⬜ Azure Language sentiment analysis
⬜ Azure Vision OCR
⬜ Custom question answering
A content moderation system ingests text from many countries and first needs to automatically determine which language each piece of text is written in before routing it to the correct language-specific downstream analysis pipeline. Which Azure Language capability accomplishes this first step? ⬜ Language detection
⬜ Sentiment analysis
⬜ Key phrase extraction
⬜ PII detection
You are creating an agent workflow in a Microsoft Foundry project to support natural voice interactions. The agent must receive continuous audio input, convert the input into text for reasoning, and then return spoken responses to a user. The workflow must support turn-taking dynamics, where the agent begins to generate speech output before the user finishes speaking, and must operate with low latency to maintain a conversational experience. You need to enable both speech to text and text to speech in a real-time agent interaction. What should you do? ⬜ Use an embeddings model to encode the audio, and then decode the audio into text and speech.
⬜ Use batch transcription to convert the audio input and return text responses from the agent.
⬜ Use speech translation to convert the audio into another language and return the translated text.
⬜ Use real-time speech to text for incoming audio and text to speech for agent responses.
A developer writes code that creates a TextAnalyticsClient object, supplying it with the resource’s endpoint and an AzureKeyCredential, and then calls methods on that object to analyze sentiment and extract key phrases from text. What is the purpose of this client object in the Azure Language SDK? ⬜ It stores UI settings for the application
⬜ It helps application code communicate with the Azure Language service
⬜ It stores the text to be analyzed
⬜ It renders the analysis results in a user interface
Domain 5: Implement Information Extraction Solutions (12%) In a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, documents and user queries are converted into high-dimensional numerical representations so that semantically similar pieces of text can be found even when they don’t share exact keywords. What are these numerical representations called? ⬜ Embeddings
⬜ Tokens
⬜ Resource tags
⬜ System messages
A logistics company wants to extract all the printed and handwritten text from scanned shipping labels and warehouse documents so it can be indexed and searched. Which Azure Vision capability is designed specifically for this text-extraction task? ⬜ OCR (Optical Character Recognition / Read API)
⬜ Face detection
⬜ Image captioning
⬜ Spatial analysis
An accounts payable team receives thousands of vendor invoices in varying layouts and wants to automatically extract standard fields (vendor name, invoice number, total amount, due date) without training any custom model, since invoices are a well-known, common document type. Which Azure AI capability should they use? ⬜ A prebuilt Document Intelligence model (such as the invoice model)
⬜ Custom Vision object detection
⬜ Conversational Language Understanding
⬜ Video Indexer
A logistics company uses a proprietary bill-of-lading form with a unique layout not covered by any of Document Intelligence’s prebuilt models, and wants to extract specific custom fields consistently from this form. What should they do? ⬜ Train a custom Document Intelligence model using labeled examples of their own form
⬜ Use the prebuilt invoice model as-is without modification
⬜ Use Custom Vision image classification instead
⬜ Use the Translator service to reformat the document
A company wants Azure AI Search to automatically pull new and updated documents from an Azure Blob Storage container on a recurring schedule and add them to a search index, without writing custom code to push each document into the index manually. Which Azure AI Search component enables this automatic, scheduled data pull? ⬜ An indexer
⬜ A skillset
⬜ A knowledge store
⬜ A vector index only
While indexing a large set of scanned PDF contracts, a company wants Azure AI Search to automatically run OCR to extract text from the scanned images, detect and redact personal information, and extract key phrases, all as part of the indexing pipeline, before the content lands in the search index. Which Azure AI Search feature orchestrates this chain of AI processing steps? ⬜ A skillset (AI enrichment pipeline)
⬜ A resource lock
⬜ A management group
⬜ A region pair
A knowledge mining solution needs to find documents that are conceptually similar to a user’s query even when the query uses completely different wording than the source documents (for example, matching “car won’t start” to a document about “vehicle fails to power on”). Plain keyword search alone would miss this match. Which Azure AI Search capability should be enabled to support this kind of conceptual matching? ⬜ Vector search (using embeddings)
⬜ A resource lock
⬜ OCR skill only
⬜ Multi-service resource consolidation
During the AI enrichment process for a set of customer support transcripts, a company wants to detect and mask any personal information (such as phone numbers or email addresses) that appears in the transcripts, as one of the automated steps in the same pipeline that also extracts key phrases and runs OCR. Which Azure AI Search skill should be added to the skillset for this specific requirement? ⬜ The PII detection skill
⬜ The image analysis skill
⬜ The language detection skill only
⬜ The custom entity lookup skill only
You have a chat app in a Microsoft Foundry project and an Azure AI Search vectorized index. You need to connect to the index to meet the following requirements: complex questions must retrieve information from multiple chunks; multi-turn conversations must influence retrieval planning; and retrievals must run in parallel to reduce latency. Which retrieval approach should you use? ⬜ Classic Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Chain of thought
⬜ Agentic Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
⬜ Iterative retrieval
