contents:
Comprehensive list of Free Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam questions, grouped by official exam domain, curated for cracking the exam with confidence.
Disclaimer: Kubernetes and the CNCF Certified Kubernetes Administrator program are protected brands. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) or The Linux Foundation. These are not the official CKA exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from the official Kubernetes documentation and the publicly published CKA curriculum. These questions cover all the objectives of the CKA official exam, and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Note: The real CKA exam is 100% hands-on and performance-based — you solve live kubectl/cluster tasks in a terminal, not multiple-choice questions. The questions below are concept-check practice questions, in the same format as our other certification posts, meant to solidify your understanding of every CKA curriculum topic before you practice the actual hands-on labs.
Free Online Practice Exam Take all 50 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:-
Free Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) Online Practice Exam
Overview This is a performance-based, hands-on certification (no multiple-choice on the real exam) for Kubernetes administrators covering cluster installation, configuration, networking, storage, and troubleshooting. Requires 6 to 8 weeks of hands-on practice depending upon your familiarity with Linux and containers. The exam costs 445 USD per attempt and includes one free retake. You need to solve 15 to 20 performance-based tasks in 120 mins from your laptop under the supervision of an online proctor, working directly in a live terminal/cluster environment. Passing score is 66%. The curriculum is updated quarterly to track new Kubernetes releases (this post follows the CNCF curriculum targeting the latest generally available Kubernetes release at time of writing). The certification is valid for 2 years. CKA Curriculum and Official Exam Page for more details. 50 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration 25% 12 2 Workloads and Scheduling 15% 8 3 Services and Networking 20% 10 4 Storage 10% 5 5 Troubleshooting 30% 15 Domain 1: Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration (25%) An administrator is bootstrapping a new Kubernetes control-plane node using kubeadm init. Which component is responsible for initializing the cluster’s control-plane components and generating the initial join token for worker nodes? ⬜ kubectl
⬜ kubeadm
⬜ kubelet
⬜ containerd
A cluster administrator wants to upgrade a kubeadm-provisioned cluster from one minor version to the next. Which statement correctly describes the required order of operations? ⬜ Upgrade all worker nodes first, then upgrade the control-plane node last.
⬜ Upgrade the kubeadm tool and the control-plane node first, then upgrade worker nodes one at a time.
⬜ Upgrade kubelet on every node simultaneously without draining any nodes.
⬜ Upgrades can be applied directly by editing the etcd database.
Which Kubernetes object type should be used to grant a specific user permission to read Pods within a single namespace, following the principle of least privilege? ⬜ ClusterRole bound with a ClusterRoleBinding
⬜ Role bound with a RoleBinding
⬜ ServiceAccount only, with no Role
⬜ PodSecurityPolicy
An administrator needs to take a consistent backup of a kubeadm cluster’s cluster state so it can be restored later. Which component’s data must be backed up to fully recover cluster state? ⬜ Only the kubelet configuration files on each node.
⬜ The etcd data store.
⬜ Only the container images cached on each node.
⬜ The local kubeconfig file on the administrator’s laptop.
A Pod needs to run directly on a specific node and be managed by the kubelet on that node without going through the normal scheduler or API-server-managed Deployment mechanism (commonly used to run control-plane components like kube-apiserver in a kubeadm cluster). What kind of Pod is this? ⬜ A DaemonSet Pod
⬜ A static Pod
⬜ A StatefulSet Pod
⬜ A Job Pod
An administrator has multiple kubeconfig files for different clusters and wants to switch between them easily using a single kubectl command context. Which kubeconfig element should be used to switch between clusters and users? ⬜ A context
⬜ A ServiceAccount token
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
⬜ A StorageClass
Which statement about Kubernetes cluster component TLS certificates is correct? ⬜ Kubernetes cluster components never use TLS certificates; all communication is unencrypted by default.
⬜ kubeadm automatically generates and manages the certificates required for control-plane components to communicate securely, and administrators can inspect their expiration with kubeadm certs check-expiration.
⬜ Certificates only need to be renewed once, at initial cluster creation, and never again.
⬜ Worker nodes do not require any certificates to join a cluster.
An administrator needs to perform maintenance on a worker node and wants to safely evict all Pods from it while preventing new Pods from being scheduled there. Which command sequence is correct? ⬜ kubectl delete node, then kubectl create node
⬜ kubectl cordon , then kubectl drain ⬜ kubectl taint only, with no cordon or drain
⬜ kubectl scale node –replicas=0
A platform team wants to extend the Kubernetes API with their own custom object type, such as a Database resource, that can be managed with standard kubectl commands. Which Kubernetes feature enables this? ⬜ A ConfigMap
⬜ A Custom Resource Definition (CRD)
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
⬜ A ResourceQuota
A company wants to package and deploy a complex application (with multiple Kubernetes manifests, configurable values, and versioned releases) more easily than applying raw YAML files individually. Which widely used CNCF tool is designed for this? ⬜ Helm
⬜ etcdctl
⬜ kubeadm
⬜ crictl
For high availability, a company is designing a kubeadm cluster’s control plane with multiple control-plane nodes. Which etcd topology co-locates etcd members on the same nodes as the control-plane components? ⬜ External etcd topology
⬜ Stacked etcd topology
⬜ Single-node etcd topology
⬜ etcd is never required in a highly available cluster
Which statement about Kubernetes user authentication is correct? ⬜ Kubernetes has a built-in, mandatory user-management database for human users, similar to a traditional operating system.
⬜ Kubernetes does not manage human user objects directly; instead it relies on external identity sources (such as client certificates, tokens, or an external identity provider) and authorizes requests via mechanisms like RBAC.
⬜ All users are automatically cluster administrators unless explicitly restricted.
⬜ ServiceAccounts and regular users are functionally identical with no differences in how they authenticate.
Domain 2: Workloads and Scheduling (15%) A team wants to ensure a fixed number of identical Pod replicas of a stateless web application are always running, with automatic rollout of new versions and the ability to roll back. Which Kubernetes object should they use? ⬜ Deployment
⬜ DaemonSet
⬜ Job
⬜ Static Pod
A company wants exactly one instance of a log-collection agent Pod running on every node in the cluster, including new nodes as they’re added. Which Kubernetes object is designed for this? ⬜ Deployment
⬜ DaemonSet
⬜ StatefulSet
⬜ ReplicaSet
A batch process needs to run a Pod to completion exactly once, and Kubernetes should retry it automatically if it fails. Which object should be used? ⬜ CronJob
⬜ Job
⬜ ReplicaSet
⬜ DaemonSet
Which Kubernetes object should be used to run a data-cleanup task automatically every night at 2 AM? ⬜ Job
⬜ CronJob
⬜ Deployment
⬜ ReplicaSet
A Pod’s container needs access to a database password without hardcoding it in the container image or in a plain-text ConfigMap. Which Kubernetes object is designed to hold this kind of sensitive value? ⬜ ConfigMap
⬜ Secret
⬜ PersistentVolumeClaim
⬜ ResourceQuota
A team notices that one Pod is consuming so much CPU that it starves other Pods on the same node. Which Pod spec fields should be set to prevent a single container from exceeding a defined CPU ceiling? ⬜ requests.memory only
⬜ limits.cpu (and limits.memory as needed)
⬜ affinity rules only
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
A company wants Pods to be scheduled only on nodes that have GPUs, using a required (hard) scheduling rule based on node labels. Which mechanism should they use? ⬜ A taint applied to the Pod
⬜ requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution node affinity
⬜ A NetworkPolicy selector
⬜ A PersistentVolumeClaim selector
A Pod needs a helper container to run and successfully complete a setup task (such as fetching configuration) BEFORE the main application container starts. Which Kubernetes feature is designed for this? ⬜ A sidecar container running continuously alongside the main container.
⬜ An init container.
⬜ A second Deployment.
⬜ A DaemonSet.
Domain 3: Services and Networking (20%) A company wants to expose a set of backend Pods to other Pods within the cluster only, using a stable internal IP address and DNS name, with no external access. Which Service type should they use? ⬜ ClusterIP
⬜ NodePort
⬜ LoadBalancer
⬜ ExternalName
A company needs to route external HTTP traffic to multiple backend Services based on the request’s hostname and URL path, using a single external entry point rather than provisioning a separate load balancer per Service. Which Kubernetes object is designed for this? ⬜ Ingress
⬜ NetworkPolicy
⬜ Endpoints
⬜ PersistentVolume
By default, can Pods in a Kubernetes cluster communicate with any other Pod, across any namespace, without restriction? ⬜ No — Kubernetes blocks all Pod-to-Pod traffic by default until a NetworkPolicy explicitly allows it.
⬜ Yes — by default, Kubernetes networking allows all Pods to communicate with all other Pods, unless a NetworkPolicy is used to restrict traffic.
⬜ Pods can only ever communicate within the same Deployment.
⬜ Pod-to-Pod communication requires manually configuring static routes for every Pod IP.
A security team wants to restrict a set of backend Pods so that they only accept incoming traffic from Pods labeled role=frontend, and reject all other traffic. Which Kubernetes object should be used? ⬜ A ResourceQuota
⬜ A NetworkPolicy with an ingress rule matching the role=frontend label selector
⬜ A Secret
⬜ A StorageClass
Within a Kubernetes cluster using the default cluster DNS add-on, what is the standard DNS name format used to reach a Service named payments in namespace prod from another namespace? ⬜ payments.svc.cluster.local only
⬜ payments.prod.svc.cluster.local
⬜ prod-payments.default.svc
⬜ payments://prod
Which statement about the Container Network Interface (CNI) in Kubernetes is correct? ⬜ Kubernetes includes one single, built-in networking implementation with no plugin architecture.
⬜ CNI is a plugin specification that allows different networking providers (such as Calico, Cilium, or Flannel) to implement Pod networking, and a cluster requires a CNI plugin to be installed for Pod-to-Pod networking to function.
⬜ CNI plugins are only used for Ingress traffic, not Pod-to-Pod communication.
⬜ CNI has been fully replaced by NetworkPolicy objects and is no longer required.
A company wants to expose a Service on a static port on every node’s IP address so it can be reached from outside the cluster, without provisioning a cloud load balancer. Which Service type fits this requirement? ⬜ ClusterIP
⬜ NodePort
⬜ ExternalName
⬜ Headless Service
An application needs to discover the individual, stable network identities of each Pod backing a Service (rather than a single load-balanced virtual IP), such as for a clustered database. Which Service configuration supports this? ⬜ A LoadBalancer Service
⬜ A Headless Service (ClusterIP set to None)
⬜ A NodePort Service
⬜ An Ingress resource
Which statement about how a Service finds the Pods it should route traffic to is correct? ⬜ A Service statically lists Pod IP addresses that never change.
⬜ A Service uses a label selector to dynamically match Pods, and Kubernetes tracks matching Pod IPs (traditionally via an Endpoints object, or EndpointSlices for scalability).
⬜ A Service can only route to Pods within the exact same Deployment object.
⬜ A Service requires manual updates to its Pod IP list every time a Pod restarts.
A platform team is evaluating the newer Kubernetes API for managing ingress traffic that offers more expressive, role-oriented routing configuration than the original Ingress resource. Which API are they most likely evaluating? ⬜ The Gateway API
⬜ The PodDisruptionBudget API
⬜ The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler API
⬜ The Admission Webhook API
Domain 4: Storage (10%) A cluster administrator has provisioned a piece of network storage as a cluster resource, and a developer wants their Pod to consume some of that storage without needing to know the underlying storage implementation details. Which two objects work together to achieve this? ⬜ ConfigMap and Secret
⬜ PersistentVolume (PV) and PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)
⬜ DaemonSet and StatefulSet
⬜ NetworkPolicy and Ingress
A company wants PersistentVolumes to be automatically created on-demand whenever a developer submits a PersistentVolumeClaim, rather than requiring an administrator to manually pre-provision volumes. Which object enables this dynamic provisioning? ⬜ A StorageClass
⬜ A ConfigMap
⬜ A ResourceQuota
⬜ A LimitRange
A Pod needs temporary scratch space that is shared between two containers in the same Pod, but the data does NOT need to survive if the Pod is deleted. Which volume type is MOST appropriate? ⬜ A PersistentVolumeClaim backed by network storage
⬜ An emptyDir volume
⬜ A StorageClass
⬜ A hostPath volume pointing to a critical system directory
Which PersistentVolume access mode allows the volume to be mounted as read-write by a single node at a time? ⬜ ReadWriteMany (RWX)
⬜ ReadOnlyMany (ROX)
⬜ ReadWriteOnce (RWO)
⬜ ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP), which allows unlimited nodes
A storage vendor wants to provide a Kubernetes-compatible storage driver for their proprietary storage system without modifying Kubernetes’ own source code. Which standard interface should they implement? ⬜ The Container Network Interface (CNI)
⬜ The Container Storage Interface (CSI)
⬜ The Container Runtime Interface (CRI)
⬜ The Custom Resource Definition (CRD) interface
Domain 5: Troubleshooting (30%) A Pod is stuck in Pending status and never gets scheduled. Which command should an administrator run FIRST to see the scheduling-related events explaining why? ⬜ kubectl logs ⬜ kubectl describe pod ⬜ kubectl delete pod ⬜ kubectl top pod A Pod’s container keeps restarting repeatedly and kubectl get pods shows its status as CrashLoopBackOff. Which command is MOST useful to see why the container is crashing, including logs from its previous run before the restart? ⬜ kubectl logs –previous
⬜ kubectl get nodes
⬜ kubectl cordon ⬜ kubectl scale deployment –replicas=0
An administrator suspects that the kube-scheduler static Pod on the control-plane node has failed to start. Where should they look to find the relevant static Pod manifest and container logs on that node? ⬜ Inside a ConfigMap named kube-scheduler-config.
⬜ The static Pod manifests directory (commonly /etc/kubernetes/manifests) and the container runtime/kubelet logs on that node.
⬜ Only inside the etcd database.
⬜ In the developer’s local kubeconfig file.
kubectl get componentstatuses (or checking control-plane health) shows the kube-controller-manager appears unhealthy on a kubeadm cluster. What is a reasonable next troubleshooting step? ⬜ Immediately reinstall the entire operating system on the node.
⬜ Check the kube-controller-manager static Pod’s status and logs on the control-plane node (e.g., with kubectl -n kube-system describe pod and container runtime logs).
⬜ Delete all Pods in all namespaces.
⬜ Ignore it since the controller-manager is optional for cluster function.
Users report that a web application’s Service is unreachable, even though its backend Pods show as Running. Which of the following is a valid troubleshooting step to isolate whether the issue is with the Service’s Pod selection? ⬜ Check that the Service’s label selector actually matches the labels on the backend Pods, and verify the resulting Endpoints/EndpointSlices are populated.
⬜ Immediately delete the Service and recreate the Deployment from scratch.
⬜ Increase the CPU limit on the backend Pods.
⬜ Change the container image tag to latest.
An administrator wants to view real-time CPU and memory usage of all Pods in a namespace to identify which one is consuming excessive resources. Which command and supporting component are required? ⬜ kubectl top pods, which requires the Metrics Server to be installed in the cluster.
⬜ kubectl get events, with no additional components required.
⬜ kubectl describe node, which always shows live Pod-level CPU/memory usage.
⬜ kubectl logs, which shows historical CPU/memory graphs.
A worker node shows a NotReady status in kubectl get nodes. Which of the following is the MOST relevant next troubleshooting step? ⬜ Check the kubelet’s status and logs on that node (e.g., systemctl status kubelet and journal logs), since kubelet health directly determines node readiness.
⬜ Delete the node object and assume it will self-heal with no other action.
⬜ Edit the ClusterRoleBinding for the default ServiceAccount.
⬜ Increase the replica count of unrelated Deployments in a different namespace.
A Pod remains stuck in ContainerCreating for a long time. kubectl describe pod shows an event about failing to pull the container image. Which of these is a plausible root cause to investigate? ⬜ The container image tag doesn’t exist, or the node lacks correct registry credentials/network access to pull it.
⬜ The Kubernetes API server has crashed and is not restartable.
⬜ The cluster’s etcd database has been corrupted beyond repair.
⬜ The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler was misconfigured.
An application inside a Pod cannot resolve other Services by their DNS names, though the Pod itself is Running. Which of the following is a reasonable early troubleshooting step? ⬜ Verify the Pod’s /etc/resolv.conf points to the cluster DNS service, and confirm the cluster DNS add-on (e.g., CoreDNS) Pods are running and healthy.
⬜ Increase the Pod’s memory limit.
⬜ Restart the kube-scheduler only.
⬜ Apply a new StorageClass.
Which command shows the recent lifecycle events for a specific object (such as a Pod, Deployment, or Node), which is often the fastest way to understand what went wrong? ⬜ kubectl apply -f
⬜ kubectl describe ⬜ kubectl config view
⬜ kubectl api-resources
A company wants application container logs to be collected and made durably available even after Pods are deleted or rescheduled, across the whole cluster. Which Kubernetes-native approach directly provides this out of the box? ⬜ Kubernetes provides this automatically with no additional setup required.
⬜ Kubernetes itself does not provide durable, cluster-wide log aggregation out of the box; a cluster-level logging architecture (e.g., a node-level logging agent shipping logs to a backend) must be deployed.
⬜ Only kubectl logs is needed, and it retains logs indefinitely by default.
⬜ PersistentVolumes automatically capture and store all container stdout/stderr.
An administrator wants to check whether the kube-apiserver itself is reachable and responding, as a first step when kubectl commands are timing out entirely. Which of these is a reasonable diagnostic action? ⬜ Check network connectivity to the API server’s endpoint/port and review the API server’s static Pod status and logs on the control-plane node.
⬜ Immediately restore the entire cluster from an old etcd snapshot without further investigation.
⬜ Delete and recreate all worker nodes.
⬜ Assume the issue is always with a single application Pod and check only that Pod’s logs.
A Pod has been running for a while, but the application inside seems to be serving errors, though the Pod’s status shows Running with 1/1 containers ready. What Kubernetes probe would help automatically detect and restart a container in this exact scenario going forward? ⬜ A startup probe only
⬜ A liveness probe configured to check the application’s actual health
⬜ A resource limit with no probes
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
An administrator wants a general reference for the recommended, systematic workflow to troubleshoot a failing application running in Kubernetes, from checking the Pod status down to container-level issues. Which official resource documents this? ⬜ The Kubernetes ‘Troubleshooting Applications’ task documentation.
⬜ The Kubernetes release notes.
⬜ The etcd API reference.
⬜ The kubeadm command-line reference only.
A container keeps getting terminated with an OOMKilled status shown in kubectl describe pod. What does this status indicate, and what is a reasonable remediation? ⬜ It indicates the container ran out of allocated memory and was killed by the kernel; consider increasing the container’s memory limit or investigating a memory leak in the application.
⬜ It indicates the container’s image failed to pull.
⬜ It indicates a DNS resolution failure inside the container.
⬜ It indicates the node has been cordoned by an administrator.

contents:
Comprehensive list of Free Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) exam questions curated for cracking the exam with confidence.
Disclaimer: Kubernetes and the CNCF Certified Kubernetes Application Developer program are protected brands. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) or The Linux Foundation. These are not the official CKAD exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from the official Kubernetes documentation and the publicly published CKAD curriculum. These questions cover all the objectives of the CKAD official exam, and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Note: The real CKAD exam is 100% hands-on and performance-based — you solve live kubectl/cluster tasks in a terminal, not multiple-choice questions. The questions below are concept-check practice questions, in the same format as our other certification posts, meant to solidify your understanding of every CKAD curriculum topic before you practice the actual hands-on labs. If you haven’t already, also check out our CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator) Exam Questions for the cluster-admin-focused counterpart to this exam.
Free Online Practice Exam Take all 50 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:-
Free Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) Online Practice Exam
Overview This is a performance-based, hands-on certification (no multiple-choice on the real exam) for developers who design, build, deploy, and troubleshoot applications on Kubernetes. Requires 4 to 6 weeks of hands-on practice depending upon your familiarity with containers and application development. The exam costs 445 USD per attempt and includes one free retake. You need to solve a set of performance-based tasks in 120 mins from your laptop under the supervision of an online proctor, working directly in a live terminal/cluster environment. The curriculum is updated quarterly to track new Kubernetes releases (this post follows the current CNCF CKAD curriculum). The certification is valid for 2 years. CKAD shares roughly half its curriculum with CKA (Services & Networking, and parts of workloads/troubleshooting) but is scoped to the application developer’s perspective rather than full cluster administration. Official Exam Page for more details. 50 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 Application Design and Build 20% 12 2 Application Deployment 20% 6 3 Application Observability and Maintenance 15% 8 4 Application Environment, Configuration and Security 25% 13 5 Services and Networking 20% 11 Domain 1: Application Design and Build (20%) A developer wants two containers in the same Pod to share the same network namespace (so they can reach each other over localhost) and the same set of mounted volumes. Which Kubernetes concept guarantees this? ⬜ Containers in the same Pod always share the Pod’s network namespace and can share mounted volumes by default.
⬜ Each container in a Pod always gets its own isolated network namespace.
⬜ Containers must be in separate Pods to share localhost networking.
⬜ Sharing localhost networking requires a dedicated NetworkPolicy.
A developer wants a lightweight helper container to run continuously alongside the main application container for the life of the Pod (for example, to stream logs to a remote endpoint), rather than running once before the main container starts. Which container type is designed for this? ⬜ An init container
⬜ A sidecar container
⬜ A Job
⬜ A DaemonSet
Which statement about Open Container Initiative (OCI) images is correct in the context of Kubernetes? ⬜ Kubernetes can only run images built specifically by Docker Desktop.
⬜ Kubernetes runs containers based on OCI-compliant container images and uses an OCI-compatible container runtime (such as containerd or CRI-O) to run them.
⬜ Kubernetes builds container images internally and does not use any image format standard.
⬜ OCI images can only be pulled from Docker Hub.
A developer wants to reduce a container image’s final size by excluding build-time tools and intermediate build artifacts from the image that actually gets deployed. Which Docker/OCI build technique is designed for this? ⬜ A multi-stage build, where a builder stage compiles the application and only the necessary artifacts are copied into a smaller final stage.
⬜ Running docker pull twice.
⬜ Setting a higher CPU limit in the Pod spec.
⬜ Adding more init containers to the Pod.
A Pod requires a specific container runtime feature and the cluster supports multiple container runtimes. Which Kubernetes interface standardizes how the kubelet communicates with any compliant container runtime (such as containerd or CRI-O)? ⬜ The Container Storage Interface (CSI)
⬜ The Container Runtime Interface (CRI)
⬜ The Container Network Interface (CNI)
⬜ The Custom Resource Definition (CRD) interface
A Pod has two containers: a main web server container and a helper container that must successfully fetch a TLS certificate before the web server starts. Which pattern correctly enforces this ordering? ⬜ Define the certificate-fetching container as a sidecar container.
⬜ Define the certificate-fetching container as an init container, since init containers run to completion, in order, before app containers start.
⬜ Put both containers in the same container image.
⬜ Use a NetworkPolicy to delay the web server’s start.
Which of these is a valid, commonly used multi-container Pod design pattern for adding functionality to a main application container without modifying its code? ⬜ The ‘ambassador’ pattern, where a helper container proxies network connections on behalf of the main container.
⬜ Running the same image twice with identical names in the same Pod.
⬜ Deploying two unrelated applications randomly into one Pod for convenience.
⬜ Disabling all containers except one at runtime.
A developer wants their application Pod to automatically restart failed containers, following the Pod’s restart policy. Which field controls this at the Pod level? ⬜ spec.restartPolicy
⬜ metadata.labels
⬜ spec.nodeName
⬜ spec.serviceAccountName
A developer needs to deploy a stateless REST API with 5 replicas and wants Kubernetes to automatically replace any replica that crashes, while supporting rolling updates. Which object should they create? ⬜ A bare Pod, repeated 5 times manually.
⬜ A Deployment with replicas: 5.
⬜ A StatefulSet with replicas: 5.
⬜ A Job with completions: 5.
A team is deploying a clustered database where each replica needs a stable, unique network identity (e.g., db-0, db-1, db-2) and its own dedicated persistent storage that survives Pod rescheduling. Which object should they use? ⬜ Deployment
⬜ DaemonSet
⬜ StatefulSet
⬜ ReplicaSet
A team wants a monitoring agent Pod to run on every node in the cluster (including future nodes added later), rather than a fixed replica count. Which object is the correct choice? ⬜ Deployment
⬜ DaemonSet
⬜ Job
⬜ CronJob
A batch report-generation script needs to run to completion once a day at midnight, and Kubernetes should retry it if it fails. Which object combination is correct? ⬜ A Deployment with replicas: 1
⬜ A CronJob, which creates a Job on the defined schedule
⬜ A DaemonSet with a schedule field
⬜ A bare Pod with restartPolicy: Always
Domain 2: Application Deployment (20%) A developer updates a Deployment’s container image to a new version, and Kubernetes gradually replaces old Pods with new ones while keeping the application available throughout. Which Deployment strategy is being used by default? ⬜ Recreate strategy
⬜ RollingUpdate strategy
⬜ Blue-green deployment, natively built into Deployment objects
⬜ Canary deployment, natively built into Deployment objects
After rolling out a new Deployment revision, the application starts failing. Which command lets the developer revert the Deployment to its previous working revision? ⬜ kubectl rollout undo deployment/
⬜ kubectl delete deployment/
⬜ kubectl scale deployment/ –replicas=0
⬜ kubectl cordon deployment/
A developer wants to control how many Pods can be unavailable at once during a Deployment’s rolling update, to balance rollout speed against maintaining capacity. Which Deployment fields control this? ⬜ replicas and selector
⬜ maxUnavailable and maxSurge under the RollingUpdate strategy
⬜ readinessProbe and livenessProbe
⬜ resources.requests and resources.limits
Which command correctly updates only the container image of an existing Deployment named web, triggering a new rollout, without editing the full YAML manifest? ⬜ kubectl set image deployment/web web-container=myapp:v2
⬜ kubectl get deployment web
⬜ kubectl label deployment web app=web
⬜ kubectl top deployment web
A developer wants to temporarily pause an in-progress Deployment rollout to make several changes without triggering multiple separate rollouts, then resume it as a single rollout. Which commands support this workflow? ⬜ kubectl rollout pause deployment/ … kubectl rollout resume deployment/
⬜ kubectl delete deployment/ then kubectl apply -f
⬜ kubectl cordon deployment/
⬜ kubectl drain deployment/
A StatefulSet named db with 3 replicas is being scaled down. In which order does Kubernetes terminate the Pods by default? ⬜ In random order, to maximize speed.
⬜ In reverse ordinal order — the highest-numbered Pod (e.g., db-2) is terminated first.
⬜ All Pods are terminated simultaneously regardless of ordinal.
⬜ In alphabetical order of the node names they’re running on.
Domain 3: Application Observability and Maintenance (15%) A container in a Pod is running but the application inside has deadlocked and stopped responding, though the process itself hasn’t exited. Which probe should be configured so Kubernetes detects this and restarts the container? ⬜ A startup probe only
⬜ A liveness probe
⬜ A readiness probe only, with no liveness probe
⬜ No probe is needed; Kubernetes detects deadlocks automatically
A Pod’s container is fully running but the application takes 30 seconds to warm up before it can serve traffic. Without any additional configuration, a naive liveness probe with a short timeout might kill the container before it finishes starting. Which probe type is specifically designed to solve this? ⬜ A readiness probe only
⬜ A startup probe, which disables liveness and readiness checks until it succeeds
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
⬜ A ResourceQuota
A Pod is Running, but a Service is not sending it any traffic. kubectl describe pod shows the container is not passing a certain probe. Which probe type, when failing, causes a Pod to be removed from a Service’s list of active endpoints without restarting the container? ⬜ Liveness probe
⬜ Readiness probe
⬜ Startup probe
⬜ Exec probe (as a category, unrelated to readiness)
A developer needs to see the last 50 lines of a currently running container’s logs, and then continue streaming new log lines as they’re generated. Which kubectl command accomplishes this? ⬜ kubectl logs –tail=50 -f
⬜ kubectl describe pod ⬜ kubectl top pod ⬜ kubectl get pod -o wide
A Pod has two containers, app and sidecar. Which command retrieves the logs specifically from the sidecar container? ⬜ kubectl logs -c sidecar
⬜ kubectl logs ⬜ kubectl exec – logs sidecar
⬜ kubectl describe pod -c sidecar
Which command displays real-time CPU and memory usage for all Pods in the current namespace, assuming the Metrics Server is installed? ⬜ kubectl get events
⬜ kubectl top pods
⬜ kubectl describe namespace
⬜ kubectl get componentstatuses
A developer wants their application to expose custom metrics (like request count or queue depth) in a format that a Prometheus-compatible monitoring stack can scrape. What is the standard approach? ⬜ Expose the metrics on an HTTP endpoint (commonly /metrics) in the Prometheus text exposition format, using a client library, so a Prometheus server can scrape it.
⬜ Write metrics directly into etcd from the application.
⬜ Metrics must be emailed to the monitoring team manually.
⬜ Use a NetworkPolicy to broadcast metrics to all Pods.
A Pod keeps restarting and kubectl get pods shows CrashLoopBackOff. Which command shows the logs from the PREVIOUS (already-terminated) instance of the container, which is often essential for diagnosing the crash? ⬜ kubectl logs –previous
⬜ kubectl logs –since=1h
⬜ kubectl get pod -o yaml
⬜ kubectl rollout status deployment/
Domain 4: Application Environment, Configuration and Security (25%) A developer building a container image wants to follow best practice by NOT running the application process as the root user inside the container. Where is this enforced at the Kubernetes Pod/container level? ⬜ In the Pod or container securityContext, using fields like runAsNonRoot and runAsUser.
⬜ In the container image’s file system permissions only, with no Kubernetes-level control.
⬜ In a NetworkPolicy.
⬜ In a StorageClass.
A development team wants to store their application container images in a private registry and have Kubernetes authenticate to pull them. Which Kubernetes object is used to hold registry credentials referenced by a Pod’s imagePullSecrets? ⬜ A ConfigMap
⬜ A Secret of type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
⬜ A ResourceQuota
⬜ A PodDisruptionBudget
A developer wants to inject a non-sensitive configuration value (such as a feature flag) into a container as an environment variable, sourced from a Kubernetes object that can be updated independently of the container image. Which object should they use? ⬜ A Secret
⬜ A ConfigMap
⬜ A PersistentVolumeClaim
⬜ A ResourceQuota
A developer needs to inject a database password into a container as an environment variable, but must avoid storing it in plain text within the Pod spec’s YAML or the container image. Which approach correctly meets this requirement? ⬜ Hardcode the password directly in the Deployment YAML’s env field.
⬜ Store the password in a Secret, and reference it in the container’s env using valueFrom.secretKeyRef.
⬜ Store the password in a public ConfigMap.
⬜ Bake the password into the container image at build time.
A developer wants an entire ConfigMap’s key-value pairs to appear as individual files inside a container, where each key becomes a filename and its value becomes the file’s content. Which approach achieves this? ⬜ Mount the ConfigMap as a volume in the Pod spec.
⬜ Reference the ConfigMap only via envFrom.
⬜ This is not possible; ConfigMaps can only be used as environment variables.
⬜ Use a StorageClass referencing the ConfigMap.
A Pod needs to make authenticated calls to the Kubernetes API server itself (for example, to list Pods in its own namespace) using an identity Kubernetes manages, rather than a human user’s credentials. Which object provides this identity? ⬜ A ServiceAccount
⬜ A ConfigMap
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
⬜ A PersistentVolume
A Pod’s ServiceAccount needs permission to list and get Secrets, but only within its own namespace, following least privilege. Which combination of objects correctly grants this? ⬜ A ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding scoped to the whole cluster.
⬜ A Role (scoped to the namespace) bound to the ServiceAccount via a RoleBinding.
⬜ No RBAC object is needed; ServiceAccounts have full access by default.
⬜ A NetworkPolicy allowing traffic to the Secrets API.
A security team wants to enforce that containers in a certain namespace cannot run as the root user and cannot escalate privileges, using a cluster-wide, built-in policy mechanism (rather than a third-party admission controller). Which Kubernetes-native feature should they use? ⬜ Pod Security Standards, enforced via Pod Security Admission at the namespace level.
⬜ A ConfigMap labeled security=enforced.
⬜ A ResourceQuota with a CPU limit.
⬜ A headless Service.
Which securityContext field, when set to true, prevents a container’s root filesystem from being written to, reducing the impact of certain container escape or tampering attempts? ⬜ runAsNonRoot
⬜ readOnlyRootFilesystem
⬜ allowPrivilegeEscalation
⬜ privileged
A namespace administrator wants to cap the total amount of CPU and memory that can be requested across ALL Pods in a namespace, to prevent one team from consuming the entire cluster’s capacity. Which object should they create? ⬜ A LimitRange
⬜ A ResourceQuota
⬜ A NetworkPolicy
⬜ A PodDisruptionBudget
A developer wants a Pod’s container to automatically pick up environment variables named after EVERY key in a ConfigMap, without listing each key individually. Which field should they use in the container spec? ⬜ env, listing each key one at a time
⬜ envFrom, referencing the ConfigMap
⬜ volumeMounts, with no ConfigMap reference
⬜ resources.requests
Which of these is generally considered a best practice regarding Secrets in Kubernetes? ⬜ Store Secrets in plain-text ConfigMaps to simplify management.
⬜ Limit which ServiceAccounts, Roles, and namespaces can access a given Secret using RBAC, and avoid printing Secret values into logs.
⬜ Commit raw Secret manifests containing plain-text sensitive values directly into a public source-code repository.
⬜ Grant every ServiceAccount in the cluster access to every Secret by default.
A developer wants to prevent a container from being able to escalate its privileges beyond its parent process, as an additional hardening measure alongside running as a non-root user. Which securityContext field controls this directly? ⬜ allowPrivilegeEscalation, set to false
⬜ readOnlyRootFilesystem, set to true
⬜ runAsUser, set to 0
⬜ hostNetwork, set to true
Domain 5: Services and Networking (20%) A security team wants to restrict a group of Pods labeled tier=backend so they can only receive traffic from Pods labeled tier=frontend, denying all other ingress traffic. Which object correctly enforces this? ⬜ A NetworkPolicy with an ingress rule that selects podSelector: {tier: backend} and allows from Pods matching tier: frontend.
⬜ A ResourceQuota restricting Pod count.
⬜ A ConfigMap labeled tier=backend.
⬜ A ServiceAccount bound to the backend Pods.
A developer has a Deployment of backend Pods and wants other Pods in the same cluster to reach them at a stable internal address, without exposing them outside the cluster. Which Service type is appropriate? ⬜ ClusterIP
⬜ NodePort
⬜ LoadBalancer
⬜ ExternalName
A developer wants a single external HTTP entry point that routes /api requests to one backend Service and /web requests to a different backend Service, based on URL path. Which object should they configure? ⬜ A ClusterIP Service
⬜ An Ingress resource with path-based routing rules
⬜ A headless Service
⬜ A PersistentVolumeClaim
A developer’s Pod tries to reach another Service by its short name (e.g., payments) instead of the fully qualified domain name, and it works correctly when calling from within the same namespace. What makes this possible? ⬜ Kubernetes cluster DNS automatically appends the Pod’s own namespace and cluster domain suffix through its configured search domains, resolving the short name.
⬜ Kubernetes requires the fully qualified name always; short names never work.
⬜ The Pod must have a hard-coded IP address for every Service it calls.
⬜ Short names only work if NetworkPolicy explicitly allows DNS.
A developer wants to test connectivity to a Service directly from their local machine during development, without modifying the Service type or deploying an Ingress. Which kubectl command temporarily forwards a local port to a Service or Pod? ⬜ kubectl port-forward svc/ 8080:80
⬜ kubectl expose service ⬜ kubectl cordon svc/
⬜ kubectl taint svc/
Which statement about Kubernetes NetworkPolicy behavior is correct when NO NetworkPolicy selects a given Pod? ⬜ All traffic to and from that Pod is denied by default.
⬜ All traffic to and from that Pod is allowed by default (Kubernetes networking is permissive unless a NetworkPolicy restricts it).
⬜ Only traffic from the same namespace is allowed.
⬜ Only traffic on port 80 is allowed.
A developer needs their application Pod to discover the individual Pod IPs backing a StatefulSet (for peer discovery in a clustered application) rather than a single load-balanced address. Which Service configuration is designed for this? ⬜ A LoadBalancer Service
⬜ A Headless Service (clusterIP: None)
⬜ A NodePort Service
⬜ An Ingress resource
A Service’s selector is app: cart, but no existing Pods currently carry the label app: cart. What happens to the Service’s Endpoints/EndpointSlices? ⬜ The Service automatically creates new Pods matching the selector.
⬜ The Service exists but has no active Endpoints, so it will not route traffic to any Pod until matching Pods appear.
⬜ The Service throws a validation error and cannot be created.
⬜ The Service falls back to routing traffic to any random Pod in the namespace.
Which Service type builds on NodePort and additionally provisions an external load balancer (typically from a cloud provider) to distribute traffic to the Service? ⬜ ClusterIP
⬜ NodePort
⬜ LoadBalancer
⬜ ExternalName
A developer wants an Ingress resource to route based on the incoming request’s hostname (e.g., api.example.com vs. shop.example.com) to two different backend Services. Which Ingress feature supports this? ⬜ Path-based routing only, with no support for hostnames.
⬜ Host-based (name-based virtual hosting) routing rules within the Ingress spec.
⬜ A separate LoadBalancer Service per hostname is strictly required instead.
⬜ NetworkPolicy hostname matching.
A developer’s application needs to reach a Service in a DIFFERENT namespace (billing) named invoices. Which is the correct fully qualified DNS name to use from a Pod in another namespace? ⬜ invoices.svc.cluster.local
⬜ invoices.billing.svc.cluster.local
⬜ billing.invoices.svc.cluster.local
⬜ invoices://billing
Take all 50 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:- Free Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) Online Practice Exam
Related Certification Exams Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) Exam Questions Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS) Exam Questions
