contents:
Comprehensive list of Free CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) exam questions curated for cracking the exam with confidence.
Disclaimer: CompTIA Security+ is a protected Brand. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with CompTIA. These are not the official CompTIA exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from free, official resources such as the CompTIA Security+ exam page, NIST Special Publications, and CISA guidance. These questions cover all the domains of the SY0-701 official exam and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Free Online Practice Exam Take all 74 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:-
Free CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) Online Practice Exam
Overview This is a vendor-neutral, foundational cybersecurity certification, ideal for anyone pursuing roles such as security analyst, systems administrator, or network administrator. Requires 4 to 6 weeks of preparation depending upon your familiarity with networking and security concepts. Current exam code is SY0-701 (launched November 7, 2023; scheduled retirement June 11, 2027) and costs 404 USD per attempt (varies by country/region). You need to solve a maximum of 90 questions, a mix of multiple-choice and performance-based questions (PBQs), in 90 minutes of testing time. Passing score is 750 (on a scale of 100-900). There is no penalty for guessing, so answer every question! Question format includes multiple choice and performance-based questions that test hands-on, scenario-based problem solving rather than just recall. There are no formal prerequisites, though CompTIA recommends CompTIA Network+ plus about two years of IT experience with a security focus. The certification is valid for 3 years and must be renewed through CompTIA’s Continuing Education (CE) program (earning CEUs or a higher-level certification) or by retaking the current exam. Official exam page for more details. 74 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 General Security Concepts 12% 11 2 Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations 22% 21 3 Security Architecture 18% 13 4 Security Operations 28% 18 5 Security Program Management and Oversight 20% 11 Domain 1: General Security Concepts (12%) A hospital encrypts patient records stored on its database servers so that even if an attacker steals the physical disks, the data cannot be read without the encryption key. Which principle of the CIA triad does this control primarily protect? ⬜ Availability
⬜ Confidentiality
⬜ Integrity
⬜ Non-repudiation
A company’s security policy requires that every login attempt, file access, and configuration change made by an administrator be recorded in a tamper-evident log for later review. Which element of the AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) framework does this describe? ⬜ Authentication
⬜ Authorization
⬜ Accounting
⬜ Non-repudiation
An organization redesigns its network so that no user or device, whether inside or outside the corporate network perimeter, is automatically trusted, and every access request must be continuously authenticated, authorized, and validated based on all available data points before access is granted. Which security concept does this describe? ⬜ Defense in depth
⬜ Zero Trust
⬜ Security through obscurity
⬜ Least functionality
A contract is digitally signed by a vendor using their private key. Later, the vendor denies having agreed to the contract, but the customer is able to cryptographically prove, using the vendor’s corresponding public key, that only the vendor could have created that signature. Which security concept does this scenario demonstrate? ⬜ Confidentiality
⬜ Availability
⬜ Non-repudiation
⬜ Obfuscation
A retail store posts visible warning signs stating that all areas are under 24-hour video surveillance, primarily intending to discourage would-be shoplifters from attempting theft in the first place, rather than to catch them in the act. Which category of security control does this represent? ⬜ Detective control
⬜ Deterrent control
⬜ Corrective control
⬜ Compensating control
Before any modification, such as a firewall rule change or a server patch, is applied to a production system, it must be documented, reviewed by a change advisory board, tested, and scheduled for a defined maintenance window, with a documented rollback plan in case something goes wrong. Which practice does this describe? ⬜ Change management
⬜ Vulnerability management
⬜ Onboarding
⬜ Data retention
Which of the following AAA elements is applied immediately after a user has logged into a computer with their username and password? ⬜ Authentication
⬜ Authorization
⬜ Identification
⬜ Accounting
Logging events in an audit log is what part of the access control system? ⬜ Non-repudiation
⬜ Authorization
⬜ Authentication
⬜ Accounting
What is meant by “data at rest”? ⬜ Data present in volatile memory
⬜ Data being transmitted over a network
⬜ Data being actively processed by a computer
⬜ Data stored on a persistent storage media
A systems engineer wants to control access to critical data. Which of the following describes a security concern regarding storing and transferring data without authorization? ⬜ Integrity
⬜ Social engineering
⬜ Confidentiality
⬜ Availability
Confidentiality, integrity, and availability together form the foundational triad of information security objectives. Which of the following is NOT one of these core objectives? ⬜ Confidentiality
⬜ Integrity
⬜ Disposal
⬜ Availability
Domain 2: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations (22%) A well-funded and highly organized group, believed to be sponsored by a foreign government, spends over a year quietly infiltrating a defense contractor’s network, carefully avoiding detection while exfiltrating sensitive design documents. Which type of threat actor does this best describe? ⬜ Script kiddie
⬜ Hacktivist
⬜ Advanced persistent threat (APT) / nation-state actor
⬜ Insider threat
An employee who has legitimate administrative access to the company’s payroll system uses that access to secretly modify their own salary information for personal gain. Which type of threat actor does this represent? ⬜ External attacker
⬜ Insider threat
⬜ Hacktivist
⬜ Shadow IT
An attacker calls the IT help desk pretending to be a company executive who is “locked out and about to miss an important client call,” pressuring the technician into resetting a password without proper identity verification. Which social engineering technique is being used? ⬜ Phishing
⬜ Pretexting
⬜ Tailgating
⬜ Typosquatting
A finance clerk receives an email that appears to come from the company’s CEO, instructing her to urgently wire funds to a new vendor account before the end of the day. The sender’s email address is nearly identical to the real CEO’s but slightly altered. Which type of attack is this? ⬜ Business email compromise (BEC)
⬜ Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS)
⬜ On-path (man-in-the-middle) attack
⬜ Credential stuffing
A hospital’s files suddenly become encrypted and inaccessible, and a message demands payment in cryptocurrency to restore access, threatening to permanently delete the data if payment is not made within 72 hours. Which type of malware is responsible for this attack? ⬜ Spyware
⬜ Ransomware
⬜ Adware
⬜ Logic bomb
Security analysts discover malicious code on a compromised server that has modified the operating system’s kernel-level functions to hide its own files, processes, and network connections from standard system tools and antivirus scans. Which type of malware is this? ⬜ Rootkit
⬜ Worm
⬜ Keylogger
⬜ Trojan
A piece of malware spreads automatically from one vulnerable machine to another across a corporate network without any user having to open a file or click a link, exploiting an unpatched network service. Which type of malware best fits this description? ⬜ Virus
⬜ Worm
⬜ Trojan
⬜ Fileless malware
A web application allows users to enter a username directly into a login form field, and that input is concatenated into a database query without any validation or parameterization. An attacker enters a specially crafted string into the field that manipulates the underlying database query to bypass authentication entirely. Which vulnerability is being exploited? ⬜ Cross-site scripting (XSS)
⬜ SQL injection
⬜ Buffer overflow
⬜ Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
Security researchers discover attackers actively exploiting a previously unknown flaw in a widely used piece of software, for which the vendor has not yet released a patch. Which term describes this type of vulnerability? ⬜ Zero-day vulnerability
⬜ Legacy vulnerability
⬜ Misconfiguration
⬜ Race condition
A programmer writes code that copies user-supplied input into a fixed-size memory buffer without checking the input’s length first. An attacker submits input longer than the buffer can hold, overwriting adjacent memory and potentially executing arbitrary code. Which vulnerability class does this describe? ⬜ Buffer overflow
⬜ Cross-site scripting
⬜ Directory traversal
⬜ Insecure deserialization
An organization ensures that a database administrator’s account only has the specific permissions needed to manage databases, and nothing more, with no access to unrelated systems like HR records or network device configuration. Which security principle is being applied? ⬜ Separation of duties
⬜ Least privilege
⬜ Job rotation
⬜ Mandatory vacation
A cybersecurity analyst for a medium-sized company needs to perform a vulnerability scan that provides an in-depth analysis of potential weaknesses in the company’s system, including misconfigured applications and security settings. The analyst is considering using a credentialed or non-credentialed scan.Which type of scan is most appropriate for this situation? ⬜ A credentialed scan, because it provides login rights for a more thorough analysis of potential vulnerabilities.
⬜ A non-credentialed scan, because it provides login rights for a more thorough analysis of potential vulnerabilities.
⬜ Both a credentialed and non-credentialed scan would be equally effective in this scenario.
⬜ Neither a credentialed nor a non-credentialed scan would be effective in this scenario.
Considering common threat vectors and attack surfaces, which statement best describes the primary risk, from a cybersecurity perspective, of using unsupported systems and applications? ⬜ Unsupported systems no longer receive vendor updates or patches, making their attack surfaces more susceptible to known exploits.
⬜ Unsupported systems are inherently more complex, thus presenting a larger attack surface.
⬜ Unsupported systems often operate on obsolete hardware, increasing their vulnerability to physical threat vectors.
⬜ Unsupported systems usually have outdated security measures, broadening the threat vectors.
An organization has just completed an assessment of all the points where a threat actor might exploit a vulnerability in the network. This analysis includes its computer systems, network ports, applications, and user interactions. What is the term for this collection of potential points of exploitation? ⬜ Attack surface
⬜ Attack vector
⬜ Threat landscape
⬜ Threat vector
A group of hackers, exploiting vulnerabilities in a certain organization’s online platforms and using spear-phishing techniques, launches a series of attacks disrupting the organization’s services. These attack vectors target both software flaws and human elements of the organization. Driven by disdain for the organization’s practices, their primary objective is to raise awareness and bring about changes in the organization’s conduct. Based on this information, what is the primary motivation of these threat actors? ⬜ Financial gain
⬜ Espionage
⬜ Political change
⬜ Vandalism
A network administrator conducts an analysis on the company’s network in attempts to determine attack surface, with the intent of reducing exploitable vectors. When analyzing the potential attack surface, which layer model allows unauthorized hosts to obtain a valid network address, possibly by spoofing, and communicate with hosts in other zones? ⬜ Layer 4
⬜ Layer 1
⬜ Layer 3
⬜ Layer 7
A security engineer discovered that an active employee copied sensitive information from the company’s shared drive and sold it online. What kind of actor describes this employee? ⬜ Advanced persistent threat
⬜ Nation-state
⬜ Insider threat
⬜ Hacktivist
A company identifies that an external threat actor has penetrated system protections and likely exfiltrated company information. Upon investigation, you identify that the threat actor found a way to capture a password hash while it was being transmitted during a user’s authentication. Which type of password attack does this scenario describe? ⬜ Dictionary attack
⬜ Brute force attack
⬜ On-path attack
⬜ XSS attack
A business development team reports that files are missing from the database system and the server log-in screens are showing a lock symbol that requires users to contact an email address to access the system and data. Which of the following attacks is the company facing? ⬜ Rootkit
⬜ Ransomware
⬜ Spyware
⬜ Bloatware
An organization’s systems and networks include many exploitable components and entry points. The organization faces a cybersecurity threat from a group located outside the organization that has extensive funding and highly skilled members capable of creating advanced exploit techniques, but no internal access to the organization’s systems. Based on these attributes, which of the following best describes this threat actor? ⬜ An internal threat actor with high capability and low resources
⬜ An external threat actor with low capability and high resources
⬜ An external threat actor with high capability and high resources
⬜ An internal threat actor with low capability and low resources
A systems engineer hardens an internet-facing server specifically to reduce its exposure to unsolicited port scans and service probes arriving from the public internet. Which type of threat is the engineer primarily concerned about? ⬜ An internal threat
⬜ A zero-day threat
⬜ An isolated threat
⬜ An external threat
Domain 3: Security Architecture (18%) A company places its public-facing web server in a separate network segment that is isolated from both the internet and the internal corporate network, with firewall rules strictly controlling traffic in and out of that segment. Which architecture concept is being applied? ⬜ Demilitarized zone (DMZ)
⬜ Virtual private network (VPN)
⬜ Network address translation (NAT)
⬜ Air gap
An organization implements an architecture in which every application, workload, and user is placed into small, tightly controlled network zones, and traffic between any two zones, even ones on the same physical network segment, must be explicitly authenticated and authorized rather than trusted based on which subnet it originates from. Which term best describes this approach? ⬜ Flat network design
⬜ Microsegmentation
⬜ Network address translation
⬜ Full-mesh VPN
A company migrates its application to a public cloud provider’s Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering. Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following is the CUSTOMER responsible for securing? ⬜ The physical security of the cloud provider’s datacenters
⬜ The guest operating system, applications, and data running on the virtual machines
⬜ The physical network cabling between the provider’s datacenters
⬜ The virtualization hypervisor itself
A DevOps team defines its servers, networks, and security groups in version-controlled configuration files, which are used to automatically and consistently provision identical environments every time, rather than manually configuring each server by hand. Which concept does this describe? ⬜ Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
⬜ Shadow IT
⬜ Virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI)
⬜ Bare-metal provisioning
A company’s disaster recovery plan states that after a major outage, the order-processing system must be restored within 4 hours, and the maximum acceptable data loss is 15 minutes’ worth of transactions. Which two metrics are being defined here, respectively? ⬜ Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
⬜ Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
⬜ Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) and Mean Time To Repair (MTTR)
⬜ Service Level Agreement (SLA) and Service Level Objective (SLO)
A water treatment facility uses specialized equipment to monitor and control physical processes such as valves and pumps. These systems were originally designed for isolated, air-gapped environments and often cannot be patched without risking process downtime or safety issues, unlike typical enterprise IT systems. Which category of systems does this describe? ⬜ Internet of Things (IoT) devices
⬜ Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control Systems (ICS)
⬜ Software as a Service (SaaS) applications
⬜ Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) endpoints
A retail company wants its customer service representatives to view masked credit card numbers, such as “XXXX XXXX XXXX 1234”, in the support system, without those representatives ever having access to the actual, usable card numbers, which are stored separately in a highly secured vault and referenced only by a substitute value. Which data protection technique is being used? ⬜ Hashing
⬜ Tokenization
⬜ Steganography
⬜ Data compression
An organization wants to scan its container images for known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations before they are deployed to production, and also wants to ensure the container runtime environment is isolated from the underlying host operating system as much as possible. Which security architecture concept is most relevant to this requirement? ⬜ Container security
⬜ Virtual desktop infrastructure
⬜ Full-disk encryption
⬜ Software-defined networking
An organization documents the specific steps its critical business functions, not just its IT systems, will take to continue operating, potentially through manual workarounds or an alternate site, during and immediately after a disruptive event, until normal operations can be restored. Which type of plan does this describe? ⬜ Business continuity plan (BCP)
⬜ Incident response plan
⬜ Acceptable use policy
⬜ Data retention schedule
A software engineer is formulating an architectural plan. When evaluating the use of a particular architecture and selection of controls, what is NOT an architectural consideration? ⬜ Availability
⬜ Risk transference
⬜ Costs
⬜ Port security
Which of the following mitigation techniques refers to the process of protecting all information on a hard drive, including the programs responsible for booting an operating system? ⬜ Network segmentation
⬜ Patch management
⬜ Full-disk encryption
⬜ Device isolation
Which of the following describes the placement and role of a firewall in a network with a defense-in-depth strategy? ⬜ A firewall is typically on internal routers and serves as a corrective control to mitigate denial of service (DoS) attacks.
⬜ A firewall is typically inline behind the border firewall and serves as a preventive control to enforce access rules.
⬜ A firewall is typically at the network border and serves as a preventive control to enforce access rules for ingress and egress traffic.
⬜ A firewall is typically at the network border and serves as a detective control to identify malicious traffic.
An organization wants to ensure the security of its sensitive data stored on the company’s physical drives, with varying levels of access for different users. Which of the following encryption methods would best suit this requirement? ⬜ Volume encryption only
⬜ A combination of volume and file encryption
⬜ Full disk encryption (FDE) only
⬜ Partition encryption only
Domain 4: Security Operations (28%) During enrollment for a new online banking application, a user is required to enter a password (something they know) and also insert a hardware security key into their laptop’s USB port (something they have) before being granted access. Which security concept is being applied? ⬜ Single-factor authentication
⬜ Multifactor authentication (MFA)
⬜ Federation
⬜ Role-based access control
After a critical vulnerability is publicly disclosed in a widely used web server software, an organization’s security team prioritizes testing and deploying the vendor’s released fix across all affected servers within days, following a documented process for evaluating, testing, and applying updates. Which security practice does this describe? ⬜ Patch management
⬜ Change management
⬜ Configuration management
⬜ Incident response
A network administrator disables Telnet access to all network switches and routers and requires administrators to use SSH instead for remote command-line management. What is the primary security benefit of this change? ⬜ SSH encrypts the session, including authentication credentials, while Telnet transmits everything in cleartext
⬜ SSH uses a faster transport protocol than Telnet
⬜ SSH does not require any authentication, simplifying access
⬜ Telnet only works over Wi-Fi networks, which is less secure
A systems administrator builds a new server image that has all unnecessary services, default accounts, and unused ports disabled or removed before the server is ever deployed into production. Which security practice does this represent? ⬜ Hardening
⬜ Patch management
⬜ Segmentation
⬜ Load balancing
A security team runs automated tools on a regular schedule to identify missing patches, outdated software versions, and insecure configurations across all servers on the network, generating a prioritized list of weaknesses to remediate. Which activity is being performed? ⬜ Penetration testing
⬜ Vulnerability scanning
⬜ Threat hunting
⬜ Digital forensics
A security operations center (SOC) uses a platform that aggregates log data from firewalls, servers, and endpoint agents across the enterprise, correlates events from multiple sources in near real time, and generates alerts when suspicious patterns are detected. Which type of tool is this? ⬜ Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)
⬜ Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) only
⬜ Vulnerability scanner
⬜ Configuration management database (CMDB)
After a SIEM generates an alert for a suspicious login, a connected platform automatically executes a predefined playbook: it disables the affected user account, isolates the affected endpoint from the network, and opens a ticket for analyst review, all without a human manually performing each step. Which type of technology enables this automated response? ⬜ Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR)
⬜ Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
⬜ Network Access Control (NAC)
⬜ Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
An organization requires that any use of a highly privileged domain administrator account go through a dedicated system that issues short-lived, just-in-time credentials, records a full session recording of everything the administrator does, and requires a second approver before access is granted. Which category of solution is being described? ⬜ Privileged Access Management (PAM)
⬜ Single sign-on (SSO)
⬜ Federation
⬜ Data loss prevention (DLP)
Before any security incident occurs, an organization develops and documents an incident response plan, trains its incident response team, deploys detection tools, and establishes communication procedures and contact lists to be ready to respond effectively. According to the NIST incident response lifecycle, which phase does this activity belong to? ⬜ Preparation
⬜ Detection and analysis
⬜ Containment, eradication, and recovery
⬜ Post-incident activity
During an active ransomware outbreak, the incident response team immediately disconnects the infected servers from the network and disables the compromised user accounts to stop the malware from spreading further, before beginning the process of removing the malware entirely. Which phase of incident response does this represent? ⬜ Preparation
⬜ Detection and analysis
⬜ Containment
⬜ Post-incident activity
During a forensic investigation into a data breach, an analyst carefully documents every person who handled a piece of digital evidence, such as a hard drive, when it was collected, and how it was stored and transferred, to ensure the evidence remains admissible and its integrity can be verified later. Which forensic concept does this describe? ⬜ Chain of custody
⬜ Data carving
⬜ Order of volatility
⬜ Legal hold
An organization maintains a continuously updated inventory of every server, laptop, and network device it owns, including its owner, location, software installed, and criticality to the business, so that security teams know exactly what needs to be protected and patched. Which foundational security operations practice does this represent? ⬜ Asset management
⬜ Change management
⬜ Threat modeling
⬜ Business impact analysis
Before decommissioned hard drives are removed from a secure facility for disposal, an organization uses a specialized process to overwrite or physically destroy the drives so that no residual data can be recovered by whoever receives the old hardware. Which practice does this describe? ⬜ Media sanitization
⬜ Data classification
⬜ Legal hold
⬜ Tokenization
After noticing unusual outbound traffic patterns, a security analyst proactively searches through endpoint and network logs for subtle indicators of compromise that automated detection tools may have missed, forming and testing hypotheses about how an attacker might have gained a foothold. Which activity does this describe? ⬜ Threat hunting
⬜ Vulnerability scanning
⬜ Business continuity planning
⬜ Change management
The company’s system has recently detected suspicious network activity, signaling a possible cybersecurity incident. The incident response team has assembled, and after going through the detection and analysis phases, the containment phase of the incident response process has started. In this phase, what is the primary objective? ⬜ Continuing the discovery of indicators of the threat actor activity
⬜ Removing the source of the threat and restoring the affected systems to a secure state
⬜ Limiting the scope and magnitude of the incident
⬜ Analyzing the incident and responses to identify whether procedures or systems could be improved
An organization’s automated scanner has just flagged a vulnerability with the identifier CVE-2023-0150. What are some initial steps the organization should take to understand and potentially address this vulnerability? ⬜ Look up the identifier in the vulnerability database and assess the vulnerability.
⬜ Modify the scanner settings to avoid detecting similar vulnerabilities in the future.
⬜ Consult the scanner’s manufacturer for advice on the vulnerability.
⬜ Ignore the identifier since it might not be significant.
At a healthcare technology company, a cybersecurity alert flagged an unusual pattern of data traffic from one of its key database servers. Initial analysis indicates a potential data breach that is not yet conclusively confirmed. The server contains sensitive patient data. If confirmed, it could have severe legal and reputational implications for the company. What steps should the incident response team take to better understand the situation? ⬜ Focus on other network abnormalities and wait for additional alerts before conducting a detailed analysis
⬜ Immediately shut down the server to prevent further data leaks
⬜ Announce the potential data breach to all stakeholders and the public to maintain transparency
⬜ Conduct a detailed analysis of the alert using threat intelligence and incident response playbooks
A member of the security operations team discovers a lost work phone while performing a scheduled control review. Based on verified need, evidence, and approved procedure, what is the most appropriate next action? ⬜ Continue business activities on a personal device until the phone is recovered
⬜ Attempt to locate the phone before notifying the support team
⬜ Use an alternative communication method and wait to see whether the device reconnects
⬜ Report the loss immediately and initiate approved device-protection and containment measures
Domain 5: Security Program Management and Oversight (20%) A security team implements automated tools and processes to continuously collect security-related metrics, assess the security posture of systems against a defined baseline, and report deviations to stakeholders on an ongoing basis, rather than relying only on periodic annual assessments. Which security operations practice does this describe? ⬜ Continuous monitoring
⬜ Annual penetration testing
⬜ Static code analysis
⬜ Disaster recovery testing
A risk management team documents each identified risk to the organization, along with its likelihood, potential impact, assigned owner, and current treatment status, in a centralized tracking document that is reviewed and updated regularly. Which risk management tool is being described? ⬜ Risk register
⬜ Business impact analysis
⬜ Data classification policy
⬜ Acceptable use policy
A risk analysis determines that a particular server has a single loss expectancy (SLE) of $50,000 for a specific threat, and that threat is expected to occur twice per year on average (an annualized rate of occurrence, or ARO, of 2). What is the Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) for this risk? ⬜ $25,000
⬜ $50,000
⬜ $100,000
⬜ $200,000
Before signing a contract with a new cloud service provider that will process sensitive customer data, an organization requires the vendor to complete a detailed security questionnaire, provide a recent independent audit report, and agree to specific contractual security obligations. Which practice does this represent? ⬜ Third-party (vendor) risk management
⬜ Change management
⬜ Job rotation
⬜ Continuous monitoring
A healthcare organization ensures that any system storing or transmitting patient health information implements specific administrative, physical, and technical safeguards required by federal law, and undergoes regular audits to demonstrate adherence to these mandatory requirements. Which term describes the organization’s obligation to meet these externally imposed legal requirements? ⬜ Compliance
⬜ Risk appetite
⬜ Due care
⬜ Vulnerability management
An organization requires every employee to complete annual training that teaches them how to recognize phishing emails, use strong passwords, and report suspicious activity, reinforced with periodic simulated phishing tests throughout the year. Which security program element does this represent? ⬜ Security awareness training
⬜ Penetration testing
⬜ Incident response
⬜ Business continuity planning
A company’s information security governance documents include a high-level, mandatory statement approved by executive leadership about protecting customer data, and a detailed, mandatory technical document specifying that all passwords must be at least 12 characters, and a voluntary, recommended document suggesting best practices for securing a home office. Which three types of governance documents does this describe, respectively? ⬜ Policy, standard, and guideline
⬜ Standard, guideline, and policy
⬜ Procedure, policy, and standard
⬜ Guideline, policy, and standard
An organization hires an independent third party to formally evaluate whether its security controls are designed and operating effectively against a recognized framework, producing a formal report with findings and an opinion that can be shared with customers and regulators. Which activity does this describe? ⬜ Security audit
⬜ Threat modeling
⬜ Vulnerability scanning
⬜ Tabletop exercise
An organization designates a specific senior business leader as being formally accountable for the accuracy, classification, and appropriate use of a particular dataset, such as customer records, even though a separate technical team handles day-to-day storage and backups of that data. Which role does this leader hold? ⬜ Data owner
⬜ Data custodian
⬜ Data processor
⬜ System administrator
A company that collects personal information from its customers publishes a document explaining what personal data it collects, why it is collected, how it is used and shared, and how individuals can exercise rights such as requesting deletion of their data. Which concept is this document primarily addressing? ⬜ Privacy notice / privacy considerations
⬜ Disaster recovery plan
⬜ Vulnerability disclosure policy
⬜ Network diagram
A software development company recognizes that some of its employees are vulnerable to phishing attacks. To address this, the company plans to set up a training program. What factors should the company primarily consider while defining such training programs? ⬜ The roles performed by the employees
⬜ The length of service of the employees
⬜ The job titles of the employees
⬜ The personal interests of the employees
Take all 74 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:- Free CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) Online Practice Exam
title: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) Exam Questions

contents:
Comprehensive list of Free Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) exam questions, grouped by official exam domain, curated for cracking the exam with confidence.
Disclaimer: Microsoft Azure is a protected Brand. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with Microsoft. These are not the official Microsoft exam questions/dumps. These questions are created from the web resources of Microsoft Learn. These questions cover all the objectives and services of the AZ-900 official exam and once you go through these questions and their concepts, you are more than ready to crack the exam in first attempt.
Online Practice Exams Take all 59 questions as timed online practice exams in the real exam format:-
Free Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) Online Practice Exam
Overview This is a Fundamentals level certification, ideal for anyone who wants a broad understanding of cloud and Azure concepts, regardless of technical background. Requires 2 to 4 weeks of preparation depending upon your familiarity with cloud concepts. Exam code is AZ-900 and costs 99 USD per attempt (varies by country/region). You need to solve 40 to 60 questions in ~45 minutes of testing time (about 65 minutes total including sign-in and surveys). Passing score is 700 (out of 1000). No negative scoring so answer all the questions! Question format includes multiple choice, multiple response, drag-and-drop, and case study style questions. There are no formal prerequisites, though basic familiarity with IT concepts and the cloud is recommended. This is a Fundamentals-level Microsoft certification, so unlike role-based certifications it does not expire. Study Guide for more details. 59 Practice Questions # Domain Weight Questions below 1 Describe Cloud Concepts 28% 16 2 Describe Azure Architecture and Services 40% 24 3 Describe Azure Management and Governance 32% 19 Domain 1: Describe Cloud Concepts (28%) A company wants to move its IT operations away from purchasing and maintaining physical servers, and instead pay only for the compute, storage, and networking it actually consumes, billed monthly. Which cloud computing characteristic does this describe? ⬜ Consumption-based (pay-as-you-go) model
⬜ Economies of scale
⬜ High availability
⬜ Fault tolerance
An organization keeps sensitive financial systems on infrastructure it owns and operates in its own datacenter, while running its public-facing marketing website on Azure. Which cloud deployment model best describes this organization’s overall strategy? ⬜ Public cloud
⬜ Private cloud
⬜ Hybrid cloud
⬜ Community cloud
A development team rents virtual machines, virtual networks, and storage from Azure, and is fully responsible for installing, configuring, and patching the operating system and any software that runs on those VMs. Which cloud service category is this? ⬜ Software as a Service (SaaS)
⬜ Platform as a Service (PaaS)
⬜ Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
⬜ Function as a Service (FaaS)
A retail company deploys a web application on Azure App Service, where Microsoft manages the underlying servers, operating system patching, and runtime, while the company’s developers focus only on writing and deploying their application code. Which cloud service category does Azure App Service represent? ⬜ Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
⬜ Platform as a Service (PaaS)
⬜ Software as a Service (SaaS)
⬜ On-premises
An organization uses Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Outlook) for its employees’ daily productivity needs. The organization does not manage any servers, operating systems, or application code for this software — it simply uses it through a web browser or app and pays a monthly subscription per user. Which cloud service category is Microsoft 365? ⬜ Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
⬜ Platform as a Service (PaaS)
⬜ Software as a Service (SaaS)
⬜ Desktop as a Service (DaaS)
During a regional Azure datacenter outage, an application that was deployed across multiple Availability Zones in the region continued serving user requests with minimal disruption. Which cloud computing benefit does this best illustrate? ⬜ Elasticity
⬜ High availability
⬜ Agility
⬜ Economies of scale
An e-commerce website automatically adds additional web server instances during a flash sale when traffic spikes, and automatically removes those instances once traffic returns to normal, without any manual intervention. Which cloud computing benefit does this describe? ⬜ Elasticity
⬜ Fault tolerance
⬜ Agility
⬜ Reliability
A startup needs to launch a new product feature quickly and provisions the required virtual machines, databases, and networking in Azure within minutes through the Azure portal, instead of waiting weeks to order and rack physical hardware. Which cloud computing benefit does this scenario best illustrate? ⬜ Agility
⬜ Fault tolerance
⬜ Economies of scale
⬜ Elasticity
A mission-critical application is designed so that if one of its underlying virtual machines crashes, another instance automatically takes over the workload with no impact on end users. Which term best describes this design characteristic? ⬜ Fault tolerance
⬜ Disaster recovery
⬜ Scalability
⬜ Consumption-based pricing
After a severe flood destroys a company’s on-premises datacenter, the company is able to restore its critical applications and data from Azure backups in a different region within a few hours, following a documented recovery plan. Which term describes this capability? ⬜ Disaster recovery
⬜ Fault tolerance
⬜ Vertical scaling
⬜ Elasticity
A company’s finance team is evaluating whether to buy and depreciate its own servers over several years (a large upfront investment) versus paying a monthly Azure subscription fee that can be adjusted based on usage. What are these two spending models called, respectively? ⬜ Capital Expenditure (CapEx) and Operational Expenditure (OpEx)
⬜ Operational Expenditure (OpEx) and Capital Expenditure (CapEx)
⬜ Elastic spending and fixed spending
⬜ Consumption spending and reservation spending
Because Microsoft operates Azure datacenters at a massive global scale and can negotiate better prices on hardware, electricity, and networking than any single company could on its own, it can offer compute and storage services to customers at a lower cost than most customers could achieve running their own datacenter. Which cloud concept does this describe? ⬜ Economies of scale
⬜ High availability
⬜ Serverless computing
⬜ Shared responsibility
When a company runs virtual machines in Azure (Infrastructure as a Service), which of the following is Microsoft responsible for, and which is the customer responsible for, under the shared responsibility model? ⬜ Microsoft is responsible for physical datacenter security and the underlying host infrastructure; the customer is responsible for the guest operating system, applications, and data on the VM
⬜ Microsoft is responsible for everything, including the customer’s application code and data
⬜ The customer is responsible for physical datacenter security; Microsoft is responsible for the guest operating system
⬜ Responsibility is split 50/50 regardless of the service model chosen
A company wants to avoid being locked into a single vendor and decides to run some workloads on Azure and others on a different public cloud provider, integrating them as needed. Which cloud strategy does this describe? ⬜ Multi-cloud
⬜ Hybrid cloud
⬜ Private cloud
⬜ Community cloud
What is one of the platform requirements to confirm when considering cloud service providers? ⬜ Marketing strategies
⬜ Employee training programs
⬜ Virtual machine (VM) compute resources
⬜ User interface design
What is characterized as the ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function? ⬜ Reliability
⬜ Predictability
⬜ Scalability
⬜ Elasticity
Domain 2: Describe Azure Architecture and Services (40%) A company wants to deploy resources close to its customers in Southeast Asia to reduce network latency. In Azure terminology, what is the term for a set of datacenters deployed within a defined perimeter and connected through a dedicated regional low-latency network, such as “Southeast Asia”? ⬜ Availability Zone
⬜ Region
⬜ Resource group
⬜ Management group
To meet disaster recovery requirements, an organization wants to replicate its data to another Azure region that is specifically matched with its primary region and is unlikely to be updated at the same time during Azure platform updates. What is this matched region called? ⬜ A sovereign region
⬜ A region pair
⬜ An Availability Zone
⬜ A resource group
An architect wants to protect an application from a datacenter-level failure (such as loss of power or cooling in one building) while keeping the resources within the same Azure region for low-latency replication. Which Azure feature should be used to distribute the application’s VMs across physically separate datacenters with independent power, cooling, and networking, all within one region? ⬜ Region pairs
⬜ Availability Zones
⬜ Resource groups
⬜ Azure Migrate
A cloud administrator wants to group a virtual machine, its associated virtual network, and its storage account together so they can be managed, monitored, and deleted as a single unit, since they all belong to the same application. Which Azure construct should be used? ⬜ Subscription
⬜ Management group
⬜ Resource group
⬜ Region
A large enterprise has separate Azure subscriptions for its Finance, HR, and Engineering departments, and wants to apply a single set of compliance policies and access controls across all three subscriptions at once, without configuring each subscription individually. Which Azure resource organization feature enables this? ⬜ Resource groups
⬜ Management groups
⬜ Availability sets
⬜ Region pairs
Which Azure service acts as the deployment and management layer for Azure, processing every request made through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, or REST API, and providing a consistent way to organize, secure, and manage resources through consistent role-based access control and tagging? ⬜ Azure Resource Manager (ARM)
⬜ Azure Monitor
⬜ Azure Advisor
⬜ Azure Policy
A gaming company runs a fleet of identical virtual machines behind a load balancer to handle a game’s backend workload, and wants the number of VM instances to automatically increase during peak play hours and decrease overnight, based on CPU utilization. Which Azure compute service is purpose-built for this scenario? ⬜ Availability sets
⬜ Virtual Machine Scale Sets
⬜ Azure Container Instances
⬜ Resource groups
An administrator configures a group of VMs to be spread across multiple fault domains (separate physical racks, power, and network) and update domains (groups that are rebooted separately during planned maintenance) within a single datacenter, to increase availability against localized hardware failure and maintenance events. What is this Azure feature called? ⬜ Availability Zone
⬜ Availability set
⬜ Region pair
⬜ Scale set
A team wants to deploy a web application without provisioning or managing any virtual machines, and wants Azure to automatically handle OS patching, scaling, and load balancing for the web tier. Which Azure service is the best fit? ⬜ Azure App Service
⬜ Azure Virtual Machines
⬜ Azure Virtual Desktop
⬜ Azure ExpressRoute
A developer needs to run a single containerized batch job for a short burst of time without provisioning a virtual machine or setting up a container orchestrator like Kubernetes. Which Azure service is designed for quickly running a single container with minimal management overhead? ⬜ Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
⬜ Azure Container Instances (ACI)
⬜ Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
⬜ Azure Functions
An organization wants to orchestrate dozens of containerized microservices, automatically handling scaling, self-healing, rolling updates, and load balancing across a cluster of nodes. Which Azure service should they use? ⬜ Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
⬜ Azure Container Instances
⬜ Azure App Service
⬜ Azure Functions
A developer wants to run a small piece of code that automatically triggers whenever a new file is uploaded to Azure Blob Storage, without provisioning any servers, and wants to pay only for the compute time consumed while the code executes. Which Azure service fits this requirement? ⬜ Azure Functions
⬜ Azure Virtual Machines
⬜ Azure Kubernetes Service
⬜ Azure Virtual Desktop
A company wants its remote employees to securely access a full Windows desktop environment and their corporate applications from any device, with the desktop session actually running in Azure rather than on the employee’s local machine. Which Azure service is designed for this? ⬜ Azure Virtual Desktop
⬜ Azure App Service
⬜ Azure Container Instances
⬜ Azure Functions
An architect is designing a network in Azure and needs private IP address spaces so that virtual machines and other resources can communicate securely with each other, the internet, and on-premises networks. Which Azure resource provides this fundamental building block for private networking? ⬜ Azure Virtual Network (VNet)
⬜ Azure DNS
⬜ Azure Load Balancer
⬜ Azure ExpressRoute
A bank needs to connect its on-premises datacenter to Azure over a dedicated, private, high-bandwidth connection that does not travel over the public internet at all, for both performance and compliance reasons. Which Azure networking service should it use? ⬜ Site-to-site VPN Gateway
⬜ Azure ExpressRoute
⬜ Azure DNS
⬜ Azure Load Balancer
A company needs to establish an encrypted connection between its on-premises network and its Azure Virtual Network over the public internet, as a lower-cost alternative to a dedicated private circuit. Which Azure service is designed for this? ⬜ VPN Gateway
⬜ Azure ExpressRoute
⬜ Azure Bastion
⬜ Azure Front Door
An application receives a large volume of incoming traffic, and the company wants to distribute that traffic evenly across several virtual machines to improve responsiveness and avoid overloading any single VM. Which Azure networking service should be used? ⬜ Azure Load Balancer
⬜ Azure DNS
⬜ Azure Virtual Network
⬜ Azure ExpressRoute
A company wants to store business-critical data so that it survives not just a hardware failure but even the loss of an entire Azure region, by maintaining copies of the data in a secondary, geographically distant Azure region. ⬜ Azure Resource Manager

What service helps you manage your Azure, on-premises, and multicloud environments? ⬜ Azure Arc

Domain 3: Describe Azure Management and Governance (32%) Before deploying any resources, an organization wants to estimate the monthly cost of a planned Azure architecture (specific VM sizes, storage accounts, and databases) so it can budget accurately. ⬜ Management groups
⬜ Availability sets
A company runs a steady, predictable workload on a set of virtual machines 24/7 for the next three years and wants to significantly reduce its compute costs compared to paying the standard pay-as-you-go rate, in exchange for committing to that usage upfront. ⬜ Free tier pricing
A data analytics team has a large, interruptible batch-processing job that can tolerate being stopped and restarted, and wants to run it as cheaply as possible by taking advantage of Azure’s spare, unused compute capacity. ⬜ Azure Advisor
⬜ Resource locks
An administrator wants to prevent a critical production database resource from being accidentally deleted by any team member, while still allowing normal read and write operations against the database to continue. Which Azure governance feature should be applied to the resource? ⬜ A CanNotDelete resource lock

⬜ Azure Advisor

A DevOps engineer wants to automate repetitive Azure resource management tasks using scripts, and wants a browser-based, pre-authenticated command-line environment (supporting both Bash and PowerShell) accessible directly from the Azure portal without installing anything locally. Which Azure tool fits this need? ⬜ Azure Cloud Shell

Comprehensive list of Free Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I) practice exam questions curated for cracking the Scrum.org PSM I assessment with confidence.
Disclaimer: Scrum.org and the Scrum Guide are protected brands/works. These exam questions are neither endorsed by nor affiliated with Scrum.org, Ken Schwaber, or Jeff Sutherland. These are not the official Scrum.org exam questions/dumps. Every question below is created strictly from the free, official Scrum Guide (the current November 2020 version) and official Scrum.org resources, never from unauthorized dump sites. Scrum.org’s own free Scrum Open practice assessment is another great official self-check resource to try before your real attempt. Once you understand the concepts behind these questions, you are more than ready to crack the real PSM I assessment on your first attempt.
Free Online Practice Exam Take all 50 questions as a timed online practice exam, free:-
Free Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I) Online Practice Exam
Overview PSM I validates that you understand Scrum as described in the Scrum Guide and how to apply it in Scrum Teams — the exam tests precise adherence to the Guide’s exact wording, not “common practice” folklore. The exam consists of 80 questions in Multiple Choice, Multiple Answer, and True/False format. You have 60 minutes to complete the assessment, and a passing score of 85% is required. The exam costs $200 USD per attempt; test passwords have no expiration date but are valid for one attempt only. PSM I certification never expires — it is a lifetime certification with no annual renewal fee, and it includes a free Credly digital credential. There are no mandatory prerequisites and no required course attendance, though Scrum.org recommends attending a Professional Scrum Master or Applying Professional Scrum course. The authoritative content source for every question below is the Scrum Guide, current November 2020 version, authored by Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland — there is no newer official revision as of this writing. Scrum.org does not publish official domain-weight percentages for PSM I (unlike some vendor-specific exams); instead, PSM I questions are drawn from three Focus Areas defined in the Professional Scrum Competencies: Understanding and Applying the Scrum Framework, Developing People and Teams, and Managing Products with Agility. This guide instead organizes its 50 practice questions around the Scrum Guide’s own structure, since that document is the actual source of truth the exam draws from. Scrum.org’s own free Scrum Open assessment is an excellent official self-check tool to try before attempting the real exam. Official PSM I certification page for more details. Topic Areas Scrum.org does not publish official percentage weights for PSM I. The breakdown below instead follows the Scrum Guide’s own major content sections, weighted by how much text and emphasis the Guide gives each area and how it maps to Scrum.org’s own Focus Areas. Scrum Events and Scrum Team accountabilities receive the most questions since they are both the most detailed sections of the Guide and the areas most consistently emphasized in real PSM I attempts.
# Topic Area (Scrum Guide Section) Approx. Questions 1 Scrum Theory and Values 8 2 The Scrum Team 11 3 Scrum Events 12 4 Scrum Artifacts and Commitments 10 5 Scrum Master Accountabilities & Servant-Leadership 9 Practice Questions According to the Scrum Guide, Scrum is founded on which two foundations? ⬜ Empiricism and lean thinking
⬜ Waterfall and empiricism
⬜ Predictive planning and lean thinking
⬜ Agile principles and iterative planning
Scrum combines four formal events for inspection and adaptation within a containing event. What is that containing event called? ⬜ The Sprint
⬜ The Daily Scrum
⬜ The Release
⬜ The Program Increment
The Scrum Guide names three pillars that uphold every implementation of empirical process control: transparency, inspection, and adaptation. Which TWO of the following statements about these pillars are accurate? ⬜ Inspection enables adaptation; inspection without adaptation is considered pointless.
⬜ Adaptation enables transparency; without adaptation, transparency is impossible.
⬜ Transparency enables inspection; inspection without transparency is misleading and wasteful.
⬜ Adaptation becomes easier when the people involved are not empowered or self-managing.
Per the Scrum Guide, what happens to inspection when it is not followed by adaptation? ⬜ It becomes more valuable
⬜ It is considered pointless
⬜ It automatically triggers a Sprint cancellation
⬜ It replaces the need for transparency
How many values does the Scrum Guide define, and what is their stated purpose? ⬜ Three values; they define the Scrum Team’s roles
⬜ Four values; they define the length of each timebox
⬜ Five values; they give direction to the Scrum Team with regard to their work, actions, and behavior
⬜ Five values; they replace the need for Scrum events
Which TWO of the following are among the five Scrum values named in the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Discipline
⬜ Courage
⬜ Predictability
⬜ Respect
According to the Scrum Guide, what is expected of a Scrum Team the moment it learns something new through inspection? ⬜ It should wait until the next Sprint Retrospective to act
⬜ It is expected to adapt immediately
⬜ It should escalate the change to the Product Owner for approval before adapting
⬜ It should document the learning for the next release cycle
True or False: According to the Scrum Guide, artifacts with low transparency can lead to decisions that diminish value and increase risk. ⬜ True
⬜ False
Which of the following correctly describes the composition of a Scrum Team as defined in the Scrum Guide? ⬜ One Scrum Master, one Product Owner, and Developers, with no sub-teams or hierarchies
⬜ A Product Owner, a Project Manager, and a Development Team led by a Team Lead
⬜ Multiple Scrum Masters overseeing several development sub-teams
⬜ A Product Owner and Developers only; the Scrum Master is optional
What team size does the Scrum Guide suggest a Scrum Team should be to remain nimble yet still complete significant work within a Sprint? ⬜ Exactly 5 people
⬜ Typically 10 or fewer people
⬜ Between 15 and 20 people
⬜ No size guidance is given
Which TWO characteristics does the current Scrum Guide use to describe Scrum Teams? ⬜ Cross-functional
⬜ Self-organizing
⬜ Self-managing
⬜ Hierarchical
Who is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ The Product Owner alone
⬜ The Developers alone
⬜ The entire Scrum Team
⬜ The Scrum Master, since they own the Definition of Done
Which TWO of the following are accountabilities of the Developers, as defined in the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Creating the Sprint Backlog, the plan for the Sprint
⬜ Ordering the Product Backlog
⬜ Instilling quality by adhering to a Definition of Done
⬜ Setting the price of the certification exam
According to the Scrum Guide, what is the Product Owner primarily accountable for? ⬜ Assigning daily tasks to the Developers
⬜ Maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team
⬜ Facilitating the Daily Scrum
⬜ Removing impediments faced by the Developers
Per the Scrum Guide, can a Product Owner delegate Product Backlog management work to others? ⬜ No, the Product Owner must personally perform every Product Backlog management activity
⬜ Yes, but the Product Owner remains accountable
⬜ Yes, and accountability transfers to whoever performs the delegated work
⬜ No, delegation would violate the self-managing nature of the Scrum Team
According to the Scrum Guide, how should stakeholders who want to change the Product Backlog proceed? ⬜ By submitting a formal change request to the Scrum Master
⬜ By trying to convince the Product Owner
⬜ By voting with the Developers during Sprint Planning
⬜ By directly editing the Product Backlog themselves
What is the Scrum Master accountable for, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Establishing Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide, and the Scrum Team’s effectiveness
⬜ Writing the Product Backlog items
⬜ Approving the Increment before it can be released
⬜ Managing the organization’s budget for the product
If a Scrum Team becomes too large to remain nimble, what does the Scrum Guide suggest? ⬜ Appoint a second Scrum Master to manage the extra members
⬜ Split into multiple sub-teams under one Scrum Master
⬜ Consider reorganizing into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams, each focused on the same product and sharing the same Product Goal, Product Backlog, and Product Owner
⬜ Increase the Sprint length to accommodate more people
True or False: According to the Scrum Guide, a Scrum Team may have multiple Product Owners representing different stakeholder groups. ⬜ True
⬜ False
According to the Scrum Guide, what is the maximum length of a Sprint? ⬜ Two weeks
⬜ One month or less
⬜ Six weeks
⬜ There is no maximum; it depends on the Product Owner
Who has the authority to cancel a Sprint, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ The Scrum Master
⬜ The Developers, by majority vote
⬜ Only the Product Owner
⬜ Any stakeholder, if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete
Which TWO of the following does the Scrum Guide state must hold true during a Sprint? ⬜ No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal
⬜ The scope of the Sprint Backlog is completely fixed and can never be renegotiated
⬜ Quality does not decrease
⬜ The Product Backlog may not be touched until the Sprint ends
What is the maximum timebox for Sprint Planning in a one-month Sprint, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Four hours
⬜ Eight hours
⬜ Two hours
⬜ There is no timebox for Sprint Planning
The Scrum Guide describes Sprint Planning as addressing three topics. Which of the following correctly reflects them? ⬜ Why is this Sprint valuable? What can be Done this Sprint? How will the chosen work get done?
⬜ Who will do the work? What is the budget? When is the deadline?
⬜ What went wrong last Sprint? What should we improve? Who is responsible?
⬜ What is the Definition of Done? Who are the stakeholders? What is the Sprint length?
Per the Scrum Guide, who decides how the selected Product Backlog items will be turned into an Increment during Sprint Planning? ⬜ The Product Owner, since they know the business priorities
⬜ The Scrum Master, who plans the technical approach
⬜ The Developers, at their sole discretion
⬜ A separate architecture review board
What is the timebox for the Daily Scrum, and who is it for, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ 30 minutes, for the entire Scrum Team including stakeholders
⬜ 15 minutes, for the Developers
⬜ 15 minutes, for the Scrum Master to report to management
⬜ One hour, for the Product Owner to review priorities
If the Product Owner or Scrum Master are actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog, how do they participate in the Daily Scrum, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ They observe silently without participating
⬜ They participate as Developers
⬜ They lead the Daily Scrum instead of the Developers
⬜ They are excluded from the Daily Scrum entirely
What is the primary purpose of the Sprint Review, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ To assign story points for the next Sprint
⬜ To inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations
⬜ To conduct a formal performance review of the Developers
⬜ To finalize the Definition of Done for the first time
What is the maximum timebox for the Sprint Review in a one-month Sprint, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Three hours
⬜ Four hours
⬜ Eight hours
⬜ There is no maximum
According to the Scrum Guide, which event concludes the Sprint and is timeboxed to a maximum of three hours for a one-month Sprint? ⬜ Sprint Planning
⬜ Daily Scrum
⬜ Sprint Review
⬜ Sprint Retrospective
True or False: According to the Scrum Guide, the Sprint Review should be limited to a presentation of the completed work. ⬜ True
⬜ False
Which commitment is associated with the Product Backlog, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ The Sprint Goal
⬜ The Definition of Done
⬜ The Product Goal
⬜ The Increment forecast
Which TWO of the following artifact-commitment pairs are accurate according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal
⬜ Increment → Definition of Done
⬜ Product Backlog → Sprint Goal
⬜ Increment → Product Goal
How does the Scrum Guide define the Product Backlog? ⬜ A fixed, unchanging list of all future work
⬜ An emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product
⬜ A list maintained exclusively by the Developers
⬜ A record of completed Sprint Retrospective action items
According to the Scrum Guide, what is Product Backlog refinement? ⬜ A formally timeboxed Scrum event held once per Sprint
⬜ The act of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items into smaller, more precise items
⬜ A ceremony required to occupy exactly 10% of team capacity
⬜ The Scrum Master’s task of reordering the backlog
Who is responsible for sizing Product Backlog items, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ The Product Owner alone
⬜ The Scrum Master
⬜ The Developers who will be doing the work
⬜ An external estimation committee
What does the Product Goal describe, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ A single Sprint’s deliverable
⬜ A future state of the product that serves as a target for the Scrum Team to plan against
⬜ The exact release date of the next version
⬜ A specific technical architecture decision
The Scrum Guide states the Sprint Backlog is composed of which three elements? ⬜ The Sprint Goal (why), the selected Product Backlog items (what), and a plan for delivering the Increment (how)
⬜ A burndown chart, a velocity report, and a risk register
⬜ The Definition of Done, a stakeholder list, and a budget
⬜ The Product Goal, the Sprint Review agenda, and a retrospective summary
True or False: According to the Scrum Guide, an Increment may be delivered to stakeholders before the end of the Sprint. ⬜ True
⬜ False
If multiple Scrum Teams are working together on one product, what does the Scrum Guide require regarding the Definition of Done? ⬜ Each team may use a completely different Definition of Done
⬜ They must mutually define and comply with the same Definition of Done
⬜ Only the Scrum Master of the lead team defines it for everyone
⬜ The Definition of Done does not apply when multiple teams are involved
According to the Scrum Guide, when is a Product Backlog item considered part of an Increment? ⬜ As soon as a Developer marks it complete in a tracking tool
⬜ Only after the Sprint Review presentation
⬜ The moment it meets the Definition of Done
⬜ When the Product Owner personally tests it
Which TWO of the following are ways the Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team’s progress
⬜ Deciding which Product Backlog items the Developers must select for the Sprint
⬜ Coaching the team members in self-management and cross-functionality
⬜ Approving the Increment for release
Which of the following correctly describes a way the Scrum Master serves the Product Owner, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Writing the Product Backlog items on the Product Owner’s behalf
⬜ Facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed
⬜ Setting the Product Goal independently of the Product Owner
⬜ Making the final call on Product Backlog ordering
Which of the following correctly describes a way the Scrum Master serves the organization, per the Scrum Guide? ⬜ Managing the organization’s hiring decisions
⬜ Leading, training, and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption
⬜ Setting the organization’s overall product strategy
⬜ Approving the organization’s annual budget
Who is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness, according to the Scrum Guide? ⬜ The Product Owner
⬜ The Developers collectively, with no single accountable role
⬜ The Scrum Master
⬜ An external Agile coach
True or False: According to the Scrum Guide, the Scrum Master assigns daily tasks to the Developers. ⬜ True
⬜ False
How does the Scrum Guide characterize Scrum Masters? ⬜ As project managers accountable for on-time delivery
⬜ As true leaders who serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization
⬜ As administrative assistants who schedule meetings
⬜ As quality assurance testers for the Increment
Who, per the Scrum Guide, ensures that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox? ⬜ The Product Owner
⬜ The Developers
⬜ The Scrum Master
⬜ The most senior Developer
A Scrum Team’s stakeholders keep approaching Developers directly mid-Sprint, disrupting their focus and bypassing the Product Owner. According to the Scrum Guide, whose accountability is it to address this organizational barrier? ⬜ The Product Owner’s, since stakeholders are their responsibility
⬜ The Scrum Master’s, by removing barriers between stakeholders and the Scrum Team
⬜ The Developers’, by refusing to speak with any stakeholder
⬜ No one’s; the Scrum Guide does not address organizational barriers
Which of the following best matches the Scrum Guide’s description of how the Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team with quality? ⬜ By personally writing the Definition of Done for the team
⬜ By helping the Scrum Team focus on creating high-value Increments that meet the Definition of Done
⬜ By testing every Increment before the Sprint Review
⬜ By lowering the Definition of Done when deadlines are tight

Free Professional Scrum Product Owner I (PSPO I) Online Practice Exam
Overview PSPO I validates a fundamental understanding of the Scrum framework and the minimum knowledge needed to fulfill the Product Owner accountabilities — maximizing product value, managing the Product Backlog, and engaging stakeholders. Cost is $200 USD per attempt (additional taxes may apply, calculated at checkout). You need to answer 80 questions in a 60-minute time limit. Passing score is 85%. Professional Scrum Product Owner I Certification for more details.
