143 Practice Questions Topic 1: SAFe Lean-Agile in government *What does it mean to “think in terms of value streams” when adopting a Lean-Agile mindset? ⬜ Prioritize individual tasks over broader objectives
⬜ Focus on optimizing individual team performance
⬜ Identify and prioritize the end-to-end delivery of value to the customer
⬜ Centralize decision-making authority
*What is the primary benefit of embracing a Lean-Agile mindset in an organization? ⬜ Improved collaboration and innovation
⬜ Slower decision-making
⬜ Increased bureaucracy
⬜ Reduced transparency
*Which statement is true about Lean-Agile development and contracting? ⬜ Quality is built-in through collaboration and automation
⬜ They are based on a foundation of compliance
⬜ Lean-Agile development contracts eliminate change orders
⬜ Lean-Agile development cannot be acquired with a fixed price contract
*Which Lean concept emphasizes eliminating waste and delivering value efficiently? ⬜ Kaizen
⬜ Scrum
⬜ Kanban
⬜ Waterfall
*Which key principle of Advanced Lean-Agile in government emphasizes decentralized decision-making and empowering frontline workers? ⬜ Decentralize control
⬜ Optimize for cost
⬜ Centralize authority
⬜ Minimize transparency
What is the primary purpose of adopting a Lean-Agile mindset in government organizations?​ ⬜ To ensure strict adherence to predefined processes
⬜ To promote flexibility, collaboration, and rapid delivery of value
⬜ To centralize decision-making authority
⬜ To maintain traditional hierarchical structures​
A federal program has started adopting Agile ceremonies like daily stand-ups and using a team backlog, yet they aren’t seeing improvements in delivery speed or quality. According to SAFe for Government guidance, what is the most likely reason the agency isn’t achieving true agility? ⬜ They need to hold longer stand-up meetings and add more status reports.
⬜ Rigid government regulations make improvement impossible, regardless of Agile adoption.
⬜ They have only copied Agile rituals without embracing Lean-Agile values and principles.
⬜ They should replace SAFe with a special Agile framework tailored for government agencies.
When implementing SAFe in a government organization, stakeholders sometimes suggest creating a modified “government-specific” version of SAFe with new terminology to fit existing processes. What does SAFe for Government recommend in this situation? ⬜ Adapt SAFe by renaming roles and artifacts to match the agency’s traditional terminology.
⬜ Use SAFe as-is, keeping standard SAFe terminology and practices unchanged.
⬜ Develop a unique Agile framework from scratch, tailored entirely to the agency’s culture.
⬜ Blend SAFe with the current waterfall governance by substituting stage-gate terms for SAFe terms.
Topic 2: Lean-Agile Mindset *Which three items are part of SAFe’s Core Values? (Choose three.) ⬜ Alignment
⬜ Relentless improvement
⬜ Decentralized decision-making
⬜ Program execution
⬜ Assume variability
⬜ Transparency
*What principle from the SAFe Core Values explains the purpose of the PI Planning retrospective? ⬜ Relentless improvement
⬜ Respect for people and culture
⬜ Innovation
⬜ Flow
Which SAFe core value emphasizes the need for all levels of the organization to work towards common objectives?​ ⬜ Transparency
⬜ Alignment
⬜ Built-in Quality
⬜ Program Execution​
In a multi-vendor government program, each contractor only shares progress at formal milestones, leading to late surprises and mistrust between the agency and suppliers. Which SAFe core value should be emphasized to improve this situation? ⬜ Built-In Quality
⬜ Alignment
⬜ Transparency
⬜ Program Execution
Which SAFe core value emphasizes the importance of decentralizing decision-making to the people closest to the work? ⬜ Alignment
⬜ Transparency
⬜ Relentless Improvement
⬜ Respect for People
*How can Lean-Agile leaders exemplify the SAFe Core Value of alignment? ⬜ Participate in backlog visibility, review, and preparation
⬜ Government and vendor managers prepare joint status reports
⬜ Invite vendor program managers to government management meetings
⬜ Demonstrate quality by refusing to accept or ship low quality work
*What is the Manifesto for Agile Software Development? ⬜ A shared set of values and principles intended to improve software development
⬜ A set of four values and twelve principles that help organizations implement systems thinking
⬜ A value system that only applies to software development
⬜ A set of practices that originated from Scrum
*What are two reasons the Agile Manifesto for Software Development is still relevant to Lean-Agile Enterprises? (Choose two.) ⬜ It provides the foundation for empowered, self-organizing Agile teams
⬜ SAFe extends the value system and principles of the Agile Manifesto to teams of Agile teams
⬜ Applying the Agile Manifesto is important for teams but less important for programs and portfolios
⬜ The foundations of the value system support organizational hierarchies for large Solutions
⬜ It enables governance and controls over plans at scale
Topic 3: SAFe Lean-Agile Principles *Which SAFe principle ensures the maximum benefit is generated by understanding trade-offs between risks, cost of delay, operational costs, and development costs for each program and Value Stream? ⬜ Take an economic view
⬜ Assume variability, preserve options
⬜ Apply systems thinking
⬜ Build incrementally with fast, integrated learning cycles
What does the SAFe principle ‘Take an economic view’ encourage government programs to consider? ⬜ Prioritize short-term cost savings
⬜ Choose vendors with the lowest hourly rate
⬜ Balance cost of delay, risk, and development costs
⬜ Eliminate trade-off discussions for faster decision-making
*Which statement is true about optimizing batch sizes for newly-formed SAFe teams in a program? ⬜ Batch size optimization happens over time as teams figure out the balance between holding cost and transaction cost
⬜ Batch size is optimized immediately by looking at transaction and holding costs
⬜ Batch size is already optimized if there is continuous flow
⬜ Batch size is optimized when transaction and holding costs seldom change
*What describes converting unpredictable events into predictable ones? ⬜ Cadence
⬜ Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration
⬜ Program Increment (PI) Planning
⬜ Backlog refinement
*What type of decision should be decentralized? ⬜ Unimportant
⬜ High cost of delay
⬜ Standard technology stack
⬜ Long-lasting
What is a key benefit of organizing around value in SAFe for government agencies? ⬜ Simplifies budgeting processes
⬜ Enhances hierarchical control
⬜ Improves flow of value to the customer
⬜ Reduces the need for cross-functional teams
What is the primary benefit of organizing around value streams in SAFe?​ ⬜ To align teams with departmental silos
⬜ To focus on delivering end-to-end value to the customer
⬜ To enhance individual performance metrics
⬜ To maintain traditional project management structures​
Which SAFe principle emphasizes delivering value incrementally to mitigate risk? ⬜ Apply systems thinking
⬜ Build incrementally with fast, integrated learning cycles
⬜ Organize around value
⬜ Base milestones on objective evaluation of working systems
*What are two reasons objective milestones like the System Demo are useful? (Choose two.) ⬜ They allow the contracting officer to release funds for payment
⬜ They satisfy phase-gate governance processes
⬜ They satisfy a SAFe requirement
⬜ They provide tangible evidence of progress
⬜ They allow for cost-effective adjustments toward an optimum solution
What is a key outcome of applying cadence in government Agile programs? ⬜ Delivers predictability only for budgeting teams
⬜ Reduces variability and provides regular synchronization points
⬜ Prevents changes during development
⬜ Ensures all work is released simultaneously
What is a benefit of using cadence and synchronization across multiple teams in a SAFe government program? ⬜ It enables teams to independently plan and deliver work
⬜ It removes the need for integrated reviews
⬜ It shifts responsibility for dependencies to the system architect
⬜ It allows for alignment, fast feedback, and cross-team coordination
What Lean-Agile principle encourages using shorter feedback cycles in government programs? ⬜ Centralized authority ensures long-term planning accuracy
⬜ Build incrementally with fast, integrated learning cycles
⬜ Outsourcing reduces complexity and feedback needs
⬜ Design complete systems before development begins
Topic 4: Agile Teams Who is responsible for designating a story as ‘Complete’ based on acceptance criteria when development is done by contractors? ⬜ The government Product Owner
⬜ The vendor program manager
⬜ The government contracting officer
⬜ The team
*Which role in SAFe has content authority over the Agile Team’s backlog? ⬜ Product Owner
⬜ Release Train Engineer
⬜ Product Management
⬜ Agile Team
Which role is primarily responsible for managing the Team Backlog in SAFe?​ ⬜ Product Owner
⬜ Scrum Master
⬜ Release Train Engineer
⬜ System Architect​
Toward the end of the Iteration, the Product Owner raises a red flag stating there is an additional requirement that needs to be added to the current Iteration. The Agile Team could handle the requirement if they work late and over the next weekend. What should the Scrum Master do? ⬜ Accept the work and extend the Iteration, informing other teams about the delay in delivery of other committed stories
⬜ Meet with the team and if they agree to work overtime, accept the work
⬜ Talk to the Product Owner, compare the new work to existing backlog priorities, and negotiate a sustainable solution
⬜ Refuse the new requirement because it is too late to accept requirements at this point in the Iteration
*What is an attribute of a high-performing team? ⬜ Healthy conflict
⬜ Slow, steady results
⬜ Strong dependency within the team
⬜ An empowered project manager
*What are two attributes of high-performing teams? (Choose two.) ⬜ Experience mutual trust
⬜ They are self-organizing
⬜ High-performing teams can be larger than the typical Agile team
⬜ High-performing teams do not require the assistance of a Scrum Master
⬜ Members of the team value uniformity
What are two attributes of high-performing Agile teams in government programs? (Choose two.) ⬜ Self-organization and mutual trust
⬜ Shared ownership of results
⬜ Exclusive use of command-and-control tools
⬜ Centralized review of all code and design decisions
Topic 5: Agile Release Train (ART) and Solution Train What is one outcome of using Agile Release Trains (ARTs) in a government agency? ⬜ They reduce the need for planning events
⬜ They align teams to a common mission and delivery cadence
⬜ They centralize decision-making at the executive level
⬜ They deliver all features only at the end of the year
Which SAFe role is responsible for providing technical leadership and defining the system architecture for the Agile Release Train (ART)? ⬜ Product Owner
⬜ System Architect
⬜ Scrum Master
⬜ Release Train Engineer (RTE)
What is one responsibility of the Release Train Engineer in SAFe government programs? ⬜ Own the technical implementation of epics
⬜ Approve contracts and budget allocations
⬜ Facilitate PI Planning and ART events
⬜ Define compliance standards and test plans
What is the role of the System Architect in a SAFe government program? ⬜ Prioritize backlog items based on business value
⬜ Ensure teams follow traditional development methods
⬜ Define the architectural vision and support compliance and interoperability
⬜ Manage day-to-day team activities
A large government program currently kicks off separate “siloed” projects for each new initiative, forming new teams that disband after delivering all contracted requirements. To adopt SAFe, what structural change should the agency make to improve the flow of value? ⬜ Continue using siloed project teams but add more documentation to coordinate between them.
⬜ Move people to whichever project has the highest priority at the moment to maximize utilization.
⬜ Plan all solution details upfront for each project, then assign teams to execute strictly to that plan.
⬜ Establish long-lived, cross-functional Agile Release Trains aligned to value streams, continuously delivering a flow of Epics from a prioritized backlog.
What is the primary purpose of the Solution Demo in SAFe’s Large Solution context? ⬜ To finalize the architectural design
⬜ To provide stakeholders with an integrated view of the solution’s progress
⬜ To conduct team-level retrospectives
⬜ To plan the next Program Increment
*When should government technology programs be organized as Solution Trains? ⬜ When the program crosses multiple agency divisions or branches
⬜ When the cost of the program exceeds $100M
⬜ When the program involves classified information
⬜ When the size and complexity require two or more ARTs
Topic 6: PI Planning *Which SAFe event provides a cadence for synchronization and alignment across multiple government agencies in a Large Solution? ⬜ PI Planning
⬜ Sprint Review
⬜ System Demo
⬜ Daily Standup
*Which SAFe ceremony is used to align all the teams to a common mission for the upcoming Program Increment (PI)? ⬜ PI Planning
⬜ System Demo
⬜ Scrum of Scrums
⬜ Release Planning
What is one benefit of Program Increment (PI) Planning? ⬜ It creates the Vision and Roadmap
⬜ It provides the opportunity to fully define the system architecture
⬜ It helps define Program Management Review agenda
⬜ It builds the social network on which the ART depends
What is a key outcome of PI Planning in SAFe?​ ⬜ A detailed project plan for the next year
⬜ A commitment to deliver specific features regardless of changing priorities
⬜ A shared understanding of objectives and alignment among teams
⬜ An isolated plan for each team without cross-team coordination​
In SAFe, what is the role of the Release Train Engineer (RTE) during PI Planning? ⬜ Define the architectural runway
⬜ Prioritize the team backlog
⬜ Facilitate the PI Planning event and ensure alignment across teams
⬜ Approve the PI Objectives
In addition to Program Increment (PI) Objectives and uncommitted objectives, what must also be identified during PI Planning?​ ⬜ Communication barriers and silos
⬜ Program risks
⬜ PI velocity goals
⬜ The chain of command​
*Which statement describes uncommitted objectives in SAFe? ⬜ They are reflected in the team’s load but not the capacity
⬜ Teams have low confidence they can meet the objective, but include it in their plan
⬜ Extra tasks a team could do in case they have time
⬜ They are included in the PI commitment, making the commitment more reliable
What is the role of PI Objectives during Program Increment Planning? ⬜ They are milestones for release governance
⬜ They communicate business value and alignment for the PI
⬜ They replace acceptance criteria for Features
⬜ They ensure compliance reviews are conducted each iteration
Why are uncommitted objectives important in government ARTs? ⬜ They serve as stretch goals only for high-performing teams
⬜ They provide visibility into work planned with lower confidence
⬜ They represent work removed from the PI Scope
⬜ They are tracked separately but included in the business value score
What is a key role of Business Owners during PI Planning in government programs? ⬜ Estimating team velocity and capacity
⬜ Assigning tasks to Agile teams
⬜ Approving final contract language
⬜ Scoring team PI Objectives to assess business value
In SAFe for Government, what is the primary purpose of aligning governance reviews with the Program Increment (PI) cadence?​ ⬜ To enforce strict compliance with initial project plans
⬜ To streamline oversight and reduce delays by synchronizing reviews with development cycles
⬜ To conduct comprehensive audits at the end of each fiscal year
⬜ To separate governance activities from development processes​
How can a government agency using SAFe improve collaboration with its vendor partners? ⬜ Require vendors to deliver complete scope before feedback
⬜ Invite vendors to participate in PI Planning and system demos
⬜ Limit vendor interaction to monthly check-ins
⬜ Prohibit vendors from joining daily standups
At what levels are confidence votes taken once dependencies and program risks are addressed? ⬜ Program and Portfolio
⬜ Program and Branch
⬜ Program and Train
⬜ Program and Team
A government program involves multiple contractor teams working on a shared system, but each team operates on its own schedules, causing integration issues. What practice should the program adopt to synchronize all teams and address the inherent uncertainty in development? ⬜ Allow each team to set its own cadence and integrate only at the end of the fiscal year.
⬜ Establish a common cadence for all teams and conduct regular PI Planning (cross-team planning) to synchronize efforts.
⬜ Mandate a detailed, unchanging 12-month project plan that all teams must follow strictly.
⬜ Rely on the prime contractor to independently coordinate and deliver an integrated system without joint planning.
Topic 7: SAFe Events *What are three reasons the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration is critical to success in SAFe? (Choose three.) ⬜ It creates a guard band that ensures program predictability on cadence
⬜ It ensures time for creative problem-solving needed by knowledge workers
⬜ It provides a consistent time for PI Planning
⬜ It creates a predictable window to allow for personal time off
⬜ It is the only way a government ART can afford to do hackathons
⬜ It provides the only time the Product Management can conduct backlog refinement
Why is the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration important in SAFe government programs? ⬜ It allows time for finalizing contract deliverables
⬜ It provides a buffer to accommodate late feature work
⬜ It supports innovation, PI Planning, and continuous improvement
⬜ It provides an opportunity to delay quality activities until the end of the PI
What is the primary purpose of the Inspect and Adapt (I&A) event in SAFe?​ ⬜ To plan the next Program Increment
⬜ To reflect on the past increment and identify improvement actions
⬜ To demonstrate the final product to stakeholders
⬜ To assign tasks to team members​
What supports early risk identification and mitigation in a SAFe government program? ⬜ Holding risk reviews only at the end of a PI
⬜ Regular System Demos and Inspect & Adapt events
⬜ Relying solely on contract status meetings
⬜ Removing uncommitted objectives from tracking
Which practice supports consistent engagement from stakeholders and enables compliance during the PI? ⬜ Conducting detailed documentation reviews after development
⬜ Participating in the System Demo
⬜ Reviewing backlog items before every release
⬜ Freezing scope during each PI
Topic 8: Program Vision and Roadmap What is the primary purpose of the Program Vision in SAFe government programs? ⬜ To define team-level tasks and responsibilities
⬜ To outline the detailed technical specifications
⬜ To provide a shared direction and context for the Agile Release Train
⬜ To establish fixed budget allocations for each team
How does the Program Roadmap assist in SAFe government program execution? ⬜ By detailing individual team sprints and tasks
⬜ By specifying exact release dates for all features
⬜ By forecasting the delivery of features over time to achieve the vision
⬜ By listing all compliance requirements in a fixed schedule
*In a SAFe Roadmap, which PIs are committed? ⬜ The first one
⬜ The first three
⬜ All
⬜ The first two
Topic 9: Feature and Capability What is the primary purpose of defining system attributes using Features in a government SAFe program? ⬜ To define contract milestones in advance
⬜ To delegate all compliance responsibility to vendors
⬜ To document the entire system design before development begins
⬜ To express system behaviors and capabilities in a value-focused way
Which attribute should a properly defined Feature include to support system definition in government programs? ⬜ A signed contract
⬜ A compliance waiver
⬜ Acceptance criteria
⬜ Waterfall design documentation
What element in SAFe is typically used to describe and manage system attributes for Agile development? ⬜ Epics
⬜ NFRs
⬜ Stories
⬜ Enablers
How does defining system attributes with Features support compliance in SAFe government programs? ⬜ By ensuring requirements are fixed before development starts
⬜ By assigning all compliance testing to vendors
⬜ By enabling traceable, testable expressions of system capabilities
⬜ By deferring reviews until final delivery
Topic 10: Agency Strategy How does SAFe recommend structuring large government programs to stay aligned with agency strategy? ⬜ Use traditional project structures with fixed scope and milestones
⬜ Prioritize system design before identifying mission goals
⬜ Organize around long-lived Value Streams and Agile Release Trains (ARTs)
⬜ Separate teams based on vendor and government affiliation
*Which represents a good example of an agency Strategic Theme? ⬜ Comply with agency development lifecycle regulations
⬜ Reduce agency IT spend
⬜ Improve cost and schedule performance of IT projects
⬜ Create a ‘one-stop shop’ for all citizen-facing services provided by the agency
*What assists with Epic evaluation and decision-making? ⬜ Strategic Themes
⬜ Program Budgets
⬜ Solution Intent
⬜ Lean Budgets
What is the purpose of having Strategic Themes in a SAFe government portfolio? ⬜ To track backlog refinement sessions at the team level
⬜ To estimate feature sizes using team velocity
⬜ To delegate compliance responsibilities
⬜ To align portfolio investments with mission and strategy
*In reference to large programs, what are Strategic Themes? ⬜ A collection of ideas used at the program level to create Epics
⬜ Itemized mission objectives connecting a portfolio to the strategy
⬜ Persuasive concepts used to aid in the ’tipping’ process of decision-makers in an agency or program
⬜ Vehicles used to decentralize decision-making
Topic 11: Lean flow of Epics *What are Business Epics in SAFe? ⬜ System attributes that deliver business value
⬜ Solution descriptions for the business
⬜ An Agile term that is equivalent to a government program
⬜ Solutions to address financial constraints
*What is the appropriate Lean action to take once all of the expected value of an Epic has been delivered, even if all of the planned Features have not been completed? ⬜ Close the Epic
⬜ Initiate an early re-compete
⬜ Finish all of the Features since they were included in the contract
⬜ Continue building Features until the contract can be modified
Which statement best describes the Lean-Agile alternative to traditional project-based development in government? ⬜ Create fixed-scope, fixed-funding projects with annual delivery targets
⬜ Manage Epics in continuous flow using a prioritized backlog and long-lived teams
⬜ Outsource projects entirely to reduce delivery overhead
⬜ Delay execution until detailed upfront planning is complete
What does SAFe recommend instead of traditional change control boards in government Agile programs? ⬜ Increasing the frequency of document reviews
⬜ Relying solely on phase-gate assessments
⬜ Using the backlog and PI Planning to manage scope changes collaboratively
⬜ Restricting all change decisions to the PMO
What helps government teams determine the best order to deliver Epics? ⬜ Technical complexity alone
⬜ Historical spending reports
⬜ Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF)
⬜ Alphabetical ranking by title
Topic 12: Lean Budgeting Which SAFe concept supports funding Value Streams rather than specific projects? ⬜ Guardrail budgeting
⬜ Fixed-scope project funding
⬜ Lean Budgets
⬜ Task-based labor rates
What is a key benefit of adopting Lean budgeting for government programs? ⬜ Reduces the need for financial oversight and reviews
⬜ Focuses on exact funding for each Feature or Story
⬜ Enables continuous funding of value streams to support adaptive priorities
⬜ Encourages annual budget commitments to fixed initiatives
What is one benefit of using Lean budgeting in government programs? ⬜ It allows spending without financial controls
⬜ It assigns fixed funding to each team or project
⬜ It delays funding decisions to later PIs
⬜ It enables continuous funding aligned with value delivery
*In Advanced Lean-Agile government, what is the primary benefit of using Lean budgeting? ⬜ It allows government agencies to spend freely without controls.
⬜ It provides a way to allocate funds to individual teams.
⬜ It promotes continuous funding and adaptability.
⬜ It centralizes budgeting decisions within the government.
What does it mean to fund Value Streams instead of projects in SAFe government programs? ⬜ It increases the number of funding approvals required each year
⬜ It requires scope to be defined up front for the entire fiscal year
⬜ It enables persistent teams to deliver value continuously within guardrails
⬜ It limits the program’s ability to adapt to changing mission needs
How does Lean budgeting benefit government programs?​ ⬜ By allocating funds strictly per project
⬜ By enabling flexible funding aligned with value delivery
⬜ By centralizing all financial decisions
⬜ By enforcing rigid budget constraints​
In SAFe for Government, what is the role of Lean Budgeting in governance?​ ⬜ It enables decentralized decision-making within guardrails
⬜ It centralizes all financial decisions to a single authority
⬜ It eliminates the need for financial oversight
⬜ It restricts funding to annual cycles​
*What two visual reporting tools can be used to help maintain fiduciary tracking of government technology programs? (Choose two.) ⬜ Feature progress charts
⬜ Burn-up charts
⬜ Detailed spreadsheets
⬜ Pro formas
⬜ Integrated master schedules
*Which reduces the cone of uncertainty? ⬜ Convergence of alternatives with flexible specifications
⬜ Convergence of requirements with designs
⬜ Convergence of architectures with design sets
⬜ Convergence of flexible specifications with design sets
Traditionally, a government agency funds each IT project with a separate, fixed budget. This makes it difficult to shift money when new high-priority needs emerge. How does SAFe’s Lean budgeting approach address this challenge? ⬜ By locking in project budgets but increasing contingency funds for scope changes.
⬜ By funding long-lived value streams (the “agency’s development factory”) instead of individual projects, allowing flexible reallocation of effort as priorities change.
⬜ By cutting funding to all projects annually to force reprioritization.
⬜ By requiring each project manager to get approval for budget changes through formal change orders.
Topic 13: Lean Estimating and Forecasting *Which statement is true for estimating and forecasting in SAFe? ⬜ ART velocities are used to conduct ‘what if’ analysis
⬜ Feature estimation is independent of team-level input
⬜ Epics should be estimated by the Epic Owner
⬜ Work breakdown structure to the task level helps increase estimation accuracy
Which element supports Lean estimating and forecasting in government programs? ⬜ Long-term waterfall requirements
⬜ Detailed up-front contracts
⬜ Team and ART velocity based on historical data
⬜ Completion-based payment gates
What is a core principle of estimating and forecasting in SAFe for government programs? ⬜ All estimation must be done upfront to lock budgets early
⬜ Teams should avoid using historical data to project delivery
⬜ Forecasting is based on actual velocity and cadence, not rigid plans
⬜ Forecasting is only meaningful at the portfolio level
How does SAFe recommend estimating and forecasting in Lean-Agile government programs? ⬜ By defining full requirements upfront and estimating delivery dates at contract award
⬜ By using detailed work breakdown structures for each iteration
⬜ By applying historical ART velocity and cadence-based planning for incremental forecasting
⬜ By relying solely on vendor proposals to estimate scope and schedule
What enables consistent and reliable forecasting in SAFe’s cadence-based model? ⬜ Mandated timelines and fixed milestones
⬜ Top-down estimation by executives
⬜ Regular planning intervals and team velocity
⬜ Upfront commitments to detailed requirements
Why is cadence-based forecasting preferred over traditional project planning in Lean-Agile environments? ⬜ It eliminates the need for scope negotiation
⬜ It locks delivery into quarterly milestones
⬜ It allows for regular adjustments based on actual team throughput
⬜ It reduces stakeholder involvement in estimation
Topic 14: Acquisition Practices How should acquisition practices evolve to support Lean-Agile in government? ⬜ Require full upfront requirements and fixed scope
⬜ Use firm fixed-price contracts with milestone gating
⬜ Shift to modular contracts that focus on outcomes and collaboration
⬜ Restrict vendors from engaging in planning events
Which two SAFe principles are most critical when adapting Lean-Agile practices to government acquisition models? (Choose two.) ⬜ Build incrementally with fast, integrated learning cycles
⬜ Take an economic view
⬜ Apply systems thinking
⬜ Organize around value
How should government acquisition practices evolve to support Lean-Agile development? ⬜ Maintain firm-fixed-price contracts to ensure delivery
⬜ Finalize requirements before awarding contracts
⬜ Shift from rigid scope control to modular, outcome-based contracts
⬜ Use change orders to manage evolving priorities
What change in acquisition practices is essential for enabling Lean-Agile development in government? ⬜ Awarding contracts based only on lowest cost proposals
⬜ Introducing modular contracts that support incremental delivery and collaboration
⬜ Relying on fixed-scope, fixed-price contracts with detailed up-front planning
⬜ Extending the timeline for vendor selection to ensure exhaustive documentation
Why do traditional acquisition methods often conflict with Agile principles in government programs? ⬜ They allow too much team autonomy
⬜ They require fixed requirements and deliverables before any work begins
⬜ They enable too much experimentation and change
⬜ They rely on minimal oversight and governance
What is a primary risk of continuing to use traditional acquisition models in Agile programs? ⬜ Overspending on contractor rates
⬜ Excessive documentation burdens
⬜ Delayed system integration
⬜ Forcing vendors into waterfall behaviors, undermining Agile execution
One of the biggest hurdles in a government Agile transformation is the standard procurement process. How should a government agency modify its acquisition practices to support a Lean-Agile approach? ⬜ Continue using traditional fixed-scope, waterfall contracts so vendors are tightly controlled.
⬜ Introduce contract structures with incremental deliverables and Lean-Agile friendly terms, enabling vendors to work in an Agile manner.
⬜ Outsource Agile development completely and manage via strict penalties for any changes in scope or schedule.
⬜ Require all Agile teams to freeze requirements upfront to fit existing contract templates.
Topic 15: Build in Quality and Compliance *What result comes from traditional ‘at the end’ quality and compliance? ⬜ Missed opportunities for iterative compliance assessment
⬜ Faster receipt of authority to operate in traditional projects
⬜ Nominal quality differences when compared with waterfall approaches
⬜ Shorter testing timelines
*What events in SAFe provide objective evidence of built-in quality and compliance? ⬜ System Demos
⬜ PI Planning
⬜ Backlog refinement
⬜ ART syncs
Which SAFe practice supports compliance and governance by integrating quality checks throughout the development process?​ ⬜ Built-in Quality
⬜ Innovation and Planning Iteration
⬜ System Demo
⬜ Release on Demand​
Which SAFe practice integrates compliance activities into the development process to ensure continuous verification and validation?​ ⬜ Built-in Quality
⬜ System Demo
⬜ Inspect and Adapt
⬜ Innovation and Planning Iteration​
Why is “Built-In Quality” critical in government Lean-Agile programs? ⬜ It helps teams move faster by delaying testing
⬜ It allows for bulk compliance checks near delivery
⬜ It ensures every increment meets security, regulatory, and functional standards
⬜ It centralizes validation efforts under the System Architect
Why is Built-In Quality essential for compliance in SAFe’s approach to government programs?​ ⬜ It allows teams to defer quality checks until the end of development
⬜ It ensures that quality and compliance are maintained throughout the development process
⬜ It reduces the need for documentation and testing
⬜ It focuses solely on meeting user requirements​
What are two benefits of implementing Built-In Quality in SAFe government programs? (Choose two.) ⬜ Reduces rework and downstream defects
⬜ Avoids compliance documentation
⬜ Improves trust in each increment of value
⬜ Allows skipping of final testing and integration
In SAFe, how is compliance integrated into the development process?​ ⬜ By conducting compliance checks only at the end of the project
⬜ By assigning compliance responsibilities solely to a separate team
⬜ By embedding compliance activities throughout the development lifecycle
⬜ By minimizing compliance to accelerate delivery​
How does SAFe ensure ongoing compliance in government programs?​ ⬜ By integrating compliance activities into the continuous delivery pipeline
⬜ By conducting compliance reviews only at the end of the project
⬜ By assigning compliance to a separate team
⬜ By minimizing documentation requirements​
How does SAFe’s compliance approach benefit government programs? ⬜ It delays audits until program completion
⬜ It embeds compliance into ongoing development activities
⬜ It minimizes required documentation
⬜ It centralizes responsibility in the legal team
How does SAFe recommend handling compliance requirements in government programs? ⬜ Address compliance at the end of the development cycle
⬜ Integrate compliance activities into the development process
⬜ Assign compliance tasks to a separate team
⬜ Delay compliance considerations until after deployment
How does SAFe’s approach to compliance differ from traditional methods in government programs?​ ⬜ Compliance is addressed only at the end of the development lifecycle
⬜ Compliance activities are integrated continuously throughout the development process
⬜ Compliance is managed exclusively by a separate oversight team
⬜ Compliance requirements are minimized to accelerate delivery​
A defense agency’s agile teams deliver working software every iteration, but the agency still conducts a massive final integration and verification phase at the end for compliance, causing long delays. What change does SAFe for Government recommend to improve flow? ⬜ Perform all compliance reviews and testing after development is complete to minimize disruption.
⬜ Limit testing to only the final system demonstration to save time during development.
⬜ Integrate verification, validation, and compliance activities into the ongoing development flow (build quality in every iteration).
⬜ Separate the compliance team entirely so that developers can work without oversight until the end.
Topic 16: Governance Practices *What is governance in a SAFe context? ⬜ A framework for decision-making to ensure programs achieve desired mission outcomes
⬜ Oversight that is provided by the PMO
⬜ Agency level regulations that ensure compliance with federal laws
⬜ Participatory budgeting events conducted twice annually by LPM
*What is the purpose of governance on a Lean-Agile government program? ⬜ To provide a framework for decision-making to achieve desired mission outcomes
⬜ To ensure the Solution is delivered within fixed time, cost, and scope constraints
⬜ To ensure compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements
⬜ To ensure contractors are accountable for how taxpayer money is spent
How does SAFe recommend adapting governance in government programs? ⬜ Use traditional phase-gate approvals to ensure rigorous compliance
⬜ Require rigid adherence to initial planning artifacts
⬜ Replace stage-gates with objective milestones and evidence-based reviews
⬜ Centralize all governance under a portfolio steering committee
Why is it important to adapt governance practices in Lean-Agile government programs? ⬜ To increase documentation for audit purposes
⬜ To enforce milestone-based funding control
⬜ To replace planning with automated tracking
⬜ To support continuous value delivery with visibility and oversight
Why should traditional phase-gate reviews be replaced with objective milestones in government SAFe programs? ⬜ They reduce the need for planning and budgeting
⬜ They provide real-time evidence of progress and fitness for purpose
⬜ They delegate compliance entirely to contractors
⬜ They are less visible to oversight bodies
What does SAFe recommend to replace traditional detailed phase-gate reviews? ⬜ Year-end milestone reporting
⬜ Daily program status meetings
⬜ Frequent objective reviews using working software
⬜ Up-front contract deliverables
What is one advantage of aligning SAFe governance events with the Program Increment cadence? ⬜ It defers all compliance and risk checks to the end of the PI
⬜ It prevents the need for traditional milestone reviews
⬜ It synchronizes reviews with development flow and increases visibility
⬜ It allows audit teams to work independently from Agile teams
Why does SAFe recommend replacing rigid milestone reviews with continuous oversight? ⬜ To allow audit activities to be delayed
⬜ To simplify budget approvals
⬜ To enable dynamic evaluation of progress based on working systems
⬜ To eliminate the need for governance reporting
What governance shift is necessary to support Lean flow in SAFe government programs? ⬜ Increase documentation requirements
⬜ Add more checkpoints between Agile teams
⬜ Review compliance only during post-deployment audit
⬜ Move from prescriptive oversight to ongoing engagement and transparency
*What are two recommendations for tracking expenditures using the Program Backlog? (Choose two.) ⬜ Tagging backlog items with funding metadata for future reporting
⬜ Organizing ARTs by funding classification
⬜ Including a fiduciary expert in backlog refinement
⬜ Using charge codes assigned by each program
⬜ Calculating a fixed cost labor cost per ART based on actual salaries
*What type of decision may significantly affect lead time for systems development? ⬜ Approved budget, required development tools, and dedicated team members
⬜ Using firm fixed price contracts
⬜ Using relative size estimating
⬜ Prioritizing the product backlog using WSJF
What is a key benefit of implementing Lean Governance in SAFe for government agencies?​ ⬜ Centralizes decision-making authority to a single oversight body
⬜ Supports oversight of spending, audit, compliance, and reporting within a Lean-Agile framework
⬜ Eliminates the need for compliance and audit activities
⬜ Replaces all existing governance structures with Agile teams​
What are two responsibilities of Lean Portfolio Management in SAFe government programs? (Choose two.) ⬜ Guide investment funding across value streams
⬜ Define team-level iteration goals
⬜ Monitor code quality metrics
⬜ Apply guardrails to enable decentralized decision-making
Which SAFe practice replaces traditional phase-gate reviews to provide objective evidence of progress in government programs?​ ⬜ System Demo
⬜ Incremental Capability Review (ICR)
⬜ Release Planning
⬜ Scrum of Scrums​
What is the role of an Incremental Capability Review (ICR)? ⬜ It replaces the need for System Demos
⬜ It finalizes contract payments for vendors
⬜ It provides objective, milestone-based progress evaluation
⬜ It delays feature releases until compliance is confirmed
How does the Incremental Capability Review (ICR) enhance governance in SAFe for government programs?​ ⬜ It provides objective evidence of working systems to assess progress
⬜ It replaces the need for all compliance documentation
⬜ It eliminates the requirement for system demos
⬜ It centralizes decision-making authority​
A PMO in a federal agency insists on using a detailed upfront project plan and formal stage-gate reviews (Requirements Review, Design Review, etc.) for an Agile program. How should governance be adapted to better support Lean-Agile development while still ensuring oversight? ⬜ Replace all governance checkpoints with team self-management and provide no oversight.
⬜ Continue with the same phase-gate process since governance must remain unchanged.
⬜ Use Lean-Agile alternatives (like objective milestones with working systems, and ongoing oversight via metrics) instead of big phase-gate reviews, to provide governance through continuous flow of value.
⬜ Micromanage the Agile teams through more frequent status meetings to maintain control.
A government IT portfolio has historically rolled over funding for certain systems each year without revisiting their strategic relevance. According to SAFe for Government, how should agencies ensure their technology investments remain aligned with current strategic priorities? ⬜ By continuing to fund the same projects year after year to maintain consistency.
⬜ By conducting periodic portfolio reviews and aligning development funding to strategic agency objectives.
⬜ By entrusting contractors to decide which initiatives best serve the agency’s strategy.
⬜ By focusing only on compliance requirements and ignoring strategic fit during budgeting.
Topic 17: Implementation Roadmap *An agency is ready to undertake a large modernization effort. Though the agency ensures the correct implementation of all stage gates in their SDLC, projects seem to always be over budget. They are exploring the use of SAFe due to the success stories from other agencies. What is the appropriate first step? ⬜ Map all stage gates to Agile events
⬜ Train Product Owners in the principles, practices, and benefits of adopting SAFe
⬜ Start an Agile project with an internal Agile Scrum Master
⬜ Identify and train change agents that will lead the effort
*When do organizations begin realizing better results when following the Implementation Roadmap? ⬜ As soon as the first Program Increment
⬜ Once all steps in the roadmap are complete
⬜ Once all training classes have been completed
⬜ Once the predictability measure exceeds 80%
*Which two statements accurately describe the SAFe Implementation Roadmap? (Choose two.) ⬜ It reflects success patterns from previous implementations of SAFe
⬜ It provides recommended sequencing of role-based training
⬜ It ensures standardization with software life cycle best practices
⬜ The steps in the roadmap must be followed in order
⬜ All steps must be complete with the first ART before launching additional trains
When implementing SAFe in a government setting, what is a key consideration for successful adoption?​ ⬜ Maintaining existing bureaucratic processes
⬜ Customizing SAFe terminology extensively
⬜ Engaging leadership to champion the change
⬜ Isolating Agile teams from the rest of the organization​
What shift does SAFe recommend for traditional project management offices (PMOs) in government agencies? ⬜ Retain control over day-to-day team assignments
⬜ Eliminate roles associated with oversight and reporting
⬜ Focus solely on compliance enforcement
⬜ Evolve into a Lean-Agile Center of Excellence supporting continuous improvement
In a SAFe implementation at a government agency, Agile teams consist of both civil servants and contractors. Initially, interactions are strained, with contractors and government personnel working more against each other than together. What cultural shift does SAFe for Government say is needed to build high-performing teams in this multi-vendor environment? ⬜ The government staff should direct the contractors with a command-and-control approach to enforce compliance.
⬜ Contractors should work independently on their deliverables to avoid conflict with government employees.
⬜ Government and contractor personnel must start collaborating as one team-of-teams, moving from an adversarial relationship to a partnership mindset.
⬜ Replace all contractors with government employees, since mixed teams cannot function effectively in Agile.
Topic 18: Lean Agile Leadership *Which aspect of leading by example challenges Lean-Agile leaders to ‘walk the talk’ by being a role model of desired professional and ethical behaviors by acting with honesty, integrity, and transparency? ⬜ Authenticity
⬜ Emotional intelligence
⬜ Life-long learning
⬜ Decentralized decision-making
*What occurs when leaders create an environment for risk-taking that supports change without fear of negative consequences to self-image, status, or career? ⬜ Psychological safety
⬜ Decentralized decision-making
⬜ Emotional intelligence
⬜ Alignment
*In SAFe, what is the primary responsibility of a Lean-Agile Leader in the government organization? ⬜ Setting the vision and strategy for the organization
⬜ Leading the Agile Release Train (ART)
⬜ Managing the daily activities of Agile teams
⬜ Providing technical guidance to development teams
How does Lean-Agile leadership improve government program outcomes? ⬜ By enforcing strict top-down accountability
⬜ By delegating all responsibilities to contractors
⬜ By reducing the role of compliance teams
⬜ By modeling servant leadership and enabling decision-making at the right level
What outcome is expected when leaders create psychological safety in a SAFe government environment? ⬜ Increased reliance on fixed-scope contracts
⬜ Elimination of backlog grooming sessions
⬜ Greater team participation, innovation, and learning
⬜ Strict enforcement of top-down command structures

103 Practice Questions Topic 1: DevOps What best describes the DevOps? ⬜ A high-performing DevOps Team
⬜ Combine Deployment and Releases ⬜ Strong organizational structure
⬜ A culture, a mindset and a set of technical practices
Which statement is true about DevOps? ⬜ It enables low-risk releases and fast recovery with fast fix-forward
⬜ It enables low-risk releases and fast recovery with no room for errors
⬜ It enables high-risk releases and fast recovery with fast fix-forward
⬜ It enables a tolerance for low-risk, low-failure, and rapid recovery
*What are two benefits of DevOps? (Choose two) ⬜ Less frequent deployments
⬜ More lead time
⬜ Less time spent on new work
⬜ Fewer defects
⬜ Less time spent fixing security issues
*Which statement describes a measurable benefit of adopting DevOps practices and principles? ⬜ It results in faster lead time, and more frequent deployments
⬜ It identifies key Value Streams
⬜ It guarantees an increase in profits and decrease in downtime
⬜ It creates a highly functional, cross-team culture
Which statement is true when continuously deploying using a DevOps model? ⬜ It alleviates the reliance on the skill sets of Agile teams
⬜ It increases the transaction cost
⬜ It lessens the severity and frequency of release failures
⬜ It ensures that changes deployed to production are always immediately available to end-users
What organizational anti-pattern does DevOps help to address? ⬜ Teams that are isolated and working within functional areas (e.g., business, operations, and technology)
⬜ Too much focus on centralized planning
⬜ Walls of confusion between Customers and the business
⬜ Organizations that make decisions along functional lines
*Gemba walks are an important competency in support of which activity of the DevOps Health Radar? ⬜ Hypothesize
⬜ Continuous Exploration
⬜ Collaborate and Research
⬜ Learn
*Which teams should coordinate when responding to production issues? ⬜ Teams across the Value Stream
⬜ Dev teams and Ops teams
⬜ Support teams and Dev teams
⬜ SRE teams and System teams
*What is the main goal of a SAFe DevOps transformation? ⬜ To create a strong DevOps team with leadership support
⬜ To create immutable infrastructure to avoid changes to the production environment
⬜ To implement an advanced tool chain to automate the entire Continuous Delivery Pipeline
⬜ To align people across the Value Stream to deliver value continuously
*DevOps is a key enabler of continuous delivery. What does continuous mean in this context? ⬜ To deploy to production and release on cadence every Iteration
⬜ To deploy to production and release at least once every Program Increment
⬜ To deploy to production as often as possible and release when the business needs it
⬜ To deploy to production multiple times per year and release on a cadence once or twice a year
Which statement describes what could happen when development and operations do not collaborate early in the pipeline? ⬜ Surprises are found in deployment that lead to significant rework and delay
⬜ Automation of integration test is not possible
⬜ Teams build things quickly but build the wrong things
⬜ Lead times are reduced
The DevOps Health Radar aligns the four aspects of the Continuous Delivery Pipeline to which four stakeholder concerns? ⬜ Exploration, integration, development, reflection
⬜ Portfolio, Solution, program, team
⬜ Productivity, efficiency, speed-to-market, competitive advantage
⬜ Alignment, quality, time-to-market, business value
What does SAFe’s CALMR approach apply to? ⬜ PI Planning
⬜ DevOps ⬜ Economic Framework
⬜ Continuous Deployment
How does “C” in CALMR approach to DevOps help to organize around value and deliver continuous value? ⬜ By automating the continuous delivery pipeline ⬜ By Measuring the flow, quality & value ⬜ By creating a culture of shared responsibility ⬜ By accelerating delivery using lean flow
*What is a core DevOps principle? ⬜ Lean Budgets
⬜ Culture
⬜ Servant leadership
⬜ Iteration review
What is one element of the CALMR approach to DevOps? ⬜ Maximize work in process ⬜ Relentlessly reduce risk
⬜ Lean Flow accelerates delivery ⬜ Activate the knowledge worker
*What should be measured in a CALMR approach to DevOps? ⬜ Deployment frequency
⬜ Mean time to restore
⬜ Everything
⬜ Flow, quality, and value
*Who is responsible for ensuring quality is built into the code in SAFe? ⬜ Agile Teams
⬜ Product Owners
⬜ Testers
⬜ Developers
Who is responsible for building and continually improving the Continuous Delivery Pipeline? ⬜ System Teams
⬜ Agile Release Trains
⬜ Scrum Teams
⬜ DevOps Teams
One goal of DevOps in SAFe is to fully automate the steps between which two pipeline activities? ⬜ Code commit and release
⬜ Code commit and user acceptance testing
⬜ Code commit and deploy
⬜ Code commit and stage
What can impede the progress of a DevOps transformation the most? ⬜ When teams use frequent retrospectives
⬜ When there is no DevOps team
⬜ When various groups in the organization have different directions and goals
⬜ Lack of funding for CI/CD pipeline tools
What marks the beginning of the Continuous Delivery Pipeline? ⬜ An idea
⬜ A committed Feature
⬜ A checked-in change
⬜ A committed user story
Topic 2: Value Stream Mapping *What is the primary benefit of value stream mapping? ⬜ It fosters collaboration among development and operations managers
⬜ It creates the hypothesis of which Solution to build
⬜ It identifies how to build Agile Release Trains
⬜ It provides insight into organizational efficiency and value flow
What is the purpose of Value Stream Mapping? ⬜ To create an action plan for continuous improvement
⬜ To create an understanding of the budget
⬜ To understand the priorities of the Product Owner (PO)
⬜ To deliver incremental value in the form of working tested software and systems
Which two statements describe the purpose of value stream mapping? (Choose two.) ⬜ To create an action plan for continuous improvement
⬜ To visualize how value flows
⬜ To deliver incremental value in the form of working, tested software and systems
⬜ To create an understanding of the budget
⬜ To understand the Product Owner’s priorities
What does value stream mapping help reveal in the Continuous Delivery Pipeline? ⬜ Bottlenecks to the flow of value
⬜ Where automation is needed
⬜ Who is responsible for optimizing the Value Stream
⬜ DevOps practices that will improve the value stream
Mapping the value stream helps accomplish which two actions? (Choose two.) ⬜ To serve as a blueprint for development
⬜ To prioritize the Program Backlog
⬜ To gain insight into organizational efficiency
⬜ To understand how the flow of value can be improved
⬜ To add or remove user segments based on business decisions
What is one of the top advantages of mapping the current state of the Value Stream? ⬜ To help identify and make short-term fixes
⬜ To help with incremental software delivery
⬜ To achieve a collective understanding and consensus around problems
⬜ To identify some of the processes within the delivery pipeline
*After the team maps the steps of the current state Value Stream during value stream mapping, what are the next two steps? (Choose two.) ⬜ Identify who is involved in each step
⬜ Create a future state value stream map
⬜ Perform a SWOT analysis
⬜ Calculate the Activity Ratio
⬜ Measure the performance at each step
What are the first two actions for visualizing the current state of the Continuous Delivery Pipeline? (Choose two.) ⬜ Identify the steps
⬜ Identify the people
⬜ Identify throughput
⬜ Identify lead time
⬜ Identify the development methodology
What are the first two areas that should be identified in value stream mapping? (Choose two.) ⬜ The steps
⬜ The people who do the work
⬜ Process time, lead time, and percent complete and accurate
⬜ The bottlenecks
⬜ The people who supervise the work
What should the team be able to do after current-state mapping? ⬜ Define a plan to reduce the lead time and increase Active Time
⬜ Identify those responsible for the biggest bottlenecks in the process
⬜ Describe the biggest bottlenecks in the delivery pipeline
⬜ Define Enabler Features that will improve the Value Stream
*Value stream mapping metrics include calculations of which three metrics? (Choose three) ⬜ Total Process Time
⬜ Rolled % Complete and Accurate
⬜ Activity Ratio
⬜ Release Frequency
⬜ Outage Frequency
⬜ Emergency Change %
*What does the %C&A metric measure in the Continuous Delivery Pipeline? ⬜ The percent concurrent and accurate process times of each pipeline activity
⬜ The percent complete and average times of each pipeline activity
⬜ The percent of change averages of each pipeline activity
⬜ The percent of time downstream customers receive work that is usable as-is
Who should be consulted first when calculating the % Complete and Accurate? ⬜ The people responsible for the next step
⬜ The lead developer
⬜ End users
⬜ Testers
What does the activity ratio measure in the Value Stream? ⬜ The percentage of time spent on non-value-added activities
⬜ The percentage of time spent on manual activities
⬜ The percentage of time spent on delays to the number of processes in the Value Stream
⬜ The percentage of time spent on value-added activities
Which statement illustrates the biggest bottleneck? ⬜ WT = 5 days, AT = 2.5 days, %C&A = 100%
⬜ WT = 1 day, AT = 0.5 day, %C&A = 90%

⬜ Finalize the PI Objectives for the upcoming PI
⬜ To serve as a buffer for teams to meet PI objectives and provide time for innovation, planning, and learning
⬜ To increase the velocity of the Agile Release Train (ART)
*What is one benefit of having a well-executed Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration? ⬜ Higher flow of program-level business value
⬜ Improved dependency management between teams
⬜ Occasional buffer time to deliver more predictably
⬜ Shorter lead times before Feature delivery
How often does the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration occur? ⬜ During every PI
⬜ Every two Iterations
⬜ Every two PIs
⬜ One per year
*The ART is near the end of the final Iteration of its first PI. Integration into staging is more challenging than estimated. The ART adds a week to the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration for integration and testing. Why is this action considered an anti-pattern? ⬜ It substantially decreases the predictability of the Solution Intent
⬜ It decreases job satisfaction by removing autonomy and purpose
⬜ Overall, train velocity goes up, and the time-to-market goes down
⬜ It reduces the overall predictability established through cadence and synchronization
What statement is true about Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration? (Choose two.) ⬜ IP Iteration is a unique, dedicated iteration that occurs every PI
⬜ IP Iteration provides dedicated time for PI Planning and I&A events
⬜ IP Iteration is a unique, dedicated iteration that occurs after every 2 or 3 PIs
⬜ IP Iteration provides dedicated time to fix defects of the previous Iterations
Which statement is true about the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration? ⬜ It is used annually when the team needs to refocus on work processes
⬜ It is used as a weekly sync point between the Scrum Masters
⬜ Without the IP Iteration, there is a risk that the ’tyranny of the urgent’ outweighs all innovation activities
⬜ The Scrum Master can decide if the IP Iteration is necessary
Which of the following is a bad practice for the IP Iteration? ⬜ Dedicate time for I&A event and PI planning event
⬜ Ensure all Stories and Team’s PI plans are completed before the IP Iteration
⬜ Spend time on innovation, exploration, and tech debt in IP Iteration
⬜ Plan work for the IP Iteration during PI Planning and wait for the IP Iteration to fix defects
Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration provides dedicated time for which events? (Choose two.) ⬜ PI Planning
⬜ Iteration Review
⬜ Inspect and Adapt
⬜ ART Sync
What are the disadvantages of not planning a dedicated Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration for every PI? ⬜ Technical debt grows uncontrollably
⬜ People burn out
⬜ No time for teams to plan, demo, or improve together
⬜ All of the above
*What is one risk of eliminating an Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration? ⬜ Teams have no time for fixing bugs
⬜ Delivery can be blocked
⬜ Technical debt can grow uncontrollably
⬜ Bottlenecks can be hard to identify and resolve
Which role should the Release Train Engineer play related to a hackathon event? ⬜ Ensure the teams have allocated story points in the Innovation and Planning Iteration during the Program Increment to account for the effort
⬜ Get approval for work to be done in the hackathon
⬜ Work with development leaders to make sure they give clear and detailed guidance to the developers on what is expected
⬜ Allow the teams as much flexibility as possible to promote innovation
What is one benefit hackathons provide during the Innovation and Planning (IP) Iteration? ⬜ They help drive innovations that help the business
⬜ They create a heads-down approach to deliver near-term value
⬜ They focus the Team on what is urgent
⬜ They foster Pairing and Peer Review practices to build T-shaped skills
*What can a Release Train Engineer (RTE) use to support Relentless Improvement for the PI? ⬜ Release management meeting
⬜ PO Sync
⬜ Iteration Retrospective
⬜ Inspect & Adapt (I&A) event
PI System Demo and Retrospective is part of the Inspect and Adapt (I&A) event, what else? (select two) ⬜ Iteration Review
⬜ PI Planning
⬜ Quantitative and qualitative measurement
⬜ Problem-solving workshop
*Which statement is true about the retrospective and problem-solving part of the Inspect & Adapt (I&A) workshop? ⬜ The improvement backlog items resulting from the problem-solving workshop should be items that only leadership can address
⬜ Encourage teams to sit together during the retrospective portion to ensure an effective outcome
⬜ Key ART stakeholders, including Business Owners, Customers, and management can participate along with the teams
⬜ The Release Train Engineer (RTE) gathers the list of problems to be solved during the final Coach Sync of the PI
During which part of an Inspect & Adapt (I&A) event are differences between planned business value and actual business value presented? ⬜ Problem-solving workshop
⬜ Retrospective
⬜ Quantitative and qualitative measurement
⬜ PI System Demo
During Inspect and Adapt, teams identified a large number of action items aimed at solving their biggest problem as a train. How should the team proceed? ⬜ Prioritize and address the most critical issues first
⬜ Ignore the action items and focus on regular tasks
⬜ Delegate all action items to a dedicated team
⬜ Disregard the identified problems and continue as usual
What is one anti-pattern of the Inspect and Adapt? ⬜ Too many ideas enter the problem-solving workshop
⬜ Not enough Team members attend the PI System Demo
⬜ Only one problem is identified by each Team in the retrospective
⬜ No actionable improvement Features are created
What is the first step of the problem-solving workshop in the Inspect and Adapt event? ⬜ Restate the new problem for the biggest root cause
⬜ Identify the biggest root cause
⬜ Perform a root-cause analysis
⬜ Agree on the problem(s) to solve
*What is the next step after identifying the root cause during the problem-solving workshop? ⬜ Restate the problem
⬜ Brainstorm solutions
⬜ Identify improvement backlog items
⬜ Trace the chain of causality
According to SAFe, which of the following metrics are reported at the Inspect and Adapt event? ⬜ ART cycle velocity
⬜ ART predictability measure
⬜ Cumulative value measure
⬜ Cumulative value rate
What is the outcome of the problem-solving workshop in the Inspect and Adapt event? ⬜ Improvement Backlog Items
⬜ Team Backlog
⬜ PI Objectives
⬜ Enabler Stories
Why is the problem-solving workshop more effective than traditional lessons learned documents? ⬜ Collaboration over documentation is a key recommendation of the Agile Manifesto
⬜ It makes improvements actionable through backlog items for the next PI
⬜ It involves a small group of leaders
⬜ Workshops are more engaging than document writing
What is a key responsibility of the Release Train Engineer (RTE) during the Inspect and Adapt (I&A) event? ⬜ Presenting the program increment deliverables to stakeholders
⬜ Assigning new user stories to the development teams
⬜ Conducting individual performance evaluations of team members
⬜ Facilitating the retrospective and identifying improvement actions
During the Inspect and Adapt event, what is the RTE responsible for? ⬜ Assigning new features to teams
⬜ Evaluating individual team member performance
⬜ Facilitating the retrospective and problem-solving workshop
⬜ Developing the next PI roadmap
At what time is the Inspect and Adapt (I&A) Event conducted? ⬜ After the System Demo
⬜ At the end of every Iteration
⬜ At the end of the PI
⬜ During the PI
What are two reasons the 5 Whys technique is effective in performing root cause analysis in the Inspect and Adapt (I&A) event? (Choose two.) ⬜ It allows for assumptions and logic traps
⬜ It is an effective way for the team to collaborate
⬜ It allows problems of a similar nature to be combined into groups
⬜ It reveals the nature of the problem by repeating “why” five times
⬜ It explores the cause-and-effect relationship underlying a particular problem
When the 5 Whys technique is used? ⬜ To identify the root cause of the problem
⬜ To define the acceptance criteria of a Story
⬜ To brainstorm on the customer journey
⬜ To define the requirements of MVP
*What is the best way for the Release Train Engineer (RTE) to show progress of work in the current PI to management? ⬜ Conduct a System Demo
⬜ Generate a velocity trend report
⬜ Conduct a retrospective
⬜ Arrange for a separate meeting with Business Owners
What is the best measure of progress for complex system development? ⬜ Inspect and Adapt
⬜ System Demo
⬜ Prioritized backlog
⬜ Iteration Review
What is one purpose of the System Demo? ⬜ To demonstrate a team’s build
⬜ To flow, dependencies, and risks
⬜ To plan the Inspect & Adapt (I&A) event
⬜ To demonstrate the full Solution in a production-like context
What is the main reason for the System Demo? ⬜ To provide an optional quality check
⬜ To enable faster feedback by integration across teams
⬜ To fulfill SAFe PI Planning requirement
⬜ To allow the product owner to provide feedback on team increment
What is one anti-pattern related to System Demos? ⬜ People from outside the Agile Release Train attend the System Demo
⬜ Team demos are accepted in place of a System Demo to avoid redundancy
⬜ System demo takes more than 15 minutes
⬜ Different team members conduct the demo each Iteration
How often should System Demos occur in the default SAFe cadence? ⬜ Every 4 weeks
⬜ When requested
⬜ Weekly
⬜ Every Iteration
Who are important attendees to the PI System Demo? ⬜ Feature Owners
⬜ Board Members
⬜ Portfolio Management
⬜ Business Owners
Which of the following Agile Manifesto Principles aligns with conducting a System Demo? ⬜ Working Software is the primary measure of progress
⬜ Welcome changing requirements, even late in development
⬜ The best way to convey information is a face-to-face conversation
⬜ The Team reflects on how to become more effective at regular intervals
*The teams on the ART just finished the second Iteration in the PI and have nothing to demonstrate at the System Demo. What steps should be taken next? ⬜ Re-architect the system so that there are no dependencies between the teams, and integration is not needed
⬜ Stop working on any new functionality and fully integrate and test the system; adjust scope based on learnings
⬜ Require every team demonstrate their team increment to the stakeholders separately in the team branch
⬜ Continue to work on new functionality and reserve time to fully integrate the system during the IP Iteration
*Which action describes the behavior of applying Systems Thinking for a Release Train Engineer (RTE)? ⬜ Demonstrates appreciation to team members in many ways
⬜ Facilitates individual decision-making over team-level decision-making
⬜ Examines what may be missing to make the environment better for the team
⬜ Encourages the team to express opinions in all circumstances
*Which action describes the behavior of applying Systems Thinking for a Release Train Engineer (RTE)? ⬜ Focuses the teams on meeting individual deadlines and commitments, ensuring each team stays on track
⬜ Analyzes the flow of value through the Agile Release Train (ART) and looks for systemic bottlenecks or dependencies to progress
⬜ Implements strict adherence to process and documentation standards, ensuring all teams follow the defined procedure of context
⬜ Tracks individual team performance metrics to foster healthy competition among teams
*What is one way to use the results from Value Stream mapping? ⬜ Identify methods for developers to code faster
⬜ Calculate the metrics and share them with the ART
⬜ Move from bottleneck to bottleneck, eliminating as many as possible
⬜ Focus on one component to optimize
*What is one tool used to identify bottlenecks? ⬜ Kanban Board
⬜ Ishikawa Diagram
⬜ Value Stream Mapping
⬜ Objectives and Key Results (OKRs)
In what way is a value stream map different from a process flow? ⬜ A value stream map uncovers local problems in functional organizations
⬜ A value stream map measures the flow of value and identifies bottlenecks for improvement
⬜ A value stream map is used to define Solution Context
⬜ A value stream map can be operational or developmental; process flows are only operational
What practice can help to identify bottlenecks in the flow of work? ⬜ Visualizing the flow of all work and track progress of individual items
⬜ Comparing transaction costs, holding costs and business value realization
⬜ Measuring lead time for all work in progress
⬜ Modeling overall process flow during value stream identification
What makes it important to periodically adjust Value Stream budgets? ⬜ To ensure minimal variance in project budgets
⬜ To generate cost savings
⬜ To take advantage of emerging opportunities
⬜ To maximize the return on Epic investment
Domain 7: Coaching the ART (12-14%) *A group of developers, Scrum Master/Team Coaches (SM/TCs), and Product Owners (POs) are interested in sharing knowledge and learning more about DevOps concepts. How can the Release Train Engineer (RTE) help them collaborate to gain knowledge about DevOps? ⬜ Schedule a DevOps bi-weekly synchronization
⬜ Provide DevOps training
⬜ Help them launch a DevOps Community of Practice (CoP)
⬜ Align them with the System Team
Teams report high success through their individual quantitative measurements, but the system results do not support the teams’ reports. What should the Release Train Engineer (RTE) do to help the teams deliver more value? ⬜ Share the quantitative measurement results with Product Management and Leadership and ask for their input
⬜ Diagnose the differences between the measurements and the results and suggest improvement items to each Team
⬜ Coach the Scrum Master/Team Coach (SM/TC) on good Retrospective techniques and ensure Teams are defining and taking a systems view approach to improvements
⬜ Work with the Team that is struggling the most to discover patterns that can be applied to the other Teams
*Several Scrum Masters/Team Coaches (SM/TCs) disagree on what to do about a shared issue. What is an appropriate coaching technique for the Release Train Engineer (RTE)? ⬜ Being the final decision maker once all feedback has been heard
⬜ Performing an empirical assessment of the problem using metrics
⬜ Bringing new emphasis to Lean-Agile’s Respect for People
⬜ Asking powerful questions to invite creativity and new possibilities
According to Patrick Lencioni’s “Five Dysfunctions of a Team”, what is a team’s ultimate competitive advantage? ⬜ Respect
⬜ Commitment
⬜ Transparency
⬜ Teamwork
According to Patrick Lencioni’s “Five Dysfunctions of a Team”, which issue most often leads to Team Dysfunctions? ⬜ Absence of Trust
⬜ Fear of Conflict
⬜ Lack of Commitment
⬜ Avoidance of Accountability
How does SAFe handle the ‘fear of conflict’ team dysfunction? ⬜ Reviews results at the end of every iteration
⬜ Avoids discussion of disagreements
⬜ Has teams engage in retrospectives
⬜ Uses Scrum to create a safe environment for conflict
Which practice helps the RTE promote accountability within the ART? ⬜ Avoiding discussions on missed commitments
⬜ Handling all issues without team involvement
⬜ Encouraging teams to self-assess and address performance gaps
⬜ Ignoring performance metrics
How can the RTE encourage healthy conflict within the ART? ⬜ Discouraging debates to maintain harmony
⬜ Avoiding discussions on contentious topics
⬜ Creating a safe environment for open dialogue
⬜ Resolving all conflicts personally
Why are powerful questions important in Agile team coaching? ⬜ They ensure the Scrum Master gives the right answers
⬜ They reduce the time spent in meetings
⬜ They are though-provoking and generate curiosity in the listener
⬜ To accelerate decision-making without discussion
Which of the following is an example of a powerful question a Scrum Master might ask to foster team insight? ⬜ Did everyone complete their tasks?
⬜ Why didn’t you finish this story?
⬜ What is it we’re not seeing?
⬜ Who caused the delay?
*What is one technique for building a one-team culture across the ART? ⬜ Rotate team members to new teams to facilitate relationship building
⬜ Foster an environment in which the whole ART succeeds and fails together
⬜ Review each teams’ predictability measure with the ART
⬜ Ensure the team leader does not show vulnerability
What is a key characteristic of a “one-team culture” within an Agile Release Train (ART)? ⬜ Each team operates independently with minimal interaction
⬜ Teams prioritize their own goals over ART objectives
⬜ Teams collaborate across boundaries to achieve shared ART goals
⬜ Communication is limited to formal meetings only
What is a key characteristic of a high-performing ART that embodies a one-team culture? ⬜ Teams working independently without coordination
⬜ Centralized decision-making by leadership
⬜ Shared goals and mutual accountability among teams
⬜ Strict adherence to individual team processes
What is a key behavior of the Release Train Engineer (RTE) that supports a one-team culture? ⬜ Assigning tasks to individual team members
⬜ Enforcing strict adherence to processes
⬜ Encouraging teams to self-organize and collaborate
⬜ Making all decisions unilaterally
At which stage will the Agile Release Train (ART) act as a one-team culture? ⬜ Forming – Teams are introduced and start to understand their roles
⬜ Storming – Teams begin to address conflicts and challenges
⬜ Norming – Teams establish norms and start to work together
⬜ Performing – Creating a flow of knowledge across the teams and the ART
During the storming stage of ART development and evolution, in which area should a Release Train Engineer (RTE) mentor Scrum Masters/Team Coaches (SM/TCs)? ⬜ Conflict resolution techniques
⬜ Establishing ART events
⬜ Creating effective flow across teams
⬜ Engineering practice improvements
*Why is it important for the Release Train Engineer (RTE) to understand Tuckman’s group dynamic stages? ⬜ Tuckman helps RTEs to better understand Team and ART topologies
⬜ An ART is a team of teams and will likely progress through the Tuckman stages
⬜ The Tuckman dynamic nature of the stages requires that we assume variability and preserve options
⬜ The Tuckman four stages should be reflected in the design of the ART Kanban
What role does the RTE play during the Forming stage of an ART? ⬜ Resolving conflicts among team members
⬜ Guiding the ART through establishing vision, mission, and objectives
⬜ Facilitating performance reviews
⬜ Implementing new technologies
At which Tuckman stage would an ART be if it is improving engineering practices and fostering more effective communication? ⬜ Forming
⬜ Storming
⬜ Norming
⬜ Performing
What are two purposes of a community of practice? (Choose two.) ⬜ To approve standards
⬜ To align tasks across teams
⬜ To refine definitions of done
⬜ To share knowledge and skills
⬜ To network
What is one goal or purpose of a Community of Practice? ⬜ To refine the Definition of Done (DoD)
⬜ To align tasks across Teams
⬜ To approve standards
⬜ To share knowledge and skills
How can a Release Train Engineer (RTE) promote a tribal culture within the ART? ⬜ By assigning tasks to teams without their input
⬜ By limiting communication between teams to reduce complexity
⬜ By facilitating events that encourage cross-team collaboration and shared learning
⬜ By focusing solely on meeting individual team metrics
Domain 8: Applying AI to the RTE Role (14-16%) *Which technology are Generative AI systems primarily built on, according to SAFe’s guidance? ⬜ A comprehensive set of static, rule-based logic
⬜ Deep Learning and neural networks
⬜ Traditional Machine Learning trained only on labeled tabular data
⬜ Manually coded decision trees maintained by a Center of Excellence
What is the primary purpose of the SAFe CoPilot AI assistant for a Release Train Engineer? ⬜ To automatically approve ART PI Objectives without RTE review
⬜ To quickly reference Framework guidance and support data-backed recommendations for value stream optimization
⬜ To replace the Scrum of Scrums meeting with an automated status report
⬜ To serve as the official system of record for ART PI Risks
Which approach reflects a foundational prompting technique SAFe recommends when using generative AI tools to support a SAFe role? ⬜ Ask a single vague question and accept the first response without refinement
⬜ Assign the AI a specific role or persona and provide clear context and constraints
⬜ Avoid providing any context so the AI can respond without bias
⬜ Submit the same prompt to multiple AI tools and average the results
*According to SAFe’s Responsible AI model, which three aspects must an AI system exhibit to be considered responsible? ⬜ Trustworthy, Explainable, and Human-centric
⬜ Fast, Scalable, and Cost-effective
⬜ Proprietary, Centralized, and Auditable
⬜ Agile, Lean, and Systemic
A company’s AI-based facial recognition system consistently fails to accurately identify individuals with darker skin tones because its training data contained mostly lighter-skinned faces. Which AI risk does this scenario illustrate? ⬜ Hallucination
⬜ Bias
⬜ Data leak
⬜ Model drift
An airline’s AI chatbot tells a customer about a discount that doesn’t actually exist. When the customer tries to redeem it, the airline is held legally responsible. Which AI risk does this scenario best illustrate? ⬜ Data leak
⬜ Bias
⬜ Hallucination
⬜ An explainability failure
Developers at a company used a public generative AI tool to help debug their code and unintentionally exposed sensitive proprietary source code to the outside world. Which attribute of Trustworthy AI was most directly compromised? ⬜ Accuracy
⬜ Resilience
⬜ Privacy
⬜ Reliability
*Which of the following is one of the four critical shifts described in SAFe’s guidance for achieving AI-Empowered Agility? ⬜ Replacing cross-functional teams with specialized, AI-only pods
⬜ Focus on Outcomes and Intent
⬜ Eliminating iterative, incremental delivery in favor of single continuous releases
⬜ Centralizing all AI decision-making exclusively at the Portfolio level
Why is “Human-in-the-Loop” (HITL) engagement important for an RTE coaching an ART that has adopted AI agents into its workflow? ⬜ It ensures AI agents never require oversight after initial setup
⬜ It keeps human judgment as the final, non-negotiable checkpoint for value, safety, and purpose, so AI’s speed doesn’t compromise accountability or quality
⬜ It allows the RTE to delegate all PI Planning facilitation duties to an AI agent
⬜ It eliminates the need for Responsible AI governance once teams are AI-augmented
As AI becomes embedded in ART workflows, SAFe states that critical coaching roles such as the RTE must become experts in which three areas to support effective human-AI collaboration? ⬜ Effective management of AI agents, advanced prompting techniques, and responsible AI practices
⬜ Portfolio budgeting, capacity allocation, and vendor contract negotiation
⬜ Test-driven development, pair programming, and code refactoring
⬜ Enterprise architecture governance, NFR definition, and solution intent management
How can an RTE responsibly use AI while preparing for PI Planning? ⬜ Let AI auto-generate the final team commitments without team input
⬜ Use AI to help synthesize draft dependencies and risks across teams for the RTE to review
⬜ Skip the ART Sync because AI already has full visibility into all teams
⬜ Replace the Scrum of Scrums with an AI-generated status report
According to Scaled Agile’s Responsible AI guidance, what are the three pillars of Responsible AI? ⬜ Fast, Cheap, and Automated AI
⬜ Trustworthy AI, Explainable AI, and Human-Centric AI
⬜ Predictive AI, Generative AI, and Agentic AI
⬜ Scalable AI, Secure AI, and Proprietary AI
An RTE shares confidential ART roadmap details with a public, third-party AI tool to get a quick summary. Which Responsible AI risk does this illustrate? ⬜ Hallucination
⬜ Bias
⬜ A data leak
⬜ Explainability
An AI assistant confidently reports a dependency between two Features that doesn’t actually exist. What is this risk called? ⬜ Bias
⬜ Hallucination
⬜ A data leak
⬜ Model drift
